Information framing and the impact of nutrition label serving size change
abstract: Abstract The framing of information can significantly influence how consumers interpret and respond to it. This paper investigates how the change in serving sizes in Nutrition Facts Panel (NFP) affects consumer choices for carbonated soft drinks (CSD). We first estimate a reduced form difference‐in‐differences (DiD) model to document causal effects on purchasing behavior. We then develop and estimate an equilibrium structural model of both consumer demand and firms' pricing and nutritional choices. Our results show that larger labeled serving sizes significantly reduced demand for regular CSDs, leading to a decline in the average amount of nutrients sold. Counterfactual simulations indicate that larger serving size adjustments (e.g., 16 oz, 24 oz, or whole bottle) would amplify these effects, while firms would partially offset demand losses through subtle calorie, sodium, and caffeine reductions. These findings suggest that strategic serving size adjustments and product reformulations from food manufacturers may support healthier consumer choices. Our welfare analysis shows that sufficiently aggressive serving size adjustments can dominate soda tax at low to moderate values of the marginal value of public funds, delivering comparable reductions in nutrient purchases without the regressive price burden that excise taxes impose on lower‐income consumers.

title: Asymmetric trading costs and ancient Greek cities
Striking the right balance: How sanctions and consequences of customer misbehavior shape hotel guests’ fairness perceptions and rebooking intentions
Professional identity as the missing link: Understanding motivational pathways among hotel employees
Serendipity and innovation in new ventures: The moderating role of primary investor type
Response to ‘Optimal tourism taxation with externalities: A rejoinder to Rosselló-Nadal and Sard (2026)’
Institutional Ownership and Corporate Exposure to Equal Employment Opportunity Lawsuits
abstract: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue This study investigates whether and how institutional ownership is associated with firms' exposure to equal employment opportunity (EEO) lawsuits under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. These lawsuits capture an underexplored form of downside ESG risk arising from firms' treatment of employees, who constitute a key corporate stakeholder group. Research Findings/Insights Using a dataset of 22,501 EEO lawsuits filed in US federal courts from 2001 to 2020, this study finds that firms with higher institutional blockholdings experience significantly fewer EEO lawsuits. This relationship persists across active, passive, long‐term, and transient investors and remains robust to an instrumental variable analysis exploiting Russell 3000 Index inclusion, change analyses, industry adjustments, and numerous robustness tests. Post‐lawsuit responses reveal three mechanisms: The largest investors withdraw capital (exit); transient investors increase voting engagement (voice); and forced CEO turnover increases, particularly in high‐blockholding firms (discipline). Institutional investors' role is amplified in low‐skilled labor environments and complemented by independent board monitoring. Theoretical/Academic Implications This study documents the role of institutional investors in mitigating the risk of workplace discrimination litigation, advancing the literature on institutional monitoring, ESG, employee welfare, and corporate governance. EEO lawsuits provide an objective, non‐self‐reported measure of a specific downside ESG risk. This study further shows how heterogeneous investors deploy different mechanisms to improve EEO outcomes. Practitioner/Policy Implications Workplace discrimination poses a threat to employee well‐being and firm reputation. Uncovering institutional investors' role in safeguarding employees' civil right to EEO provides useful insights for policymakers, boards, and investors.

title: One size does not fit all: management strategies to reduce turnover intention among public sector employees
Childhood abuse profiles and psychological distress in emerging adulthood: Gender differences across housing cost burden contexts
How childhood sexual abuse disclosure response practices shape survivors' psychological wellbeing
Why Do Spanish University Students Flirt in Nightlife Venues?
Using Artificial Intelligence to Access Reproductive Healthcare Information by U.S. States Following Sexual Assault
“There’s No Magic Pill to Help Me, Right?”: Sex After Early Midlife Bilateral Salpingo-Oophorectomy
abstract: Abstract Women with risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (RRBSO) report poorer sexual health than women of a similar age with intact ovaries. Since women with RRBSO lose the ability to make endogenous 17-β-estradiol (E2), open questions include whether: (1) poorer sexual function is associated with E2 loss and (2) exogenous estradiol therapy (ET BSO ) is related to amelioration of objective decrements and subjective experiences. We combined online questionnaires with qualitative interviews to explore the sexual function of women with pathogenic variants in the BRCA1/2 genes and RRBSO not taking ET BSO (RRBSO) and those taking ET BSO (RRBSO + ET BSO ). We compared their quantitative responses to those of age-matched women with intact ovaries (AMC) and women in spontaneous menopause (SM). RRBSO had lower total sexual function scores than AMC and more sexually related distress than AMC than SM. In terms of lived experience with RRBSO + /–ET BSO , qualitative interviews mirrored the quantitative data with reports of pain, loss of sexual desire, and dryness, in addition to concerns about identity, relational challenges, and lacking crucial information regarding sexual response after RRBSO. The combination of the objective and subjective reports details worse sexual function and experience of younger women with RRBSO regardless of ET BSO . Since ET BSO does not appear to ameliorate all aspects of sexual function and distress for many women with RRBSO, it is critical to consider other interventions including fully informed consent prior to RRBSO.

title: A physics-informed deep clustering framework with single-cell voltage features for early fault identification in automotive PEM fuel cell
Co-optimizing revenue generation and lifetime degradation of lithium-ion batteries in energy markets using physics-based modeling
Mixed lignocellulosic biomass for continuous bioethanol production: logistics, process integration and biodesign
Just by design, not by default: Why social indicators are essential for a circular economy
Medium-Entropy LDH-Driven Electronic Coupling of MnO x for Preferential Oxidation of Formaldehyde
abstract: Abstract Preferential oxidation of formaldehyde (HCHO) in natural gas engine exhaust is pivotal to prevent NH3–SCR catalyst deactivation and inhibit highly toxic hydrogen cyanide (HCN) formation. Although manganese-based catalysts exhibit prominent activity for HCHO oxidation, complete mineralization is still hindered by poor electron-transfer efficiency and insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Herein, we fabricate hierarchical medium-entropy LDH nanoflower-anchored MnOx catalysts (MnO2@NiMgAl-MELH) via a facile in situ growth strategy, enabling 100% mineralization of HCHO at room temperature. Structural characterizations and DFT calculations verify that Ni–Mn electronic coupling optimizes the electronic structure, facilitates charge transfer, reduces oxygen vacancy formation energy, and boosts O2 and H2O activation to generate abundant ROS (O2–, O22–, and surface −OH). Furthermore, in situ DRIFTS confirms that ROS synergistically accelerate HCHO and formate intermediate oxidation, achieving complete mineralization of HCHO. This work develops a low-cost and high-performance catalyst for HCHO preferential oxidation and offers a broadly applicable strategy for air pollutant purification.

title: PFAS in Follicular Fluid, Anti-Mullerian Hormone, and Oocyte Developmental Competence: A Prospective Study in GIVES
abstract: Abstract In this prospective study based on the Guangxi In Vitro Fertilization and the Environment Study (GIVES) cohort, we measured poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the ovarian follicular fluid of 729 participants to investigate their association with oocyte developmental competence. The PFAS mixture was negatively associated with Metaphase II (MII) oocyte rate, with chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonic acids (Cl-PFESAs) identified as the primary contributor in Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) models. Cl-PFESAs were negatively associated with oocyte maturation [relative risk (RR) = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.56–0.79], fertilization (RR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.67–0.90), blastocyst formation (RR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.70–0.94), and high-quality blastocyst formation (RR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.41–0.58). Serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) may act as a key modifier, with a stronger association observed in women with low AMH for MII oocyte rate [relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.12–0.54] and fertilization rate (RERI = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.003–0.49). Our findings indicate that PFAS, particularly Cl-PFESAs, in follicular fluid are linked to impaired oocyte developmental competence, with AMH serving as a potential modifier. Further studies are warranted to validate our findings and assess the implications of PFAS for reproductive outcomes.

title: From passive carriers to selective filters: how microplastic aging shapes antibiotic resistance gene abundance
Should you ask directly? What rice farmers reveal in list experiments regarding improper disposal of agricultural waste
Advancing nutrient circularity in agriculture: Critical perspectives on recycling-derived bio-based fertilisers, production, and adoption challenges
abstract: Recycling-derived bio-based fertilisers (RD-BBFs) are an emerging sustainable solution for nutrient management in agriculture, addressing the pressing need to reduce reliance on mineral fertilisers sourced from finite resources. This paper reviews journal articles and EU legislative documents, primarily focusing on RD-BBFs, which involve sources such as animal manure, agri-food industry waste, urban green waste, and food waste. They are produced through various processes, including composting, anaerobic digestion, stripping, scrubbing and precipitation, among others. The Fertilising Products Regulations 2019/1009 create a market for RD-BBFs in the EU, encouraging their use among farmers; however, the legislation has not covered all the RD-BBFs. Additionally, this study provides an overview of RD-BBF pathways through material flow analysis (MFA) and life cycle assessment (LCA), as analytical tools that help assess the environmental and economic benefits of RD-BBFs. Most analytical studies are limited to a few nutrients and RD-BBFs; further comprehensive studies are needed to consider other nutrients and RD-BBFs. Considering their mineral fertiliser equivalent value (MFEV), this study demonstrates how RD-BBFs could help to close the nutrient loop and enhance agricultural sustainability. Further studies are needed to investigate the long-term effects of RD-BBFs in various geographical regions across Europe. Furthermore, this review identifies hurdles to RD-BBF adoption, including variability in nutrient content, plant available MFEV, economic considerations, and societal acceptance. Strategies for overcoming these constraints are presented. Overall, RD-BBF is a viable option for reducing dependency on fossil-based fertilisers. This study highlights the potential for RD-BBFs to promote sustainable agriculture while enhancing resource efficiency and promoting environmental preservation.

title: Mealworm frass affects the chemical properties and nutrient dynamics in two lupin varieties under contrasting soils
Enzymatic PET depolymerization: a review of engineering biocatalysts and systems for efficient plastic deconstruction
abstract: The ever-increasing accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste poses a severe threat to global ecosystems and human health. Biological upcycling (integrating enzymatic depolymerization with microbial conversion of the resulting monomers) has emerged as a promising approach to overcome the limitations of traditional mechanical and chemical recycling. This review provides a systematic and critical synthesis of recent advances in PET bio-upcycling, covering the period from 2016 to 2026. We first discuss the discovery, classification, structural features, and catalytic mechanisms of PET-hydrolyzing enzymes, highlighting the rate-limiting constraints imposed by glass transition temperature, substrate crystallinity, interfacial interactions, and product inhibition. We then evaluate protein engineering strategies that have dramatically enhanced thermostability, substrate binding, and multi-enzyme synergy, yielding benchmark variants capable of near-complete depolymerization of post-consumer PET within hours to days. Concurrent innovations in whole-cell biocatalysis, enzyme immobilization, surface display, and microbial consortia are examined, with emphasis on how metabolic division of labor and substrate channeling can alleviate product inhibition and process mixed plastic waste. We also summarize metabolic engineering efforts that have enabled conversion of PET-derived terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG) into more than 25 value-added products, including biopolymers, platform chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and specialty compounds. Finally, we discuss remaining technological barriers, economic feasibility, and future frontiers (including computational enzyme design, synthetic consortia, tandem chemo-biological processes, and industrial-scale demonstration) and propose a phased roadmap for industrial translation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive resource for advancing PET bio-upcycling from laboratory innovation toward practical implementation in a circular plastics economy.

title: Electrospun Co3O4/CeO2 hollow nanotubes for photocatalytic degradation of PET plastics with peroxymonosulfate activation: Performance and DFT insight
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics cause significant environmental harm. Traditional treatment methods, such as landfilling and incineration, can cause secondary pollution. Here, an efficient synergistic photocatalytic system is presented, based on Co 3 O 4 /CeO 2 hollow nanotubes prepared by electrospinning, to activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and promote the degradation of PET plastics. The results show that the as-prepared Co 3 O 4 /CeO 2 composite catalyst exhibits the best performance under illumination; the weight loss rate of PET can reach ∼82.7 ± 4.5% in the presence of a 3 mM PMS solution (pH 7). The effects of parameters (e.g., PMS dose and coexisting anions) on PET degradation were systematically investigated. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and free radical quenching experiments confirm that the •OH, 1 O 2, and SO 4 •− active species contribute the most to the degradation of PET plastics. Density Functional Theory analysis shows that Co-d-pDOS and Ce-f-pDOS modulations in Co 3 O 4 /CeO 2 synergistically enhance the PET photocatalytic decomposition efficiency. Finally, we discuss the mechanism by which the catalyst/light/PMS system degrades PET in water.

title: Flow regulation capacity determines reservoir phytoplankton community assembly: threshold, mechanisms, and implications
abstract: Dam construction changes lotic rivers to lentic reservoirs with divergent hydraulic residence time (HRT), altering phytoplankton communities. However, how community assembly shifts along HRT gradients and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated phytoplankton communities from 21 reservoirs spanning a broad HRT range (0.21–94.65 d) in China, quantifying assembly patterns and disentangling the roles of the regional species pool and local habitat in shaping community assembly. The modified stochasticity ratio (MST) declined non-linearly with increasing HRT and a breakpoint at 10 d was identified. Reservoirs with HRT < 10 d had MST > 0.5, whereas those with HRT > 10 d showed an MST < 0.5, indicating a shift from stochastic- to deterministic-dominated assembly across this threshold. For reservoirs with HRT < 10 d, observed β–γ relationships matched null expectations, consistent with a stronger influence of the regional species pool; stochastic processes were dominated by drift and dispersal. Among reservoirs > 10 d HRT, observed β–γ relationships deviated from null expectations, indicating stronger local habitat filtering. Nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus) explained ∼33% of habitat effects, while water temperature explained ∼13%. Deterministic assembly was characterized by strong species sorting and niche partitioning. By linking HRT to phytoplankton assembly timescales, our findings identified an operationally relevant 10-day HRT threshold, highlighting that strategic manipulation of HRT can steer phytoplankton assembly and support ecosystem resilience in dammed rivers.

title: Integrating MaxEnt and explainable AI to assess habitat suitability and conservation gaps of Przewalski's gazelle (Procapra przewalskii) in the Qinghai Lake region
abstract: Habitat suitability assessment and conservation gap identification are critical for endangered species conservation. Using Przewalski's gazelle ( Procapra przewalskii ), an endangered ungulate endemic to China, we assessed habitat suitability, key environmental predictors, and conservation gaps in the Qinghai Lake region. Based on 1597 field occurrence records collected from 2020 to 2025, we integrated the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Partial Dependence Plots (PDPs), and GAP analysis. The selected MaxEnt model showed high discriminatory ability within the surveyed region (mean test AUC = 0.972 ± 0.003). The Human Influence Index (HII), mean temperature and precipitation of the driest quarter, elevation, and vegetation type were key predictors associated with habitat suitability, while mean diurnal range and HII had the highest mean SHAP importance. Suitable habitats were concentrated around Qinghai Lake and in the northern Gonghe Basin. The Qinghai Lake Basin represented the current core distribution area, whereas the Gonghe Basin contained extensive currently predicted suitable habitat and may represent an important conservation opportunity. GAP analysis showed that 71.83% of suitable habitat and 52.34% of the current distribution range lay outside the protected-area boundaries assessed in this study. Fence occurrence in the Hubei population area was significantly associated with relatively high predicted habitat suitability and showed marked spatial clustering. These findings provide spatially explicit evidence for protected-area optimization and habitat management of Przewalski's gazelle.

title: Biochar granulation and particle size influence hydrological performance of green roof substrates
abstract: Green roofs are increasingly implemented in cities to improve stormwater management and provide additional ecosystem services. Biochar, a carbon-rich material derived from pyrolyzed biomass, has emerged as a promising substrate additive to improve hydrological performance of green roofs. Biochar granulation and particle size modification have been suggested as effective approaches to mitigate erosion losses but research on the effects of biochar post-processing on hydrological performance remains scarce, and data on fundamental hydraulic properties of biochar-amended green roof substrates is entirely lacking. We investigated how biochar granulation and particle size influence surface and pore characteristics and hydraulic properties of green roof substrates in laboratory experiments. Granulated biochars exhibited collapsed surface morphology and pore structure, resulting in consistent hydrological responses across particle size ranges, likely due to the homogeneous structure formed during granulation. In contrast, unprocessed biochars showed a significant increase in Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area and pore volume with decreasing particle size. The amendment of granulated biochars improved substrate field capacity, suggesting potential enhancement of stormwater retention. The addition of fine (0.5–1 mm) and intermediate-sized (2–2.8 mm) unprocessed biochars also increased plant available water. Although reduced saturated hydraulic conductivity associated with fine unprocessed biochars may improve green roof detention capacity, fine biochar particle size may increase erosion losses and periodic waterlogging. We conclude that the application of either granulated biochar or intermediate-sized unprocessed biochar may provide a balanced enhancement of stormwater retention and detention capacities, as well as improved plant available water in green roof systems.

title: Potentials and drivers of soil quality improvement – an index based on-farm evaluation
Remobilization risk of Cd in aged pig manure biochar under rice rhizosphere influence: Evidence from six-season cultivation
abstract: Biochar is widely used to immobilize cadmium (Cd) in contaminated paddy soils; however, the long-term stability of biochar-adsorbed Cd under rice rhizosphere influence remains poorly understood, raising concerns about its potential secondary release. Herein, we investigated the remobilization behavior and speciation evolution of Cd from Cd-loaded pig manure biochar (Cd-PMB) using a six-season rice pot experiment, combined with a sequential simulated aging procedure designed to decouple the contributions of soil solution chemistry, root exudates, and oxidative processes. Two rice cultivars with contrasting Cd accumulation capacities were employed. Total Cd in Cd-PMB decreased by 84.3%–89.2% after six seasons, with >50% of the loss occurring during the first season, driven predominantly by cation exchange and rhizosphere acidification. Speciation analysis revealed that the ion-exchangeable Cd fraction was almost completely released (>95%) irrespective of planting treatment, while physically adsorbed and hydrogen-bonded Cd were preferentially remobilized under rhizosphere influence. Notably, complexed Cd exhibited a dual-phase dynamic, which initially increased by 8.1%–19.3% through secondary complexation onto newly formed carboxyl sites and subsequently declined during prolonged aging as these sites underwent protonation and oxidative degradation, as confirmed by Fourier‐transform infrared and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses and further supported by significant Pearson correlations between COOH/ C O 3 2 − and Q com -Cd (r = 0.801, p < 0.05). The simulated aging experiments confirmed that soil solution, root exudates, and oxidative aging synergistically promote Cd release from distinct binding pools. Our findings demonstrate that biochar-adsorbed Cd undergoes substantial, binding form–dependent remobilization during aging, posing a secondary risk that necessitates explicit consideration in long-term safety assessments of biochar-amended soils.

title: A bioindicator-based approach for evaluating environmental dioxin-like POPs burden: Implications for contamination surveillance and exposure risk assessment
abstract: Recent global emission inventories, attributing significant releases of dioxin-like persistent organic pollutants (dl-POPs) to open burning activities, necessitate surveillance and emission control measures that invariably extend to non-point sources alongside conventionally weighed stationary point sources. The study presents an integrated field-based approach that employs foraging animal-origin food as bioindicators to systematically investigate and compare the environmental fingerprints and exposure risks of dl-POPs under such emission scenarios. The chosen study sites, viz. a legacy municipal solid waste (MSW) dumpsite and a biomedical waste incinerator (BMWI), along with a rare case of accidental fire incidents, represented classic real-world instances of transient/non-point and continuous/point sources. The observed substantially higher median dl-POPs levels in cow's milk and chicken eggs from the BMWI site (8.04 and 10.8 pgTEQ/g fat), relative to the MSW dumpsite (2.78 and 2.89 pgTEQ/g fat), highlighted continuous point sources as critical contributors to environmental burdens. Notably, dynamic trends of PCDD/Fs levels in milk and eggs over successive sampling phases suggested the contributive effect of fire breakouts to locally produced food contamination. Based on dietary exposure assessment, median dl-POPs weekly intake from the BMWI site and MSW dumpsite ranged up to 11.2 and 3.88 pgTEQ kg −1 bw week −1 , respectively, which are up to 5.6 and 1.9 times the EFSA-assigned tolerable weekly intake, indicating elevated health risk for consumers. The study upholds great relevance for data-deficient emerging economies to validate emission inventories, strengthen monitoring and source-specific emission control, and support regulatory frameworks in food commodities.

title: RSM and ANN-driven optimization of Reactive Blue 221 biosorption by inactive Aspergillus niger: Mass transfer mechanisms, pareto analysis, and a circular economy approach
abstract: Synthetic reactive dyes are persistent pollutants often found in textile wastewater due to their complex aromatic and sulfonated structures. This study evaluated inactive Aspergillus niger biomass as a biosorbent for removing Reactive Blue 221 (RB 221) from aqueous solutions. Batch experiments indicated that the Langmuir isotherm best described the equilibrium data, with a maximum monolayer capacity of 32.89 mg/g at 30 °C. Kinetic data fit well with the pseudo-second-order and Elovich models, pointing to physicochemical interactions on a heterogeneous surface. Kinetic evaluation via Weber-Morris and Boyd models indicated that the mass transfer rate was co-limited by both external film and intraparticle diffusion. Meanwhile, SEM, EDS, and FTIR analyses confirmed the localized physicochemical binding mechanisms, revealing post-biosorption morphological changes, dye-specific elemental signals, and the participation of protonated amines in binding sulfonate-rich RB 221. Thermodynamic parameters (ΔG° < 0 and ΔH° > 0) confirmed a spontaneous, endothermic process. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) with a Central Composite Design optimized the process, where conditions of pH 5.25, 7.95 g/L dosage, 30 °C, and 87.50 mg/L dye concentration yielded a maximum predicted removal efficiency of 89.17%, which was experimentally validated at 89.25%. Contribution analysis highlighted biosorbent dosage as the key operational parameter, accounting for ∼90% of the total process variance. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with a 4-20-10-1 topology yielded superior predictive accuracy compared to the quadratic RSM model (R 2 = 0.9941 vs. 0.968). Combined with a preliminary cost assessment and a proposed waste-to-energy disposal route, these findings demonstrate that inactive A. niger is a practical, low-cost, and sustainable biosorbent for textile wastewater treatment.

title: Managing urban park landscape patterns to balance plant diversity and biotic homogenization across life forms: A case study of Chaoyang District, Beijing
abstract: Biodiversity loss and the homogenization of plant communities are commonly observed in urbanized environments, highlighting the importance of maintaining plant diversity and compositional distinctness in urban green spaces. Urban parks are key refugia for plants, yet it remains unclear how their landscape patterns can be configured to simultaneously enhance species richness and reduce compositional homogenization across different plant life forms. Based on transect surveys of 820 plant species in 31 urban parks in Chaoyang District, Beijing, we combined multi-life-form analyses with a data-driven landscape framework to (i) identify the landscape metrics that best explain variation in plant richness and community composition, and (ii) quantify the trade-offs involved in reconciling their divergent requirements. We found consistently high levels of biotic homogenization across all plant types (all species, trees, shrubs, herbs and vines). Seventeen key landscape metrics were selected as important predictors of richness and composition, among which the interspersion and juxtaposition index provided particularly clear ecological interpretation. Higher morphological complexity of water bodies was associated with lower species richness, which may partly reflect shoreline hardening or reduced riparian habitat quality, whereas higher patch numbers of both green space and water generally promoted species richness and compositional distinctness. However, patch-number adjustments should not simply aim for maximization, but may instead follow a conceptual “peak-shaving and gap-filling” heuristic to balance additional patch creation with reduced redundancy in landscape configurations. For parks lacking water bodies, introducing water features may be considered where hydrologically and ecologically feasible, particularly when designed with naturalized shorelines to support plant richness and compositional distinctness. Our results provide a conceptual and data-driven framework for targeting landscape pattern adjustments in urban parks to promote plant diversity while alleviating biotic homogenization.

title: Particle size-dependent carbon source capture and carbon allocation pathways by activated sludge
Differences in Dust Emission and Near‐Surface Transport Patterns Among Three Surface Substrate Types
abstract: ABSTRACT Soil wind erosion is a major driver of atmospheric dust emissions and land degradation. Many studies have examined dust release from different substrates, but differences in methods and units still limit quantitative understanding of how surface conditions and wind jointly control dust emission and near‐surface transport. A closed‐circuit wind tunnel was used to compare dust emission and vertical transport from dune sand (sand, D 50 = 176 μm), farmland soil (sandy loam, D 50 = 86 μm), and dry lakebed sediments (sand, D 50 = 153 μm). At 14 m s −1 , farmlands transported 6.2–7.2 times more PM 2.5 and 7.1–8.3 times more PM 10 than the other two substrates ( p < 0.001), while dunes and lakebeds transported more total mass. In the emitted material, dunes contributed the lowest fine particle proportion (PM 63 < 6.6%), farmlands maintained high fine fractions (PM 63 up to 55.5%), and lakebeds produced fine‐rich emissions at low wind speed but shifted towards low fine fractions as speed increased. Vertically, fine‐particle proportions increased with height over farmland soil across all wind speeds. Under the strongest wind, dune sand and dry lakebed sediment showed declining transported‐mass profiles and no significant height trends in particle‐size proportions. These results show that the surfaces that dominate total mass are not the same as those that dominate health‐relevant PM. This unified comparative analysis, grounded in controlled wind‐tunnel observations, supports targeted mitigation through modest‐height windbreaks for fine‐dust control on farmland, surface‐roughness enhancement on dunes, and crust stabilization on dry lakebeds.

JACKKNIFE EMPIRICAL LIKELIHOOD FOR INFINITE-ORDER U -STATISTICS
abstract: Infinite-order U -statistics play a vital role in modern statistics. However, given their degree k n $k_n$ k Subscript n depends on the sample size n , quantifying their variability is quite challenging, as fixed-degree theories cannot be directly adopted. In this article, we propose a jackknife empirical likelihood (EL) framework that can be used to construct confidence intervals for an infinite-order U -statistic. We establish sufficient conditions for the limiting chi-squared distribution of the JEL ratio statistic and introduce an efficient partition-sampling realization for practical implementation. To evaluate the performance of the proposed methodology, we conduct simulation studies in the context of subsampling-based ensemble methods and the maximum test, respectively, comparing its performance with four competing methods. The simulation studies yield satisfactory results across the board. Finally, we demonstrate the practical application of our method using a United States Forest Service timber auctions dataset to predict the highest bid at an auction.

title: Vertical Integration and Coordination in Modernising Staple Food Value Chains: Evidence From Myanmar's Rice Sector
abstract: ABSTRACT Increased vertical integration and coordination are defining features of transforming and modernising agricultural value chains in low‐ and middle‐income countries, with important implications for market efficiency and farm‐level transformation. However, research documenting these processes in transforming domestic value chains is limited, with existing studies largely focusing on large firms, foreign direct investment and high‐value food products, leaving less understood how domestic processors in staple food value chains expand into complementary businesses and services. We study these processes in the rice value chain—the most important staple in Southeast Asia—in Myanmar, using unique large‐scale data from domestic rice mills and farmers. We show that both modern and traditional mills serve as key nodes in local rice value chains, fulfilling diverse roles beyond processing at both the farm and post‐harvest levels. Yet, statistical tests that control for mill and farmer characteristics, respectively, show that modern mills are more engaged in vertical integration and coordination, particularly in post‐harvest value chain segments, highlighting the co‐development of modern processing and business expansion. Consistent with this pattern in the miller data, farmers using a modern mill are more likely to receive complementary services—especially post‐harvest—and to adopt modern production practices more broadly. However, this expansion is uneven, with services reaching large farms more frequently than small and medium farms.

title: Mitigating School Closures: Parental Responses and Tutoring Vouchers
abstract: ABSTRACT We investigate how school closures affect educational outcomes through parental responses. Using quasi‐experimental variation in school‐level closure days and linked administrative‐survey data, we find that 10 additional closure days raise private tutoring expenditure by 4.1% and within‐school test‐score dispersion by 25%; over the average 53‐day closure, low‐income students lose 0.09 SD. To quantify substitution between schooling and parental investment and evaluate compensatory policy, we estimate a tournament model in which schooling and tutoring jointly produce test scores. Tutoring substitutes for in‐person days, burdening low‐income households disproportionately. Counterfactuals show a means‐tested voucher fully offsets the resulting rise in inequality.

title: Environmental Incidents and Sustainability Pricing Provisions

title: Measuring Measurement Error
abstract: Abstract We collect 2,848 instrumental variable (IV) regressions from 391 papers published in top economics and finance journals and show that estimated IV coefficients are often much larger than their OLS counterparts, even when theory suggests they should be smaller. We derive meta-regression estimators that distinguish measurement error bias from omitted variable bias and simultaneity bias; applying our estimators to a set of 1,040 comparable regressions from 139 papers, we find that measurement error shrinks reported coefficients by about two to four times. Measurement error remains quantitatively important even after accounting for weak instruments, publication bias, instrument invalidity, and heterogeneous treatment effects. Our results suggest that measurement error is a severe, pervasive, and understated source of bias in economics and finance.

title: Generalizing the Pareto principle with endogenous populations
Simulating competitive collocation strategies with deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Abstract This paper introduces a simulation model based on deep reinforcement learning to study competitive collocation strategies of two internationalizing firms. Drawing on the strategic interaction and competitive collocation literature in IB, we explore the factors determining the performance-optimizing degree of collocation in market-seeking internationalization for a duopoly in product markets. Our simulation suggests that a high degree of collocation between the two firms is optimal in many circumstances. Whereas mid-to-high levels of collocation are driven by low competitive intensity, low entry barriers, low home-market size, and high market-size variation, complete collocation emerges under high competitive intensity, low first-mover advantage, and smaller home-market size. High entry barriers, combined with low variation in market size and strong liabilities of foreignness, drive the opposite case of complete mutual avoidance. A key takeaway from the simulation is a focus on the competing firm in global expansion: in many cases, it becomes key to limit the rival’s growth options and to enter key markets before access becomes more restricted. We discuss the possibilities of using computer-simulation-based approaches to theorizing on internationalization.

title: CEO Ideologically (In)Congruent Activism and Investor Reactions: An Attribution of CEO Intentions Perspective
abstract: Abstract The phenomenon of chief executive officers (CEOs) taking activism stances on contested sociopolitical issues is increasing, yet it remains unclear how observing investors discern CEO intentions behind activism engagements, thereby shaping their judgments and subsequent reactions. By relaxing the assumption that CEO activism is an unabashed expression of personal beliefs, we propose the concept of CEO ideologically (in)congruent activism and develop a framework wherein investors may attribute CEO intentions underlying incongruent (versus congruent) activism engagements as more organization‐driven (versus self‐driven) interest pursuits, thereby leading to more positive investor evaluations and reactions. Furthermore, we argue that the positive effect of CEO ideologically incongruent activism on investor reactions will be amplified when the CEO owns a higher level of stock ownership but weakened when the firm receives a greater corporate social responsibility (CSR) rating. We corroborate our propositions using a sample of CEO activism events for S&P 500 firms from 2012 to 2021. Our findings demonstrate the heterogeneity and critical influence of CEO intentions behind activism engagements and shed light on how investors integrate multi‐informational cues when evaluating and reacting to managerial incongruent behaviours.

title: EXPRESS: The Role of Digital Ad Clutter in Ad Viewership and Memory
abstract: Advertisers face an increasingly cluttered digital ecosystem where customer attention matters. Despite this, the extent to which digital advertising clutter influences ad viewership remains unclear. This paper presents three separate eye-tracking experiments (subjects: N = 99, N = 250, and N = 575) using over a dozen custom-built web pages to better understand how digital ad clutter affects consumers’ viewing of digital ads. Across experiments, we show that increased clutter led consumers to allocate more attention to the overall advertising space and adjust how they distribute viewership across ad positions. A complementary survey revealed that clutter also reduced ad memory and recall for individual ads. We discuss the implications for advertisers and publishers regarding ad pricing and placement in crowded digital environments.

title: EXPRESS: Correcting omitted-variable bias without instruments: An ICA-based alternative to Gaussian copula methods
abstract: This paper proposes an instrument-free correction for omitted-variable bias and overcomes a key limitation of Gaussian copula control function (GCCF) approaches. Omitted-variable bias is the most common source of endogeneity in marketing, and many articles apply GCCF to address it. Yet GCCF require a nonlinear regressor-error relation, whereas textbooks assume linear, additive relationships between regressors and omitted variables. The authors prove that GCCF is biased in classical omitted-variable settings. Extant articles that address omitted-variables with GCCF also show language cues implicitly assuming linear relationships, which invalidate the use of GCCF. The proposed endogeneity correction is tailored to this prominent case, utilizing independent component analysis (ICA). It assumes a latent normally distributed component that additively influences both the endogenous regressor and the error. This can be interpreted as the sum of omitted variables, which, according to the Central Limit Theorem, add up to a normal distribution. Through ICA, this component is identified and extracted from the endogenous regressor, rendering the regression model free of endogeneity and enabling causal inference. The paper proves that the model is point-identified despite endogeneity due to omitted variables, that the proposed estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal, and that Jackknife resampling yields valid standard errors.

title: EXPRESS: Why are products so similar despite diverse consumer needs? The interplay between advertising and horizontal product differentiation
abstract: Firms are often less differentiated than standard price-competition models predict. We explain this gap by showing how firms can use informative or reminder advertising to soften competition. When firms choose locations, advertising, and prices endogenously, they may choose to soften price competition through limited advertising rather than greater product differentiation, allowing them to locate closer together while limiting price competition. This outcome of low advertising and central collocation is especially likely when advertising costs are high. We also observe that partially-differentiated equilibria, with one firm locating centrally and the other at an edge, and full differentiation, can each emerge under certain conditions. Thus, firms endogenously choose a mix of advertising and product differentiation to moderate price competition. Further, the shape of travel costs influences the equilibrium outcome. If the disutility from distance is highly convex, such as occurs when consumer preferences exhibit satisficing, central collocation becomes the unique equilibrium when more consumers are concentrated at the edge locations. However, when the disutility from distance is linear, having more customers located towards the edge locations makes collocation less likely. Overall, the interaction of advertising costs, consumer preferences, and location choices help explain why firms often forgo product differentiation.

title: Competition and Diversity in Generative AI
abstract: Recent evidence, both in the laboratory and in the wild, suggests that the use of generative artificial intelligence reduces the diversity of content produced. As generative AI penetrates more markets and reaches widespread adoption, should we still expect to see content homogenization? Our work begins with a simple observation: content producers do not act in isolation. Instead, they compete with one another (e.g., for customers or attention). We explore the impact competition has on both content diversity and overall social welfare when producers use generative AI. Through a formal game-theoretic model, we show that competitive markets select for diverse AI models, mitigating monoculture. We further show that a generative AI model that performs well in isolation (i.e., according to a benchmark) may fail to provide value in a competitive market. Our results highlight the importance of evaluating generative AI models across the breadth of their output distributions, particularly when they will be deployed in competitive environments. We validate our theoretical results with a series of experiments involving generative text and image models. Overall, our results suggest that homogenization due to generative AI is unlikely to persist under strong competition. This paper was accepted by Itai Ashlagi, market design, platform, and demand analytics. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02761 .

title: The Buy-in Effect: When Increasing Initial Effort Encourages Follow-Through
abstract: Behavioral interventions often focus on reducing friction to encourage behavior change. In contrast, we provide evidence that adding initial friction to a sign-up process can increase follow-through behavior. In a field experiment with a state department of transportation ([Formula: see text]), we test whether adding modest friction during sign-up for a carpool platform increases usage. Although a more effortful sign-up process leads to 25% fewer sign-ups, overall usage increases. Importantly, these results were only partly explained by selection: Using an intent-to-treat analysis, participants with a more effortful sign-up process took 1.6 times more carpool trips per week over four months, leading to more overall trips despite fewer users. In a second experiment with online task work, participants with more effortful sign-up were 37% more likely to return the next day and completed more work overall. These results suggest that adding friction may be an overlooked strategy when follow-through, rather than initial uptake, is the primary goal. This paper was accepted by George Wu, behavioral economics and decision analysis. Funding: The authors acknowledge funding from the University of Konstanz for Study 2, Harvard University Pershing Square Foundation for Human Research, and Harvard Business School. The funders had no role in data collection and analysis, the decision to publish, or preparation of this manuscript. Supplemental Material: The online appendices and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.03600 .

title: Measuring Organizational Constructs in Large-Scale Text: An interpretive framework combining topic modeling and BERT
abstract: Measuring organizational constructs in large-scale unstructured text requires methods that preserve interpretive depth while enabling systematic, per-document classification. Structural Topic Modeling (STM) supports interpretive depth by surfacing patterns that inform construct operationalization, but its topic proportions are not designed as standalone per-document construct measures; transformer-based models such as BERT can scale measurement but require construct operationalization grounded in interpretive work. We address this challenge through a two-stage framework in which STM and BERT play structurally distinct roles. Coding schemes are developed through qualitative interpretation and STM analysis; BERT is then fine-tuned to apply these schemes across documents. We formalize two research approaches—construct-guided and pattern-discovery—that provide principled paths from different theoretical starting points toward a shared methodological endpoint: validated, auditable per-document construct measures. We illustrate the framework using more than 20,000 employee reviews. The framework supports iterative construct validation, using computational diagnostics to guide interpretive refinement and producing document-level measures suitable for theory-informed organizational analysis.

title: Media Review: Homebound: Caste, Muslim Identity, and the Organizational Politics of Stigmatized Lives
