title: Impact of sensing modality on surrogate safety metrics: A radar–camera fusion framework for signalized intersection approach monitoring
abstract: Camera systems are common in surrogate safety analysis at signalized intersections, but their velocity estimates remain underexamined. For approach-lane following, frame-to-frame position differencing introduces errors from bounding-box jitter and perspective distortion that propagate into Time-to-Collision (TTC) and a longitudinal following time gap (FTG). We develop a roadside radar–camera fusion framework combining Doppler measurements with CCTV detections using geometric association and a learned confidence model, evaluated against drone trajectories at two intersections. Unfiltered camera estimation produces 3.26 times the exposure-normalized rate of critical TTC episodes that fusion reports. Temporal filtering reduces noise but compresses leader–follower speed differences, suppressing TTC observations. Fusion reduces velocity error standard deviation from 12.59 to 7.39 mph (41.3%) and raises correlation with drone velocity from r = 0.548 to r = 0.760 ( Δ r = 0.212 ). Savitzky–Golay and Kalman smoothing close this gap, but they use future observations or require ground-truth tuning. Better velocity correlation does not guarantee better TTC results, because correlation evaluates individual speeds whereas TTC depends on the instantaneous difference between them. Two filtered versions of fusion with nearly identical correlation ( Δ r = 0.0039 ) report critical rates 9.74 points apart. The Kalman-smoothed camera, most accurate on velocity, differs from the drone critical TTC rate by 37.72 points. Unfiltered camera estimation flags a critical interaction where the drone does not in 5.60% of pair-frames, against 1.90% for fusion. This pattern replicates directionally at a second site with an oblique camera view. Velocity validation alone cannot establish safety-metric reliability. Radar–camera fusion can provide a more stable basis for monitoring at both sites.

title: Cumulative social determinants of health and long-term health outcomes among survivors of childhood sexual abuse: A retrospective chart review
Provisional Masculine Resources and Disastrous Gender Inequalities
abstract: Drawing on participant observation and 139 in-depth interviews following a California megafire, this paper demonstrates how disasters work as social settings that generate and organize access to what I term “provisional masculine resources” while providing opportunities to articulate inequalities as natural and inevitable. These data demonstrate how gender regimes maintain flexibility in response to exogenous shocks (i.e., disasters) by shifting the definitions of and access to relational, gendered behaviors. Unequal gender regimes are produced and legitimated in disastrous times by (1) clarifying the complementary traits and behaviors associated with hegemonic masculinity and emphasized femininity, (2) organizing potent social rewards around gendered relationships, and (3) providing opportunities to articulate gendered identities and behaviors as natural. In the case of fire recovery, provisional masculine resources explain how the means through which men accomplish manhood change in availability temporally, at different times producing positive social rewards and negative consequences, yet continuously work to uphold unequal, patriarchal gender regimes.

title: Generative AI vs. Human Sources for Sexual Health Information: Credibility, Trust, and Behavioral Intentions in a U.S. College Sample
abstract: Limited access to comprehensive sexual health education has prompted a need to consider the utility of alternative strategies, such as generative artificial intelligence (genAI), for delivering accurate and accessible sexual health information. Although genAI tools can generate health information, less is known about how perceptions of the source of information shape evaluations of content (e.g., human vs. genAI). The present study examined whether college students' perceptions of sexual health information differed based on source attribution. Participants (N = 266) were students recruited from a single university in the southeastern USA in 2025. They were randomly assigned to conditions in which they were made to believe that three sexual health passages that were identical across conditions (sexual communication, body image, and sexual pleasure and safety) were written by genAI, an academic expert, a community health professional, or a peer/social media influencer. Across outcomes-including perceived accuracy and clarity, warmth and helpfulness, trustworthiness, self-efficacy, and willingness to act-genAI-attributed information was evaluated less favorably than identical information attributed to human sources. For willingness to act, there were differences in source effects across topics, such that effects were strongest for sexual pleasure/safety and weakest for sexual communication. Findings remained significant after controlling for genAI familiarity/use and attitudes. Findings indicate that evaluations of sexual health information depend not only on informational content but also on perceived source legitimacy, suggesting that AI-based tools may be the most effective when paired with human guidance to support trust and actionability.

title: Unlocking the potential benefits of intertemporal resources via explicit embedding future value of the end-of-day state in day-ahead dispatch
Coordinated computing-energy optimization of data center microgrids in a joint kilowatt-negawatt P2P market
State-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries from random local charging fragments: A reliability-aware local-global fusion framework
Effects of climatic control on microenvironmental responses in desert PV systems: A comparative analysis with machine learning interpretation
abstract: Microenvironmental responses to desert photovoltaic (PV) systems have been increasingly reported, yet how these responses vary across contrasting arid climate backgrounds remains insufficiently understood under comparable engineering settings. In this study, cross-climate field observations, Δ-response modeling, and SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) interpretation were combined to examine PV-induced environmental change at the Wuwei and Hami sites in northwestern China. Instead of reproducing absolute local states, the models estimated PV-induced deviations from the reference (REF) position, ΔY(position) = Y(position) − Y(REF), for the below-panel (BL) and interrow (IT) positions. The Wuwei site exhibited coupled hydrothermal regulation, with enhanced shallow soil-water retention after rainfall, whereas the Hami site exhibited predominantly thermal regulation because its moisture-retention pathway was largely inactive under extremely low precipitation, coarse soil, and strong evaporative demand. Soil-temperature perturbations were consistently predictable (best-model R 2 = 0.93–0.99), whereas air-temperature perturbations showed moderate skill (R 2 = 0.41–0.65) and relative-humidity perturbations were strongly site dependent (Hami: 0.14–0.19; Wuwei: 0.47–0.97). Grouped SHAP analysis distinguished the predictor groups associated with air-temperature, soil-thermal, and soil-moisture responses. Sparse interaction networks further elucidated the joint roles of these predictor groups in shaping model responses across climates and distinguished relatively stable thermal structures from climate-sensitive hydrothermal linkages. It is hoped that these analyses will contribute to the development of climate-adaptive, site-specific environmental monitoring strategies for desert PV plants.

title: Spatiotemporal analysis of global future photovoltaic potential and its driving mechanisms
abstract: Accurate estimation of photovoltaic (PV) potential under future climate scenarios is critical for global decarbonization and energy transition planning. This study employed the Global Solar Energy Estimation model to calculate PV potential and carbon mitigation across three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) using calibrated data of 2015–2100 from the CMIP6 data based on the Bayesian Model Averaging method. Results showed that the global annual mean PV capacity factor (CF) (power generation) was 0.1622 (2010 TWh), 0.1597 (1993 TWh), and 0.1543 (1961 TWh) under low (SSP1-2.6), intermediate (SSP2-4.5), and high (SSP5-8.5) carbon emission scenarios, respectively. Correspondingly, 33%, 12%, and 8% of global land area exhibited significant increases in CFs. Experiments of climate impacts on PV potential revealed that a reduction in PV CF (power generation) of 0.0008 (1 TWh) per decade under high carbon emission scenario, driven by a decline in surface solar radiation from increased aerosols and cloud cover, along with panel efficiency losses from rising air temperature. Investigation of physical factors on PV potential indicated that the advanced crystalline silicon materials and two-axis panel tracking systems demonstrated substantial potential in enhancing PV power generation and carbon mitigation. Moreover, the driving mechanisms of the climate variables on PV potential was also investigated based on the Structural Equation Modeling method. Our findings quantify the potential of PV technology in generation and decarbonization, assisting in policy development in energy transitions to address climate change.

title: Degradation-aware optimization of SOFC operating strategies under off-design balance-of-plant dynamics
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems face significant performance and cost challenges due to stack degradation and the resulting off-design operation of balance-of-plant (BoP) components. This study presents an optimization framework for SOFC operation that explicitly accounts for stack degradation and off-design BoP dynamics. A 10-cell hydrogen-fueled SOFC stack was fabricated and tested under varied flow and humidity conditions to obtain polarization data, which were used to calibrate the system model with an R 2 of 94.7–99.2%. The calibrated model, coupled with surrogate-based optimization, enables time-segmented scheduling of current density and fuel utilization with periodic setpoint updates over a 20-year techno-economic assessment based on levelized cost of electricity (LCOE), electrical efficiency, and lifetime electricity output. The results show that, under the assumptions of the representative case study, the optimized schedules can reduce LCOE by up to 16%, increase lifetime electrical efficiency by more than 10 percentage points, and increase cumulative electricity output by nearly 20%. In addition, the sensitivity of the optimal schedules to the adjustment interval reveals practical trade-offs between economic performance and computational cost. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to identify improved long-term SOFC operating strategies under degradation and off-design constraints, while the absolute economic values remain case-dependent.

title: Infoergy equation: A case study on vehicle energy management technology
abstract: “Infoergy” is not a typo, but rather the energization of information, which is an abbreviation for “information-energy”. Vehicle energy-saving is progressively evolving toward intelligent energy management systems that integrate information interaction; however, there remains a lack of quantitative description of the coupling relationship between information quantity and energy consumption. This hinders the full utilization of information to uncover energy-saving potential in energy management decisions and prevents an objective assessment of information's contribution to enhancing system energy efficiency. Therefore, this study proposes for the first time an information-energy equation that describes the intrinsic connection between information and energy in vehicle energy management technology. Aiming at the comprehensive information representation of multi-source time-varying information within the context of vehicle energy management, this equation defines vehicle velocity as the observable random variable of working condition information to quantify its uncertainty. An energy-saving potential evaluation system is then established. Then, by utilizing information metrics and energy-saving indicators to construct a nonlinear mapping model, it reveals the impact of working condition complexity on energy consumption from the perspective of information. The validation results demonstrate that the proposed infoergy equation exhibits excellent fitting accuracy and generalization capability. It effectively reproduces energy consumption trends and possesses good physical interpretability. At the application level, compared to other methods, the new paradigm of information-energy coupling mechanisms demonstrates better energy-saving effects. It provides a novel theoretical foundation and precise quantitative tools for unlocking energy-saving potential in intelligent energy management, laying the groundwork for deep energy savings in intelligent transportation systems.

title: Two-stage random forest framework for offshore platform identification to analyze spatial patterns and activity levels
abstract: Offshore oil and gas platforms constitute critical infrastructure for national energy resource development, with their spatial density and operational activity exerting direct influence on national energy production capacity and the stability of maritime energy corridors. This study develops a multi-source remote sensing framework for identifying and analysing global offshore oil and gas platforms, integrating Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, and VIIRS nighttime light imagery. A two-stage random forest approach is used for platform identification, supporting the construction of a global long-term platform dataset and subsequent spatial and temporal analyses. Utilizing monthly VIIRS nighttime light time series from 2017 to 2024, platform activity patterns are characterized through a radiometric contrast approach, revealing temporal variations and distinct seasonal characteristics across major producing countries. Furthermore, a framework for analysing the global spatial patterns of offshore oil and gas platforms was developed. Using the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) as the basic unit of analysis, the framework employs indicators including platform density, average nearest-neighbor distance, nearest-neighbor index, and local clustering intensity to quantitatively characterize their spatial distribution and clustering characteristics, revealing regional differences and spatial heterogeneity in offshore oil and gas development. The multi-source remote sensing framework and quantitative analyses developed in this study provide a consistent basis for characterising the global spatial and temporal patterns of offshore oil and gas platforms, and may support further research on offshore energy development, marine spatial planning, and related resource management.

title: Role of Coordination Environment in the Oxidation of CrIII Aminocarboxylate Complexes by Hydrous Manganese Oxide
abstract: Abstract Oxidation of CrIII to CrVI by MnIII,IV (hydr)oxides plays an important role in controlling chromium mobility and toxicity in soils and sediments. Previous studies on CrIII oxidation by hydrous manganese oxide (HMO) reveals that reaction rates are highly sensitive to CrIII speciation, with aminocarboxylate complexes exhibiting reaction-induced Mn2+ accumulation at HMO surfaces, which progressively inhibits CrVI production. In this work, we compare initial CrVI production rates for well-defined, presynthesized CrIII–aminocarboxylate complexes with the chelating agents iminodiacetic acid (IDA), nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA), N-(2-hydroxyethyl)ethylenediaminetriacetic acid (HEDTA), and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA). Initial-rate measurements minimize the influence of secondary ligand oxidation, reaction-generated MnII, and associated changes in HMO reactivity, thereby providing a common basis for comparing the effects of CrIII coordination environment. Initial CrVI production rates spanned 8 orders of magnitude and generally decrease as aminocarboxylate ligands occupy a greater fraction of the CrIII coordination sphere and fewer coordination positions remain occupied by H2O and OH–. These results demonstrate that CrIII oxidation by Mn oxides is acutely sensitive to the CrIII coordination environment, with important implications for CrVI formation in natural and engineered systems. These findings demonstrate that meaningful prediction of CrVI formation requires explicit consideration of CrIII speciation.

title: Kinetics of CO2 Hydrate Formation and Chemical-Potential-Driven Dissociation in Porous Media
abstract: Abstract Gas hydrates can form when water and a guest gas coexist within the hydrate stability field. Gas hydrates in porous rocks block flow fields. During CO2 storage in depleted reservoirs, pressure reduction and Joule–Thomson cooling may place near-well regions within the CO2 hydrate stability zone, raising concerns about injectivity loss. Hydrate stability is commonly inferred from the bulk pressure–temperature (P–T) phase diagram, which neglects flow and gas humidity transport under sustained flow. Using time-resolved optical microscopy in a “fish-bone” micromodel at fixed P and T, we find that injecting low-humidity CO2 produces a pore-scale cycle of hydrate formation and dissociation. The hydrate nucleates along gas–water–solid contact lines and grows by consuming CO2 dissolved in trapped pore water and then slows as CO2 supply becomes diffusion-limited through the hydrate layer. Despite constant bulk P and T, the low humidity of the injected CO2 extracts water as vapor, creating a water chemical potential deficit at the gas–hydrate interface and driving an inlet-to-outlet dissociation front. These results show that hydrate persistence under flow depends on pore-scale transport and gas-side water chemical potential and cannot be inferred from bulk P–T stability conditions alone.

title: OH-Initiated Heterogeneous Reactions of Novel Organophosphate Esters: Insights into Oxidation Chemistry and Atmospheric Persistence
abstract: Abstract Novel organophosphate esters (OPEs), formed through chemical transformation of commercial antioxidants, are emerging contaminants with widespread environmental occurrence and potential health effects. Despite their widespread detection, the atmospheric reactivity, persistence, and transformation of novel OPEs remain unknown. Here, the heterogeneous OH oxidation of two surface-bound novel OPEs [tris(2,4-ditert-butylphenyl) phosphate (TDtBPP) and triisodecyl phosphate (TiDeP)] was explored by investigating the reaction kinetics and chemical mechanisms. The measured heterogeneous rate constants for TDtBPP and TiDeP were (2.81 ± 0.12) × 10–12 and (1.99 ± 0.16) × 10–12 cm3 molecules–1 s–1, respectively, equivalent to atmospheric lifetimes of up to 6.3 and 9.0 days. These lifetimes are significantly longer than previously predicted values (<1 day), suggesting that they are much more persistent in air than predicted. Based on UPLC-HRMS measurements, 22 transformation products from the heterogeneous reactions were identified for the first time. Analysis of atmospheric particle samples from two megacities in China identified four TDtBPP transformation products, demonstrating that the oxidation chemistry can occur under genuine environmental conditions. In-silico hazard screening further indicated that many transformation products may be more bioaccumulative and more toxic than the parent novel OPEs. The results not only provide new insights into the atmospheric persistence of novel OPEs but also underscore the significance of considering atmospheric transformation in the risk assessment of these emerging contaminants.

title: Correspondence on “Legacy and Emerging Plasticizers and Stabilizers in PVC Floorings and Implications for Recycling”
Rebuttal to Correspondence on “Legacy and Emerging Plasticizers and Stabilizers in PVC Floorings and Implications for Recycling”
Analysis of the Potential Mediating Role of Plasma Proteins in the Association Between Air Pollution Exposure and Lung Cancer Risk Among Ever-Smokers
abstract: Abstract The biological mechanisms linking air pollution to lung carcinogenesis remain underexplored. This study aimed to identify key proteins and pathways involved in mediating the effects of air pollutants on lung cancer risk. We analyzed 95 matched lung cancer case–control pairs of ever-smokers with prediagnosis plasma protein profiles measured in the Cancer Prevention Study-II Nutrition Cohort. We assessed associations between protein levels and six individual air pollutants, air pollution mixture, and lung cancer risk, adjusting for confounders and multiple testing. We identified overlapping proteins and enriched pathways associated with both exposures and lung cancer risk, followed by an exploratory high-dimensional mediation analysis (HIMA) to investigate the potential mediating roles of proteins. Seventeen proteins were associated with both exposures and lung cancer, including CX3CL1, ADAM15, and CXCL17 (P < 0.05). HIMA identified six proteins, including CX3CL1 and CXCL17, as potential mediating proteins of individual pollutant-lung cancer associations (Bonferroni-corrected P < 0.05), while these findings did not remain significant when excluding cases diagnosed within one year of blood draw. The exploratory results suggest that proteins and pathways related to inflammatory chemokine signaling, immune modulation, and altered cell proliferation, migration, and survival may play significant roles in air pollution-lung cancer association among ever-smokers.

title: Fe3 + Activation of Metal Sulfides for High-Performance Mercury Removal from Nonferrous Smelting Gas: A Dual Mercury Adsorption Mechanism
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric elemental mercury (Hg0) emitted from the nonferrous metallurgy industry poses severe risks to ecosystems. Although metal sulfides are promising in Hg0 adsorption under high-concentration SO2 conditions, they typically suffer from poor performance at elevated temperatures due to weak binding affinity. Herein, a trivalent iron (Fe3+) activation strategy to boost Hg0 adsorption activity of metal sulfides was developed for the first time, which leverages electron-deficient Fe3+ to induce electronic reconstruction. This Fe3+ activation strategy is applicable to various metal sulfides, generating Fe sites with high activity and stability. Among the various candidates, the Fe3+-activated MoS2 delivers a record-theoretical saturated Hg0 adsorption capacity of 69.56 mg·g–1 at 150 °C, which is 4.35 times higher than that of pristine MoS2. The sulfur vacancies on MoS2 serve as the key anchoring sites for Fe3+, generating stable single-atom, dimer, and trimer Fe configurations. These new Fe centers, benefiting from charge modulation, can simultaneously adsorb two Hg atoms via charge transfer and orbital hybridization. The Fe3+-activated MoS2 exhibits strong resistance to SO2 and H2O, maintaining high Hg0 removal efficiency under a smelting gas atmosphere. This work reveals new configurations of Hg adsorption and provides a convenient route to design high-performance sorbents for heavy metal purification.

title: Divergent Responses of Manganese Oxides to Olivine Dissolution and Their Control on Trace Metal Fates under an Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement Scenario
abstract: Abstract Olivine-based ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is a promising carbon dioxide removal technology; however, the geochemical fate of olivine-derived toxic metals, particularly nickel (Ni) and chromium (Cr) at marine sediment interfaces, remains poorly constrained. We employed dialysis-membrane microcosms to isolate olivine from Mn oxides, allowing only dissolved species to diffuse and react under three olivine loadings (1, 5, and 10 g L–1) in seawater for 60 days. Results revealed that (1) Ni was preferentially sequestered by the Mn oxides, with δ-MnO2 showing higher uptake capacity than birnessite, (2) Cr was co-sequestered with secondary Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxides rather than adsorbing directly onto Mn oxides, and (3) synergistic Ni2+ isomorphic substitution and Fe(II)-driven Mn(III) reduction rearranged δ-MnO2 into a more stable hexagonal layered framework. Consequently, both δ-MnO2 and birnessite act as long-term Ni sinks, preventing Ni remobilization via desorption or diagenetic phase transitions. These findings support a proposed “spatial decoupling” OAE strategy, where olivine is pre-dissolved in land- or ship-based reactors to remove Cr via Fe co-precipitation. Subsequent discharge of the Ni-bearing alkaline effluent into shallow coastal regions allows benthic Mn oxides to scavenge Ni, reducing toxicity risks associated with direct mineral contact.

title: Regional Impacts of Unconventional Oil and Gas Operations on Ozone and Air Toxics
abstract: Abstract Unconventional oil and gas development (UOGD) has expanded over the past three decades and now accounts for most of U.S. oil and natural gas production. Although prior studies link local UOGD activity to health outcomes, they provide limited evidence directly attributing ambient pollutant levels to UOGD emissions. We address this gap by quantifying UOGD impacts on ozone and air toxics using the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model with the Integrated Source Apportionment Method (ISAM), enabling an explicit linkage between UOGD emissions and ambient concentrations. UOGD activities produce substantial local contributions to primary air toxics and continental-scale influences on ozone. Across CONUS, UOGD increases population-weighted annual averages of maximum daily average 8-h (MDA8) ozone, 1-h benzene, 1-h nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and 1-h formaldehyde (HCHO) concentrations by roughly 1 ppb, 1.1 ppt, 0.035 ppb, and 0.03 ppb, respectively. Annual maximum UOGD contributions to MDA8 ozone are about half of those from other anthropogenic sources. ISAM also reveals unexpectedly large UOGD-driven ozone enhancement (up to 4–5 ppb) in the Los Angeles region from Texas emissions, a feature less evident in brute-force sensitivity tests. These findings highlight the need to further examine interstate UOGD influences on nonattainment areas and source-impact quantification methods.

title: Photochemical Interactions of Nitrate Photolysis and Photosensitization of BBOA: Enhanced HONO Production and the Formation of Nitrophenols
abstract: Abstract Renoxification of nitrate to reactive nitrogen species (RNS) can sustain atmospheric oxidant production. Because nitrate and light-absorbing brown carbon can coexist in biomass burning (BB) plumes, their photochemical interaction may alter RNS cycling. Furthermore, nitration of phenols in biomass burning organic aerosol (BBOA) can form nitrophenols, potentially increasing the warming effect of aged BBOA. Yet the mechanisms of renoxification and nitration in irradiated nitrate-BBOA mixtures remain poorly understood. We experimentally investigate these coupled processes over a wide range of fir-wood BBOA concentrations during aqueous nitrate photolysis (10 mM) under acidic conditions using H2SO4. At low BBOA concentration (TOCBBOA/NO3– ≤ 0.0036 mg L–1/mg L–1), the steady-state production rate of HONO (Pss_HONO) increased as BBOA concentration increased, reaching a maximum enhancement factor of 1.8 driven primarily by triplet-mediated photosensitized reduction of NO2 to HONO. At higher BBOA concentration (TOCBBOA/NO3– > 0.0036 mg L–1/mg L–1), Pss_HONO progressively decreased and was nearly fully suppressed at TOCBBOA/NO3– = 0.7 mg L–1/mg L–1. This inhibition is attributed to reactions of aqueous HNO2/NO2 with phenols, accompanied by formation of nitrophenols. These findings point to a potentially overlooked daytime HONO source and an atmospheric source of nitrophenols, a key class of BrC chromophores, via photochemical interactions between nitrate photolysis and photosensitization of BBOA.

title: Research Priorities for a Circular Economy for Plastic Sustainability in the Caribbean
abstract: Abstract Caribbean countries bear a disproportionate burden of marine plastic pollution because of their small landmass, high population density, and insufficient waste management infrastructure. Many Caribbean nations depend on informal, unmanaged landfills, underscoring an urgent need for more resilient, sustainable systems. This perspective synthesizes existing data to map the region’s plastic waste landscape and leverages regional expertise to identify key research priorities. This work emerged from interdisciplinary international professionals and members of the CEPlaSt (circular economy for plastic sustainability) network. A major barrier to circularity is the lack of reliable data on waste composition and flows, alongside stark infrastructure disparities across the wider Caribbean region. Addressing these gaps through targeted investment and region-specific planning is essential to modernize waste systems, reduce plastic emissions, and advance a sustainable Caribbean plastic circular economy.

title: Submarine Groundwater Discharge Acts as a Significant Vector for Coastal Organophosphate Esters: Joint Evidence from Pollution Surveys and Radionuclide Analysis
abstract: Abstract Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are ubiquitous marine contaminants that raise global concern. While surface inputs are well-studied, the role of subsurface transport remains poorly constrained. Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) drives seawater-groundwater interactions, yet its impact on OPEs behavior remains overlooked. This study comprehensively investigates the distribution, transport property and sources of OPEs from coastal groundwater to seawater in the Beibu Gulf, China. No statistically significant difference in Σ19OPEs levels was found between groundwater and tidal flat porewater, while both matrices exhibited significantly higher levels than seawater. The high compositional similarity, strong correlations (p < 0.01) and PCA overlap of OPEs in different waters, as well as their shared source profiles indicated the transport potential of OPEs from groundwater to seawater. Multiple statistical modeling integrating OPEs, environmental factors and DOM components reveals the land-to-sea transport pathways and biogeochemical processes of OPEs via SGD. Furthermore, radon isotope analysis verified the presence of SGD, offering evidence for SGD-mediated OPE transport. For the first time, this work integrates pollutant investigation, multiple statistical analysis, and radionuclide tracing, to identify SGD as a previously underestimated vector of coastal OPEs and elucidates its potential transport mechanisms, providing crucial support for integrated land-sea management and risk assessment.

title: Associations of PM2.5 and Its Oxidative Potential with Childhood Allergy-Related Symptoms: A Cross-Sectional Study in Guangdong Province, China
abstract: Abstract Evidence linking PM2.5 exposure to allergic symptoms remains limited and inconsistent, partly because most studies rely on mass-based metrics alone. We conducted a population-based study among 131,346 children aged 6–18 years in six cities of Guangdong, China, to compare associations of PM2.5 mass concentration, oxidative potential (OP), and chemical components (metals, carbonaceous components, and ions) with rhinitis, rhinoconjunctivitis, and eczema symptoms. OP was assessed using the dithiothreitol assay and expressed as volume-normalized (DTTv) and mass-normalized (DTTm) metrics. PM2.5 mass and OP were generally positively associated with the three allergy-related symptoms. OP, particularly DTTm, provided more consistent and robust evidence of associations across outcomes than PM2.5 mass, supported by lower AIC/BIC values and greater stability in two-pollutant models. Single-component and mixture analyses indicated that multiple PM2.5 constituents contributed to allergy-related symptoms, and OP may partly explain the associations of Co, OC, Cu, and Hg, with the largest estimated indirect proportion reaching 36.2% for OC and rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms through DTTm. These findings suggest that OP captures health-relevant characteristics beyond particle mass and may serve as a complementary exposure indicator for understanding childhood symptoms of allergic diseases.

title: Aqueous Carbonyl-Amino Aggregation Drives Atmospheric Nitrogen-Containing Oligomer Formation in China Haze
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-containing organic compounds (NOCs) are ubiquitous in the troposphere and contribute to the reactive nitrogen cycle and aerosol light absorption, yet their formation mechanisms remain unclear, especially in polluted regions. Here, we characterized NOCs in PM2.5 during winter haze in the North China Plain (NCP), with a comparison to those in the Sichuan Basin (ScB). Reduced-nitrogen NOCs (Re-NOCs) accounted for 40% of organics detected in the ESI+ mode, highlighting their importance within atmospheric NOCs. Compared to dry haze (DH) in NCP, high-molecular-weight (HMW, m/z > 250) Re-NOCs in humid haze (HH) were enhanced, which positively correlated with NH4+ and the mass ratio of aqueous-phase secondary organic aerosols to total water-soluble organic aerosols, along with increases in aliphatic chain length and molecular unsaturation, indicating carbonyl-amino-driven oligomerization and cyclization. Aliphatic Re-NOCs dominated the Re-NOCs during HH, together with strong correlations of a typical NOC oligomer (C8H13N3O2) with water-soluble organic nitrogen and HMW Re-NOCs, further suggesting oligomerization as a key formation pathway for NOCs. We found that stronger aerosol acidity and higher temperature favored oligomerization of Re-NOCs compared to cyclization, resulting in enhanced C8H13N3O2 in ScB relative to that in NCP. Our work revealed oligomerization as a critical mechanism shaping the NOC composition, particularly HMW species.

title: Performance of a bifacial photovoltaic thermal dryer integrated with PCM thermal energy storage
Evaluating working fluids and radial inflow turbine configurations for the design of efficient organic Rankine cycles in data center waste heat recovery
Knowledge and perceptions of climate change impacts on mental health in vulnerable populations in Africa: A scoping review
Rapid UAV-based detection of crane (Grus grus) mortality hotspots during an H5N1 avian influenza outbreak using deep learning
abstract: Rapid detection of wildlife mortality during infectious disease outbreaks is essential for ecological risk mitigation, zoonotic-risk management, and timely intervention, yet field surveys are often slow, labor-intensive, and spatially limited. This study evaluates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery combined with deep learning as an operational surveillance tool for mapping live and deceased Common Cranes ( Grus grus ) during a highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1) outbreak in the Hula Valley, Israel. High-resolution RGB imagery was collected over aquatic roosting and terrestrial feeding habitats and annotated to distinguish living and dead individuals. A YOLOv8-based detection framework was tested using habitat-specific training, combined multi-habitat training, and transfer learning from a large avian dataset, together with selective data augmentation, sliding-window inference, and Weighted Boxes Fusion. Living cranes were detected reliably across habitats, with AP@50 reaching 0.89 in mosaicked feeding-area imagery and 0.98 in raw feeding-area imagery. Dead cranes were detected accurately in water bodies (AP@50 ≈ 0.90), but detection in terrestrial feeding areas remained more limited (AP@50 ≈ 0.64–0.70), based on aerial annotations without in situ confirmation. Oversampling, undersampling, and focal loss provided limited improvement, suggesting that class imbalance alone does not fully explain the lower terrestrial detection performance, and that carcass scarcity, limited visual diversity, and ambiguity against heterogeneous ground backgrounds may also contribute. Joint multi-habitat training and transfer learning improved generalization for the rare dead-crane class on land. These findings demonstrate the value of UAV-based deep learning for rapid mortality assessment and hotspot identification during wildlife disease outbreaks.

title: Prediction of arsenic, cadmium, and lead bioaccessibility for regional-scale management of legacy-contaminated soils
abstract: Urban and peri-industrial soils contaminated by past urban and industrial activities frequently exhibit elevated contents in potentially toxic elements (PTEs) such as arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), and lead (Pb) that exceed regulatory thresholds. Accurate characterization of this contamination is essential for effective risk management of exposed populations. In this context, assessing oral bioaccessibility is a critical step for reliably evaluating exposure risks via the ingestion of soil particles and preventing the overestimation of human health hazards often caused by relying solely on total element contents. However, large-scale bioaccessibility assessments remain scarce, as most studies rely either on total contents or small, site-specific datasets, limiting the development of regionally applicable risk assessment frameworks. This study quantifies the oral bioaccessibility of As, Cd, and Pb at the regional scale, based on aqua regia contents and Unified BARGE Method (UBM) measurements for 223 topsoil samples collected across major historical industrial basins in Wallonia (Belgium). Chemical fractionation (BCR protocol) and soil properties were used to identify the main controls on PTEs bioaccessibility. The results show that while As is mainly controlled by the geogenic background, Cd and Pb are predominantly of anthropogenic origin, frequently exceeding regulatory thresholds. We further demonstrate that actual exposure risks are heavily modulated by chemical speciation: on average, only 24% of total (aqua regia content) As is bioaccessible, compared to substantially higher fractions for Cd (82%) and Pb (57%), which are primarily associated with reducible Fe/Mn oxyhydroxide phases. Bioaccessible contents can be predicted from total (aqua regia) element contents ( R 2 = 0.47–0.98), increasing to R 2 = 0.83–0.95 for As when the cumulative BCR content after Step 3 is included. Based on a large, consolidated dataset covering seven industrial areas, this approach enables the integration of regionally derived bioaccessibility values into human health risk models, while supporting the development of site-specific tools, including predictive models based on routine soil data and spatial mapping for land managers. The proposed framework is transferable to similar contaminated environments worldwide, contributing to reduced uncertainty in regional-scale risk assessments and guiding evidence-based soil management strategies.

title: An indoor daylighting-heating terminal incorporating side-emitting optical fibers and phase change materials: Experimental assessment of daylighting and thermal performance
Energy consumption and loss mechanisms in electrified tractor powertrains: A system-level evaluation based on a field-validated diesel tractor model
abstract: This study presents a system-level evaluation of onboard energy consumption and loss mechanisms in electrified tractor powertrains under representative agricultural workloads. A baseline diesel tractor model was developed and validated using field-measured moldboard-plowing data, reproducing the principal vehicle-level responses with NRMSE and MAPE values below 5%. Using the field-validated baseline, a series hybrid electric tractor (Ser HEV), fuel cell electric tractor (FCV), and battery electric tractor (BEV) were comparatively evaluated under a tillage duty cycle. Relative to the conventional diesel tractor, the FCV reduced onboard energy consumption by approximately 31–54%, while the BEV configurations achieved reductions of approximately 62–75%, depending on workload and battery capacity. The Ser HEV reduced energy consumption under light and medium workloads but showed an 11.1% increase under the high-load condition because of additional energy-conversion stages. Energy-distribution analysis showed that electrification substantially reduces power-source losses while increasing the relative importance of drivetrain- and wheel-to-drawbar losses. Within the adopted comparative model, increasing battery capacity for extended BEV operation increased vehicle mass and was associated with greater modeled wheel-to-drawbar loss, resulting in higher onboard energy demand for the long-range BEV than for the short-range configuration. These results demonstrate that tractor electrification should be evaluated at the system level by considering energy-conversion pathways, energy-management strategy, onboard energy capacity, and vehicle mass together.

title: Two-stage capacity and operational optimization of integrated PV-storage-EV charging systems under uncertainty
Modeling and experimental validation of helium-based thermal management system with transcritical heat sink for hydrogen-fueled aero engines
abstract: Liquid hydrogen (LH 2 ) fuel offers a pathway toward decarbonizing aviation but introduces thermal management challenges arising from its cryogenic and chemically reactive nature. Intermediate cycle heat exchange (ICHE) systems employing a chemically inert intermediate fluid to decouple the cryogenic fuel from high-temperature air have emerged as a promising architecture. However, as the cryogenic working fluid traverses the pseudo-critical region, drastic thermophysical property variations propagate through the intermediate loop, producing a coupled nonlinear response that conventional analyses cannot capture. Existing transfer matrix-based formulations remain restricted to the constant-property regime, and experimental data on cryogenic ICHE configurations are scarce. Here, a helium-based ICHE system with transcritical heat sink is investigated through coupled modeling and experiment. A HEX segmental transfer matrix model is developed within a system-level analytical framework, recasting the nonlinear heat transfer under drastic property variation into a 2×2 coefficient transfer matrix. The model is validated on a cryogenic ICHE platform employing liquid nitrogen as a surrogate for LH 2 , with the predicted printed circuit heat exchanger (PCHE) heat transfer rate deviating from experimental data by only 1.46% and 87.1% of system-level predictions falling within the ±15% deviation band. Parametric analysis reveals that heat-source and cold-source boundary adjustments produce a global synchronous variation of the system temperature field, while the intermediate fluid mass flow rate serves as an independent means for redistributing thermal load between series-connected components. The framework provides a system-level modeling and design basis for thermal management of hydrogen-fueled aero engines.

title: Multi-objective optimization of a centrifugal pump based on non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm Ⅲ and the coupling characteristics of pressure fluctuation-entropy production rate
National Wage Contracts, Monopsony, and Welfare in a North-South Economy,
abstract: Abstract In countries characterized by significant geographical disparities in productivity, nationwide labour contracts may cause local unemployment by preventing the adjustments that would occur in a competitive labour market. Here we argue, however, that when there are mobility frictions and monopsony power, nationwide contracts may still be preferable to local contracts. Using a spatial general equilibrium model calibrated on the Italian North-South divide, we suggest that nationwide wage contracts may still lead to narrower regional welfare gaps if monopsony power is sufficiently strong in low-productivity areas.
journal_name: Journal of the European Economic Association

title: The Immigration Surplus Revisited
abstract: Abstract We extend the immigration surplus results of Borjas (1995). In a closed competitive constant-returns economy, we show that an influx of migrants (holding their skill mix fixed) must increase the total real income of natives, for any number of factor inputs, any pattern of substitutability or complementarity between them, and any number of intermediate or final goods – with larger gains if natives and migrants differ more in skill mix. If natives supply labour elastically across skill types, their welfare gains are diminished, even if they respond by moving to higher-paying jobs. We illustrate our results using a US calibration.

title: Investors' ideology and corporate symbolic and substantive climate actions
abstract: Abstract Research Summary Prior research suggests that institutional investors' liberalism is associated with firms' engagement in environmental sustainability, yet whether this association manifests in symbolic or substantive actions remains unclear. Taking a question‐driven approach, our analyses of Russell 3000 firms (2010–2020) reveal that investor liberalism, measured as the proportion of donations made to the Democratic Party, is positively associated with symbolic climate actions only from 2016 onward (a period when political polarization intensified), reversing a negative association during 2010–2015. Its positive association with substantive actions from 2016 onward, however, appears only among consistent Democratic donors (stronger liberal values), among dedicated investors, or in firms without CEO duality (greater investor influence). These findings indicate that liberal investor ownership may encourage, rather than deter, firms' environmental decoupling. Managerial Summary Liberal institutional investors tend to favor greater corporate environmental sustainability efforts, but are they associated with firms' symbolic or substantive climate actions? Our findings based on U.S. firms reveal that across the full 2010–2020 period, firms with more liberal investors, as indicated by their Democratic‐leaning political donations, do not exhibit more symbolic or substantive climate actions. From 2016 onward, as political polarization intensified, firms with more liberal investors exhibited more symbolic climate actions but not substantive ones. During this period, only investors with stronger liberal commitment (i.e., consistent Democratic donors) are associated with more substantive actions. Democratic‐donating investors are also associated with more substantive actions when they are dedicated investors or when firm CEOs do not chair their boards.

title: The Media Freedom Paradox: A Global Study of Corporate Greenwashing
abstract: ABSTRACT Media freedom is widely regarded as a disciplining force that constrains corporate misconduct. We challenge this view in the environmental domain by developing the concept of the media freedom paradox . While a free media environment may deter greenwashing by raising the expected costs of exposure ( the watchdog effect ), it simultaneously amplifies normative pressures on firms to appear environmentally responsible, incentivizing symbolic disclosure over substantive action ( the symbolic compliance effect ). Using a sample of 3956 publicly listed firms across 46 countries over 2015–2025, we show that higher media freedom is associated with significantly higher levels of corporate greenwashing, supporting the symbolic compliance effect . This counterintuitive finding reflects the fact that media freedom intensifies normative pressure on firms to appear responsible faster than it improves the verifiability of their claims. This effect is amplified where environmental regulation is weak and where media markets are more privatized. A free press appears as a necessary but insufficient condition for credible environmental governance.

title: From Stakeholder Pressure to Public Value: The Role of Non‐Financial Reporting in the Waste Management Sector
abstract: ABSTRACT The research investigates the creation and destruction of public value in the Italian waste management sector through stakeholder engagement and the quality of nonfinancial reporting (NFR). Drawing on stakeholder theory and public service logic, public value is conceptualized as the result of dynamic relational processes, where stakeholder salience mediates the impact of external pressure on organizational priorities. A structural model is developed and empirically tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) on a sample of 69 Italian waste management firms disclosing nonfinancial information. The analysis shows that stakeholder pressure (especially from customers and governments) affects the quality and inclusiveness of NFR. High‐quality NFR enhances stakeholder salience by absorbing environmental and social claims into governance and reporting practices, promoting a more responsive and accountable service delivery. Public value is measured by using a hybrid set of indicators combining financial performance (ROI and ROE) with socio‐environmental outcomes (e.g., recycling rates and waste reduction). The findings highlight the strategic importance of participatory, materiality‐driven reporting in fostering public value creation.

title: Organizational centralization of accounting functions and forward-looking disclosure quality: evidence from financial shared service centers
abstract: This paper examines how the organizational centralization of accounting functions, an underexplored element of firms' reporting infrastructure, relates to the quality of forward-looking disclosures. Using novel hand-collected data on financial shared service center (FSSC) adoption among Chinese A-share listed firms, we document a robust and positive association between FSSC adoption and the accuracy of management earnings forecasts. These forecasts are also more specific, and capital markets react more strongly to them. Further analyses show that FSSC adoption is associated with shorter audit report lags and fewer subsequent financial restatements. The association between FSSC adoption and forecast accuracy is also stronger among firms with greater internal information frictions. These findings are consistent with the view that FSSCs improve managers' access to timely and reliable accounting information, thereby supporting more accurate forecasts. We also find that FSSC effectiveness is stronger among firms with greater digital capabilities and a stronger culture of unity, as well as among more mature FSSCs and those operating under multi-center structures. Our findings add to the literature on reporting infrastructure and disclosure quality and offer insights for firms and policymakers considering FSSC adoption as part of digital transformation strategies.
journal_name: Journal of Accounting and Public Policy

title: Expense disclosures and the social meaning of charitable donations
abstract: Purpose This study examines how donors use expense disclosures when evaluating charities. Design/methodology/approach We conducted 35 interviews with individual donors using a vignette-based method, combining Zelizer's (2012, 1997) theory of the social meaning of money with Kolhede and Gomez-Arias’ (2022) donor typology of “impressionable”, “intrinsic” and “sceptic” donors. Findings Donors interpret expense disclosures through relational and moral frameworks rather than purely technical or economic ones. Impressionable donors treat expense information primarily as a trust signal, relying more on social cues and reputation. Intrinsic donors use ethical, mission-focused reasoning, valuing explanations of how spending benefits beneficiaries. Sceptic donors engage analytically, using disclosures to judge integrity, efficiency and legitimacy. Impressionable, intrinsic and sceptic donors focused not only on how much was spent, but on whether expenditure was perceived to meaningfully contribute to the charities’ mission and outcomes. Research limitations/implications Our findings suggest that donor behaviour cannot be fully understood through economic models alone and call for greater attention to the social and ethical dimensions of financial information. We also highlight the limitations of standard expense classifications and the need for more contextualised disclosures. Practical implications Charities should provide expense disclosures that are layered and inclusive, combining numerical clarity, contextual explanation and value-based narratives to address differing information needs. Doing so can help build trust, avoid the nonprofit starvation cycle, and foster stronger, more sustainable donor relationships. Originality/value We reconceptualise expense disclosures as part of relational work, showing that donors assign moral and symbolic meaning to financial data, challenging assumptions of purely rational donor behaviour.

title: Social Safety Nets and Corporate Tax Avoidance: Evidence From Paid Family Leave Programs
abstract: ABSTRACT Social safety nets are essential to a resilient and adaptive economic system. This study examines their influence on corporate tax avoidance using the staggered implementation of U.S. state‐level paid family leave (PFL) programs, social safety net policies designed to enhance employees' work‐life balance, as a quasi‐natural experiment. We find a statistically and economically significant decline in corporate tax avoidance following PFL adoption. The results hold across various robustness tests. A structural equation model shows that the effect is mediated by decreases in employee turnover and improvements in employee productivity. The effect is stronger among firms facing greater financing frictions and among labor‐intensive firms. Overall, this study identifies a reduction in corporate tax avoidance as an unintended consequence of social safety nets.

title: Consumerism in The Digital Age: A Philosophical Reflection on Online Buying Practices in Chennai
abstract: With the rapid growth of e-commerce, understanding the key factors shaping online consumer buying behaviour is essential for businesses and marketers. This study investigates the influence of five critical factors—website usability, security concerns, trust, convenience—on consumer decision- making in online shopping. It examines how a seamless and user-friendly website enhances engagement, while security concerns and trust significantly impact purchasing confidence. Moreover, convenience and competitive pricing play a crucial role in shaping buying preferences. By analysing consumer perceptions and behaviours, this research offers valuable insights to enhance online shopping experiences and develop effective marketing strategies. The findings aim to help businesses optimize their digital platforms, fostering greater customer satisfaction and long- term loyalty.
journal_name: Structural Equation Modeling A Multidisciplinary Journal

title: Subjective cognitive decline and objective cognitive performance across diverse intersectional identities by gender, race/ethnicity, and educational attainment
abstract: Abstract Subjective cognitive decline and subtle objective cognitive impairment are important early clinical stages of dementia, but the extent to which they vary across intersectional identities remains poorly understood. We examined differences in subjective and objective cognition across intersectional identities defined by gender, race/ethnicity, and education. We analyzed 20,814 participants aged 45+ from the Brain Health Registry. Subjective cognition was measured using the 39-item Everyday Cognition Scale. Objective cognition was measured using the Cambridge Cognition Paired Associates Learning test. We defined 24 intersectional strata based on gender (men, women), race/ethnicity (Latino, Asian, Black, White), and education (≤associate’s, bachelor’s, graduate degree). Using Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA), we estimated age-adjusted linear mixed models then additionally adjusted for the additive effects of gender, race/ethnicity, and education to evaluate whether random effects of the intersectional identity strata explained variance beyond individual fixed effects. Between-stratum variance accounted for ≤6% of the total variance in subjective and objective cognition. Most (79-98%) of this between-stratum variance was explained by additive effects of gender, race/ethnicity, and education. Additive sociodemographic effects explained most disparities in mid- to late-life subjective and objective cognition across intersectional strata, with limited residual intersectional heterogeneity beyond these additive effects.

title: “Something was happening, and on the other hand, it wasn't”: Relational knowledge formation in intrafamilial child sexual abuse
Mandatory reporting of child sexual exploitation online: A qualitative study of school staff perspectives in Hong Kong
A cooperative framework for building cluster, charging cluster, and microgrid park with coordinated sharing of energy, carbon allowances, and green electricity certificates
Energy service companies as transition intermediaries: Functions, business models, and prospects for demand-side decarbonization
Atmospheric Concentrations and Emissions of Major HFCs at Six Background Stations in China during 2012–2023
abstract: Abstract In this study, a long-term atmospheric observation of HFC-23, -32, -125, -134a, -143a, and -152a was conducted at six background stations across China from 2011 to 2023. Using a tracer ratio method with HCFC-22 as the reference, emissions from four main economic regions, Northeast Plain (NEP), North China Plain (NCP), Yangtze River Delta (YRD), and Central South China (CSC), were estimated, and their trends were analyzed over four phases: Phase 1 (2012–2016), Phase 2 (2017–2018), Phase 3 (2019–2020), and Phase 4 (2021–2023). The results show that from 2011 to 2023, the atmospheric mixing ratios of all studied HFCs except HFC-152a exhibited increasing trends. Nationally, emissions of HFC-23 show a decreasing tendency during Phase 4, while emissions of HFC-32, -125, -134a, and -143a continued to rise throughout Phases 3 and 4. These four HFCs were identified as the dominant species, accounting for over 76% of total HFCs’ mass emissions. From Phase 3 to Phase 4, CO2-equivalent HFC emissions per capita increased slightly, whereas emissions per unit GDP decreased, which is mainly attributable to significant HFC reductions in the CSC region. Nevertheless, China’s average HFC emission intensities (whether calculated per unit GDP or per capita) remain approximately 1.5–1.6 times the global average.

title: Parenteral Nutrition as a Source of Xenobiotic Exposure in Preterm Infants in a Single-Center Case Study
abstract: Abstract In premature infants, successful ex utero maturation depends on endogenous and exogenous stimuli. Chemical insults during this period may impact long-term development. Given immature hepatic biotransformation, parenteral xenobiotic exposure may be of particular toxicological relevance. We conducted a single-center case study to characterize the xenobiotic burden of neonatal parenteral nutrition (PN). A standardized PN regimen for a 28-week, 1000 g reference infant was passed through infusion lines and the flow-through analyzed via a multianalyte exposome LC-MS/MS assay. Eighteen of 221 targeted xenobiotics were detected. Diisononyl phthalate (DINP, 780 ng/mL), bisphenol A (BPA, 250 ng/mL), methylparaben (MP, 74 ng/mL), and 5-hydroxymethyl-2-furanoic acid (HMFA, 43 ng/mL) showed the highest mean concentrations. The estimated daily intake of BPA (9.5 μg/kg bw/d) exceeded calculated and official Health-Based Guidance Values. Consistent with immature detoxification, pharmacokinetic modeling suggested accumulation of DINP, MINP, and free BPA in premature infants. The higher predicted exposure of premature infants to free BPA warrants investigation into 4-methyl-2,4-bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)pent-1-ene (MBP) formation under potentially saturated Phase II metabolism. An exploratory analysis of plasma data from extremely premature infants indicated PN as a contributory rather than predominant source of intervention-related exposure. These findings represent a relevant clinical reference scenario rather than a population-wide exposure estimate.

title: Fine-scale mapping and nonlinear attribution of heavy metal(loid)s in urban soils using spatially enhanced machine learning algorithms
abstract: Sparse sampling and spatial heterogeneity constrain the prediction of heavy metal(loid)s in urban soils. Using 77 composite surface-soil samples from Hangzhou, China, we compared Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR) for eight elements under three predictor schemes: environmental variables (ENV), ENV with local spatial lags (ENV + SL), and ENV + SL with interpolation-derived predictors (ENV + SL + SP). Standalone interpolation and ENV-based regression kriging provided additional comparisons. Selected models achieved pooled out-of-fold R 2 values of 0.322–0.555, with the lowest value for Cd and the highest for Pb. XGBoost performed best for six elements, whereas SVR performed best for Mn and Pb. ENV + SL + SP was selected for seven elements, while Pb was best predicted by ENV-only SVR. The best ENV + SL + SP models exceeded the stronger ordinary kriging or inverse distance weighting baseline by 0.040–0.343 in R 2 . Residual kriging improved ENV-only predictions in 15 of 24 comparisons. ENV-only SHAP analysis identified element-specific associations with soil properties, vegetation, precipitation, and road proximity. Predictions were generated for 82,782 grid cells at 250 m resolution. Conditional residual-bootstrap ranges for background-exceedance area were approximately 79–85% for As, 83–91% for Cd, 52–62% for Cu, and 43–54% for Zn. Based on out-of-fold exceedance detection, maps for As, Cu, and Zn may help prioritize confirmatory sampling, whereas those for Cd, Cr, Mn, Ni, and Pb should primarily support preliminary screening. Independent field validation remains necessary, and low predicted concentrations cannot exclude localized hotspots.

title: Precipitation buffers gully erosion through vegetation cover across the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Gully erosion is important trace left by soil erosion, and its density characteristics are regarded as a significant indicator of land degradation. The Tibetan Plateau, with little human influence, is an ideal site for studying the natural development of gullies. In this study, three indicators, namely gully number density (GND), gully length density (GLD) and gully area density (GAD), were used to investigate the spatial pattern of gully erosion on the Tibetan Plateau. The optimized XGboost algorithm and spatialized SHapley Additive exPlanations were employed to model three gully densities, and identifies the significance of driving factors along with the response relationships of gully density to these factors. The results reveal that arid regions in the northern Tibetan Plateau are high-value areas for gully density. Mean annual precipitation (MAP) dominates the gully density spatial pattern, followed by elevation and slope steepness. The two indicators of the cryosphere, namely, the permafrost thermal stability and the snow cover days, had the least impact on gully density. This indicates that gully erosion is dominated by precipitation rather than freeze-thaw. The inhibitory effect of MAP on gully erosion was observed, mainly through its role in promoting vegetation growth. Additionally, this study identified two key MAP thresholds of 150 mm and 400 mm, which play an important role in gully density. Specifically, in arid regions with MAP below 150 mm and in semi-humid to humid regions with MAP exceeding 400 mm, MAP emerges as the dominant factor. In contrast, within semi-arid areas (150 mm < MAP < 400 mm), the dominant influencing factors are more complex. Through quantitative assessment, this study reveals that gully erosion on the Tibetan Plateau is mainly driven by precipitation rather than freeze-thaw. Moreover, at a regional scale, precipitation suppresses gully erosion by promoting vegetation cover, rather than promotes gully erosion. These findings offer new insights for the gully erosion mechanism, provide an important perspective for research on the dominant drivers of soil erosion, and deliver guidance for soil and water conservation efforts on the Tibetan Plateau.

title: Tillage practices affect the synergetic relationship between soil organic carbon and crop yield under straw return
abstract: Straw returning is a pivotal strategy to enhance soil organic carbon (SOC) concentration and crop yield. However, the synergy between these two outcomes and its spatial variability under different tillage practices remain poorly quantified. Therefore, we conducted a meta-analysis using 1767 paired observations from 222 studies in China, including 726 SOC comparisons and 1041 yield comparisons, with 428 observations contributing to both analyses. Observations with complete baseline soil data were then combined with harmonized gridded spatial predictors to generate scenario-based adaptation maps. Our findings demonstrate that straw return significantly increased SOC concentration by 10.66% and crop yield by 7.96% compared to straw removal, with a significant positive correlation between the two responses. The strength of this synergy, however, was strongly modulated by crop type and tillage practice, and differed between topsoil and subsoil layers. Notably, subsoiling (SS) and no-till (NT) more frequently produced simultaneous benefits for both SOC and yield, whereas conventional tillage (CT) and rotary tillage (RT) showed greater variability. However, these estimates carry uncertainty due to uneven observational coverage for certain crops and the inherent limitations of grid-based environmental data. Our findings suggest that strategic combinations of straw return with appropriate tillage and crop selection can effectively reconcile SOC concentration with productivity goals. We conclude that region-specific adaptation is essential for sustainable agricultural management under straw return.

title: Gas-solid migration and stabilization of sulfur during thermal treatment of sulfur-rich coal gangue: A multi-waste management strategy
abstract: Sulfur-rich coal gangue can release sulfur-containing gases during thermal utilization and mine backfilling; however, the coupling relationship between sulfur transformation and the evolution of Fe-bearing minerals remains poorly understood. In this study, ion chromatography, thermogravimetric analysis, X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and gas analysis were systematically integrated to elucidate sulfur migration behavior during thermal treatment and to evaluate waste-derived sulfur-fixing agents prepared from steel slag and shell powder through water and alkali activation. The results revealed that sulfur occurred predominantly in pyrite and underwent a stepwise transformation of S 2 2− → S n 2− (n > 2)/S 0 → S(VI), mainly as SO 4 2− , accompanied by the oxidation of iron from Fe(II)-S to Fe(II)-O and Fe(III)-O. SO 2 release was most pronounced at approximately 500 °C, identifying the critical temperature range for sulfur-emission control. The alkali-activated agent maintained an SO 2 inhibition efficiency above 96.67% at 300-500 °C and increased sulfur retention from 41% to 70% compared with the water-activated agent. Although alkali activation did not substantially alter the CaCO 3 -dominated crystalline composition, it promoted reactive sulfur capture and sulfate formation in the solid residue. This study establishes a coupled Fe–S transformation mechanism and demonstrates a sustainable waste-derived approach for converting gaseous sulfur emissions into stable solid phases, providing new insights into the mitigation of sulfur-related environmental risks during sulfur-rich coal gangue utilization.

title: Optimizing dryland ecological restoration: Unveiling the lagged and nonlinear threshold effects on carbon-water compound use efficiency
abstract: Ecological restoration regulates carbon water processes in arid and semi-arid ecosystems, yet its lagged and threshold effects remain unclear. Using multi-source remote sensing data from 2000 to 2022, we identified forest restoration regions, shrubland–grassland restoration regions, and gradual vegetation restoration regions ( VRRs ) in the Ningxia–Inner Mongolia Reach of the Yellow River and quantified their lagged effects on carbon use efficiency ( CUE ), water use efficiency ( WUE) , and carbon-water compound use efficiency ( COM) using distributed lag nonlinear models. VRRs dominated restoration, with restoration occurring earlier in the semi-arid area. CUE showed a dominant response at lag 5, whereas WUE and COM showed lagged responses at lag 3–5 in the arid area but immediate responses in the semi-arid area. Restoration thresholds varied by climate. In the arid area, SGRRs and VRRs had a safe restoration range of 23%–48% for annual newly added restoration proportion at the 1-km grid-cell scale, while negative WUE and COM responses emerged when restoration exceeded approximately 60%, associated with lag 3–5 effects. In the semi-arid area, restoration could exceed 60% without adverse effects. FRRs showed a low threshold of 10%–15%, SGRRs an optimal threshold of approximately 52%, and VRRs a higher threshold of 49%–61%. These findings provide a basis for climate-specific ecological restoration that maximizes long-term carbon–water synergies.

title: Revealing the spatial heterogeneity of pine wilt disease spread in China through Geographical Pattern Causality analysis
Government-commissioned industrial wastewater governance: A tripartite evolutionary game of local governments, third-party pollution control enterprises, and non-state-owned polluting enterprises
abstract: In China's government-commissioned industrial-park and public industrial-wastewater projects, local government (LG) purchases third-party pollution control enterprises (TPPCEs), while non-state-owned polluting enterprises (NSOPEs) provide operational cooperation. However, treatment providers may reduce effort after receiving payment, and NSOPEs may refuse cooperation when participation costs exceed expected benefits. To examine these interconnected problems, this study develops a tripartite evolutionary game involving LG, TPPCEs, and NSOPEs. The model distinguishes fixed contract payments from performance-based rewards and breach penalties and incorporates cost sharing when NSOPEs refuse cooperation while compliant treatment continues. Local stability analysis and numerical simulations across five scenarios reveal three findings. First, unconditional fixed payments do not change TPPCEs' relative incentives to comply, whereas performance rewards and breach penalties strengthen compliance incentives under LG's active governance. Second, TPPCEs' compliance and NSOPEs' participation depend on distinct payoff thresholds. Third, breach penalties and cost sharing complement each other when both compliance and participation incentives are insufficient. Together, they can support stable joint governance when LG monitoring incentives are also adequate. These findings clarify how contractual incentives and participation conditions jointly determine cooperation and provide a basis for targeting the specific constraints preventing stable wastewater governance.

title: A blessing or a curse? The impact of artificial intelligence innovation on corporate energy efficiency
abstract: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) innovation influences corporate energy efficiency and the underlying mechanisms. We develop a general equilibrium model incorporating energy input and endogenous AI technology to explain how AI innovation improves energy efficiency through production process optimization. Using a deep-learning-based text identification, we develop a firm-level measure of AI innovation for Chinese listed companies over the period 2008–2022. Our empirical results show that AI innovation significantly improves corporate energy efficiency, while the mechanism analysis provides evidence consistent with production process optimization as an important transmission channel. This positive effect is stronger among firms operating in key technological sectors and capital-intensive industries. Further, we find that disruptive AI innovation produces a larger effect than general AI innovation. We also document that local governments' attention to AI development and intra-firm data sharing strengthen the energy-efficiency gains associated with AI innovation. This study contributes to research on digital innovation and firm sustainability by showing how AI-driven innovation translates into efficiency-enhancing outcomes through organizational and data-governance mechanisms.
