Are salaries getting worse? Many scientists think so
The Selfish Gene, 50 years on — it’s time for an update
Price Gouging and the Monopoly Option
abstract: Abstract We investigate a dynamic oligopoly model with two phases: a normal phase where an essential input is available, and a disruption phase where firms must rely on inventories. Disruptions create an overcutting pricing incentive arising from the option to forgo sales and monopolize the market once rivals stock out. This monopoly option causes the price to jump to a supracompetitive level at the advent of the disruption and to remain above the competitive price path throughout. Price caps raise welfare, but reduce inventory investment. Government reserves reduce prices and raise buffer stocks, as do reserve mandates when financially feasible.

title: The effect of prime brokers’ balance sheet constraints on hedge fund performance: Evidence from the GSIB surcharge
Bismarck’s Welfare State and the Socialists
Failures of contingent reasoning in screening decisions
abstract: Abstract Screening decisions—choosing a costly action that reveals information about an unknown quality—can be crucial in various situations, such as hiring workers or designing policies. Choosing whether to screen can be difficult because it requires recognizing and trading off the benefits of information with the costs of getting it. We investigate whether people recognize when the benefits of screening dominate its costs and what causes them to choose otherwise. Our online experiment simulates a hiring scenario with an initial trial task. Participants can first reveal candidates’ quality at a small cost and then choose which candidate to hire. Most participants choose the dominated task that does not reveal the candidates’ quality, and this mistake persists even with experience and feedback. We show that this insufficient screening is driven by failures to anticipate inference and plan the full strategy.

title: Speaking With One Voice: Shareholder Collaboration on Activism
abstract: Abstract I study how an activist shareholder organizes a cost-sharing coalition with active shareholders while seeking support from passive shareholders outside the coalition. A larger coalition shifts more of the campaign cost to members, allowing the activist to pursue lower-value proposals. Observing a larger coalition therefore lowers passive shareholders’ posterior expectation of proposal value. The activist chooses the largest coalition that preserves support from pivotal passive shareholders, endogenizing coalition size. Consequently, coalition size need not be a monotone measure of activist influence, and activism frequency depends on passive shareholders’ preferences. Coalition building strengthens the proxy-fight threat and can increase prevote settlements. (JEL G34, G23, D83)

title: Fixing the cryptofinance conundrum: the politics of crypto-assets regulation in the EU
Pricing Geopolitical Risk: Closed-Form Valuation of Futures and Options on the GPR Index
abstract: On July 31, 2026, the European Central Bank (ECB) published the results of its thematic reverse stress test on geopolitical risk, in which 110 directly supervised banks identified scenarios severe enough to deplete CET1 capital by 300 bps. The exercise delivered narratives but not probabilities: without a market price of geopolitical risk, it has no quantitative anchor. This article closes that gap by applying the Grünbichler–Longstaff (1996) square-root, mean-reverting state-variable model directly to the Caldara–Iacoviello Geopolitical Risk (GPR) index, yielding closed-form prices for GPR futures and European options. Exact maximum-likelihood estimation on the monthly series from 1985 to June 2026 delivers a mean-reversion half-life of about two months toward a long-run mean of approximately 104, with the Feller condition satisfied with substantial slack, so the non-central chi-square pricing structure applies without modification. Applied to the ECB exercise, the framework converts the supervisory threshold into a tail-probability statement. Under the physical measure, the 12-month exceedance probability is approximately 12%—the answer a historical-simulation stress test would report. Under the risk-neutral measure it lies between 29% and 79% across the range of the market price of geopolitical risk motivated by analogy to inflation-swap risk premia—a bandwidth that is wide precisely because no traded GPR instrument yet identifies this parameter. Because the modeling techniques are deliberately standard, the article’s contribution is the practical layer: specification tests grounding the process choice in the data, confidence intervals around the physical anchor, a sensitivity analysis over the loss-channel mapping, and an explicit model-risk map organized for supervisory validation. The wedge between the physical probability and the risk-neutral band is the geopolitical risk premium, and a single observed transaction price on a cash-settled GPR contract—exchange-listed in the VSTOXX/VIX mold or OTC in the inflation-swap mold—would collapse the bandwidth to a point.

title: “The Minimum Wage Is the Maximum Wage”: How Goal Replacement Perpetuates Means–Ends Decoupling
abstract: This research examines how organizations contribute to the perpetuation of means–ends decoupling (MED) within issue-based fields organized around societal problems, under conditions of heightened field scrutiny. In such settings, organizations often profess commitment to field goals and visibly comply with institutionally prescribed practices to satisfy monitoring, reporting, and public evaluation requirements. However, many adopted goals remain underachieved, raising questions about how compliance without progress endures and how claims of commitment remain credible under transparency regimes intended to spur substantive goal pursuit. Our data came from 75 interviews with 68 brands, suppliers, and third-party organizations pursuing worker well-being in global fashion supply chains. We unveil auditability-based goal replacement as an organizational-level mechanism through which actors rhetorically foreground compliance as public evidence of commitment while narrowing internal goal pursuit to auditable thresholds that serve their core goals, thereby allowing shortfalls to persist. Self-silencing about this substitution and the instrumentalizing of shortfalls close the configuration into a self-reinforcing loop. The study advances MED scholarship by (i) showing how organizations leverage field conditions and appropriate the existing scrutiny infrastructures to advance their core goals while reproducing the means–ends gap, (ii) problematizing the authenticity of commitment claims, and (iii) explaining how goal-ineffective compliance prevails as a credible substitute for adopted goals. It also extends research on organizational responses to institutional complexity and calls for greater attention to institutional impact—that is, the realized advancement of the societal aim an institution emerged to address.

title: Sustainability in marketing: A systematic analysis and future research agenda
journal_name: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science

title: Common ownership and consumer welfare
abstract: Abstract Rival firms with shared institutional investors (i.e., common owners) may compete less aggressively, potentially harming consumer welfare. Yet, research on common ownership has primarily focused on firm performance, often overlooking welfare outcomes or revealing contradictory results. This paper adopts a strategic network perspective to examine how common ownership affects firms’ service quality and pricing levels, which directly impact consumer welfare, and how customer and competitor factors that alter the focus of competitive strategy moderate these effects. To test the hypotheses, the authors analyze a rich, multi-market dataset of U.S. airline firms from 1995 to 2025. Findings reveal that competing firms with higher common ownership tend to have lower service quality and set higher prices. However, this effect is attenuated for firms with high customer-asset value and amplified among rivals competing across multiple markets. The findings demonstrate common ownership’s influence on firms’ marketing mix strategies and offer actionable insights for managers, policymakers, and investors.
journal_name: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science

title: The Equity Market Implications of the Retail Investment Boom
abstract: We quantify the equilibrium impact of retail traders on the U.S. equity market within a structural model of asset demand. Estimating investor-specific demand curves, we find that Robinhood traders are fundamentally distinct from all other investors, including other households: their demand is the most elastic and tilts most strongly toward volatile and microcap stocks. Each dollar invested through Robinhood generates more than five dollars in aggregate equity repricing, exceeding hedge funds, other households, and all other investor types. We decompose the cross-sectional variation in stock returns during Robinhood’s growth surge in 2020 into investor-specific components and find that shifts in Robinhood traders’ latent demand drove 11% of small-cap return volatility despite their negligible aggregate wealth share. To explain these demand shifts, we show that Robinhood traders are the only investor group whose latent demand is well explained by attention proxies: their demand exhibits a V-shaped response to past returns and rises sharply with trading volume. Our findings suggest that the growth of retail trading platforms represents a fundamental shift in the composition of equity demand with equilibrium consequences disproportionate to retail investors’ share of aggregate wealth. This paper was accepted by Lukas Schmid, finance. Funding: P. van der Beck acknowledges financial support from the Swiss National Science Foundation. Supplemental Material: The data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.04854 .

title: Corporate Pension Risk-Taking in a Low Interest Rate Environment
abstract: We examine how funding deficit pressures shape the risk-taking of U.S. corporate defined-benefit pension plans and how targeted regulatory relief can mitigate these incentives. Using the 2012 Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Act reform, which temporarily eased funding pressure by revising discount rate calculations, we show that plans receiving greater relief significantly reduced their equity allocations and shifted toward safer assets. This derisking was most pronounced among active plans and those sponsored by more financially constrained firms. Our findings demonstrate that targeted regulatory relief can curb risk-taking incentives even without altering underlying economic conditions or financial reporting standards and shed light on the likely (and unlikely) frictions driving such behavior. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. Funding: R. Pinto acknowledges financial support from the Lancaster University Management School Pump Prime Program. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02928 .

title: Qualitative Research in the Age of AI: Considerations, Critiques, and Craft
abstract: publishersversion

title: Thank You, Now What? How Donors Respond to Calls to Action
Testing a moderated mediated model through intellectual capital of smart circularity and brand loyalty in Saudi Arabia
Brave new cities? Governance configurations for sustainable city logistics
abstract: Purpose Despite extensive research and policy efforts, there is still no consensus over the aspects that must be influenced to mitigate the environmental and social impact of city logistics. Existing approaches have primarily focused on optimizing urban freight operations but have struggled to generate lasting and systemic improvements. Building on recent supply chain management (SCM) calls to conceptualize supply chains as socially embedded systems, this study aims to investigate why cities implementing broadly similar collaborative governance initiatives produce different sustainable city logistics outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative configurational analysis was conducted across twenty French city logistics initiatives. Drawing on Furnari et al.’s (2021) configurational theorizing toolkit, governance conditions were iteratively identified and combined to explain variation in sustainable city logistics outcomes. Findings The analysis identifies five governance configurations. Rather than depending on collaborative governance alone, high-impact outcomes emerge from the interaction among governance structure, stakeholder representation, structural commitment and intervention scale. Research limitations/implications The governance configurations identified are grounded in French city logistics initiatives and should be further strengthened through fieldwork, and then examined in other institutional contexts. Future research should investigate how governance configurations evolve over time and across different socially embedded supply chains. Practical implications Managers and public authorities should focus less on replicating individual governance practices and more on assembling governance configurations that combine broad stakeholder representation, collaborative decision-making, structural commitment and coordinated ecosystem-level interventions. Originality/value The study advances SCM research by reconceptualizing sustainable city logistics as a governance and coordination challenge embedded within socially embedded supply chains. By doing so, it further demonstrates how configurational theorizing explains wicked sustainability problems in SCM by shifting attention from isolated governance mechanisms toward governance configurations as the appropriate unit of analysis.
journal_name: Supply Chain Management: An International Journal

title: Color lightness as a sensory marketing cue: implications for guest decision-making
abstract: Purpose The comfort of sleep-related hotel amenities plays a critical role in shaping guests’ perceptions and booking intentions. Although prior research suggests that color lightness influences perceived comfort, existing studies have primarily focused on manufactured goods. Given the fundamental differences between goods and hospitality services, this study aims to examine how bedding color lightness influences hotel guests’ perceptions and behavioral intentions in the service context. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Accessibility-Diagnosticity Theory, this research uses one pretest and two experiments to examine the effects of bedding color lightness on perceived comfort, brand image and willingness to pay, as well as the underlying mechanism explaining the relationship between color lightness and willingness to pay. Findings Compared with light-colored bedding, dark-colored bedding significantly enhances perceived comfort, brand image and willingness to pay. Brand image and perceived comfort serially mediate the relationship between color lightness and willingness to pay. Research limitations/implications Color lightness serves as an accessible and diagnostic cue shaping consumer responses. The findings provide practical insights into how hotel businesses can leverage color lightness in bedding design and visual marketing communication to enhance guests’ perceptions and behavioral intentions. Originality/value Prior research in manufacturing contexts suggests a direct association between light colors and perceived comfort. However, this study shows that, in hospitality settings, darker colors can enhance perceived comfort, as experiential comfort is shaped through brand-level perceptions. Such critical insights highlight how the underlying mechanism of color lightness operates differently in service contexts, reflecting the unique characteristics of hospitality settings.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: When robots take the initiative: how robotic service proactivity shapes customer experience of hospitableness
abstract: Purpose Drawing on social response theory, this research aims to examine whether, how and when robotic service proactivity fosters customer experience of hospitableness. Design/methodology/approach A multistudy design consisting of three scenario-based experiments and one field validation survey was used to test the proposed conceptual model. Findings Customers reported a more intense experience of hospitableness when service robots displayed higher levels of proactivity. Automated social presence accounted for this effect, and the effect was amplified when robots possessed a more human-like appearance. Practical implications This research presents actionable insights for optimizing the coordinated management of robotic behaviors and appearances to enhance customer-robot interaction experiences. Originality/value This research extends research on service robots from static design to dynamic behavior, positioning robotic service proactivity as a key driver of customer experience of hospitableness. From the perspective of customer social responses, this study reveals automated social presence as the socio-emotional mechanism. It further establishes humanoid appearance as a moderating factor, demonstrating that proactive behavior yields greater benefits when robot form and behavior are aligned. These findings advance research on service robot form–behavior consistency and offer novel implications for robot design.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: How could fun activities motivate informal field-based learning?
abstract: Purpose As the motivational mechanisms through which workplace practices activate employees’ informal field-based learning (IFBL) remain underexplored, this study aims to address this gap by examining how fun activities (FA) influence IFBL in hotel contexts. Design/methodology/approach Three-wave survey data were collected from 424 frontline and backstage employees in Chinese hotels and analyzed through the AMOS and Macro PROCESS in SPSS. Findings The results showed that the interaction between FA and individual playfulness influenced IFBL through two distinct mediators: harmonious passion (HP) and obsessive passion (OP), depending on employees’ playfulness. FA activated HP only among employees with high playfulness, whereas among those with low playfulness, FA activated only OP. Practical implications Organizations should design FA that genuinely meet employees’ needs, thereby satisfying psychological needs such as autonomy and activating HP to promote IFBL. Importantly, employees should be given greater flexibility in choosing the form and frequency of their participation in FA according to their level of playfulness. Originality/value This research advances understanding of the organizational antecedents of IFBL and explores the motivational mechanisms that stimulate hotel employees’ IFBL by integrating organizational- and individual-level research on fun and play.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Can Academia Ethically Use Tools of Techno-Colonial Extraction? The “Problem” of GenAI
abstract: Debates on generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in qualitative research focus on methodological utility versus epistemological harm. We reframe the issue from conditions of use to conditions of production , arguing GenAI’s foundation in exploitative digital labor and geopolitical inequality presents a more fundamental ethical challenge for business and society scholars, who risk complicity in these extractive systems. We outline several pathways through which scholars and institutions can engage GenAI more responsibly.

title: From clearance to capital: regulatory timing, financing conditions, and observability limits in medical-device commercialization
abstract: Abstract An authorized medical device may still need outside capital before its sponsor, the firm responsible for it, can manufacture and launch it. The paper asks what public U.S. records can show about whether authorization timing relates to access to that capital, and what a credible test needs. It does not estimate a financing or commercialization effect. The data combine 52,910 successful authorizations for submissions received in 2008–2024, a monthly capital-market measure, and a prototype match of 510(k) applicant names to Form D notices of private securities offerings. Among submissions received through 2022, the longest tenth accounts for 49.4–57.4 percent of days above the pathway median. Receipt-to-decision durations include applicant-response periods and do not measure unexpected or agency-caused delay. The market measure takes similar values in neighboring months. Its nine high periods, runs of two or more high months, last two to nine months; its relevance to individual sponsors is untested. As an observability diagnostic, the Form D prototype shows how name linkage can mislead. Records in the longest-duration quartile less often have a notice within a year (2.1 versus 3.1 percent in the shortest). Their applicant names, however, also appear less often among issuers (8.7 versus 14.4 percent), and among records with a name found, the notice share is not lower. About 11 percent of outcome windows are incomplete, and amendments count as notices. The contribution is to document these measurement requirements and to specify a sponsor-level test with validated identities, decision-date forecasts at receipt, and dated capital events.

title: It is all about digitalization: investigating antecedents and effects of digital transformation
abstract: Abstract Digital transformation is increasingly recognized as a vital driver of competitiveness, yet the precise organizational factors that most strongly influence its success remain ambiguous. This study addresses this gap by examining how strategic, operational, organizational, and cultural factors jointly relate to digital transformation outcomes, and by uncovering the mediating role of innovation success in shaping overall company success. Drawing upon data from 279 organizational key informants in Germany with substantive involvement in digital transformation, this study develops a holistic framework that not only identifies key organizational factors relevant for digital transformation success but also compares their associations with transformation success when considered simultaneously. The findings reveal numerically larger associations for cultural and operational factors, whereas strategic and organizational factors exhibit smaller coefficients, with the organizational-domain association only marginally significant ( p < 0.10). Although bootstrap-based parameter-difference tests do not support a statistically established ranking of the four domains, the results underline the relevance of all four domains while suggesting that cultural and operational conditions may warrant particular attention depending on firms’ specific transformation context. Furthermore, the results reveal a significant indirect association between digital transformation success and company success through innovation success, accounting for around 60% of the total association in the specified model. Hence, organizations seeking to maximize the returns on their digital initiatives should consider cultural and operational conditions alongside the strategic and organizational foundations of digital transformation. Taken together, these insights offer actionable guidance for businesses aiming to allocate their resources strategically, consider cultural and operational conditions as important diagnostic starting points, and harness the full potential of digital transformation through a concerted emphasis on innovation.

title: Going green but seeing red: Tensions in initiating collective market shaping for sustainability
abstract: Empirical research on market shaping for environmental outcomes remains rare in business marketing research, and existing studies are largely biased towards successful cases while overlooking the challenging “front end” of collective market shaping. This study examines how actor-perceived tensions emanating from the business context influence efforts to initiate a collective market-shaping process for improved environmental outcomes. Drawing on a real-time qualitative case study of a European cruise shipbuilding network, we focus on the phase in which a shared market vision and coordinated action have yet to emerge. Our findings show that accumulated tensions hinder the microprocesses required for initiating collective market shaping. These tensions manifest as conflict, scattered activity and inactivity, delaying progress towards collective market shaping. Shifting attention from successful outcomes to early-stage tensions, this study contributes to market-shaping research by uncovering why collective market-shaping efforts for sustainability may fail to take shape in complex industrial networks.

title: How do monetary rewards impact free knowledge contribution? – business implication for Q&A platforms
How employees appropriate AI in the workplace: Effects of task characteristic and organizational culture
Who's ready for AI? The strategic leader–employee confidence divide and its economic and cultural contexts
Mindful consumption: how social media shapes fashion choices and brand pride
abstract: Purpose Fashion brands increasingly use social media to promote sustainability, but different social media marketing activities may not shape mindful consumption in the same way or have the same influence across cultural contexts. This study aims to examine how social media marketing activities (entertainment, electronic word-of-mouth, trendiness, interactivity and personalisation), consumer knowledge and environmental concern influence mindful consumption. It also examines the relationships between mindful consumption, sustainable consumption and brand pride, comparing consumers in the UK and Malaysia. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on attitude–behaviour–context theory, the study collected survey data from 468 fashion consumers (UK, n = 245; Malaysia, n = 223) and tested the proposed model using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Multi-group analysis was conducted to compare results between the two countries. Findings The results indicate that interactivity and personalisation significantly predicted mindful consumption among British consumers, but not among Malaysian consumers. Entertainment, electronic word-of-mouth and trendiness had no significant effect in either country. In contrast, environmental concern and consumer knowledge were significant predictors in both markets. Mindful consumption significantly predicted sustainable consumption in both countries, while sustainable consumption significantly predicted brand pride, with a stronger effect in Malaysia. Research limitations/implications This research extends the sustainable consumption literature by addressing the literature gap and responding to the call of a recent study to explore antecedents and consequences of mindful consumption of sustainable fashion. It also provides novel insights into how social media marketing, consumer knowledge and environmental concerns have different effects on mindful consumption among Malaysian and British consumers, which leads to improving brand pride. Practical implications This paper provides practical implications for fashion brands on the differences in using social media marketing to improve their connection with consumers through enhanced mindful consumption among Malaysian and British consumers. Originality/value The study provides actionable insights for fashion brands on which social media marketing activities shape mindful consumption across different markets, while highlighting the consistent importance of consumer knowledge and environmental concern in both the UK and Malaysia. It also shows that mindful consumption is linked not only to sustainable consumption but also to brand pride, extending understanding of its outcomes from sustainable behaviour to consumers’ emotional responses towards brands. This provides a broader understanding of the value of mindful consumption across different cultural settings.

title: Zero price or token price? The impact of bundle promotional format on promotional attractiveness and value discounting
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the relative attractiveness of freebie (e.g. “buy one, get one free”) and token-price (e.g. “buy one, get the second one for only 1¢”) promotions in the short run and value discounting effect for the separate items in the long run. Design/methodology/approach Two imaginary-scenario and two incentive-compatible experiments test the hypotheses. Findings Token-price promotions are more attractive than freebie promotions no matter if the supplemental item is identical to the focal item or not. Moreover, when the two items are identical, consumers who encounter a token-price (vs freebie) promotion express stronger value discounting for the focal item. This effect reverses when the items are nonidentical. Research limitations/implications Future research should examine whether the bundle promotional format effect differs with the amount of the token price and the complementarity of the focal and supplemental items. Practical implications Practitioners can draw on the findings to determine when to use freebie or token-price promotions and how to adjust bundle promotional strategies according to the type of the supplemental item. Originality/value This study improves understanding of the effects of freebie and token-price promotions, especially over the long-term. Based on mental accounting theory, the authors build a comprehensive framework that explains how the bundle promotional format influences promotional attractiveness and value discounting.

title: Talking or typing? How GenAI modality, product type, and multitasking shape recommendation response behaviour
abstract: Purpose This research aims to explore how generative AI (GenAI) recommendation modality (text vs voice) influences consumer recommendation adoption and how this effect further interacts with product type (search vs experience), processing fluency and multitasking to shape consumers’ behavioural responses to recommendations. Given that GenAI recommendation systems increasingly support interactive consumer decision-making, the authors examine modality as a key design feature shaping how GenAI-generated recommendations are delivered to consumers. Design/methodology/approach Across five studies, the authors examine how GenAI recommendation modality influences consumers’ recommendation adoption. The preliminary field study uses actual customer interactions in a natural commercial environment to establish the practical relevance of the phenomenon. Study 1 replicates the core modality effect in a controlled Chinese experiment. Study 2 examines the moderating role of product type. Studies 3 and 4 investigate processing fluency and multitasking as the underlying mechanism and boundary condition, using behavioural measures across all studies. Findings The findings demonstrate that GenAI recommendation modality affects consumers’ recommendation adoption, with text-based recommendations outperforming voice-based recommendations. The modality also interacts with product type and this effect is mediated by processing fluency: text-based recommendations elicit stronger behavioural responses for search products, whereas voice-based recommendations are more effective for experience products. Multitasking further moderates this pattern, favouring voice-based recommendations under high cognitive load across product types. Research limitations/implications The findings are based on controlled experimental settings and future work could examine additional contextual or individual-level moderators to enhance external validity. Practical implications Marketers should tailor GenAI recommendation modalities based on product type and anticipated multitasking environments. Text-based interactions are more suitable for detail-oriented search products, whereas voice-based interactions better suit experience products and multitasking contexts. Originality/value This research contributes to the GenAI literature by identifying recommendation modality as a critical yet understudied design feature of GenAI recommendation systems. The findings show that recommendation modality plays a central role in shaping consumer responses to GenAI-generated recommendations and extend processing fluency theory and task–technology fit by integrating product type and multitasking as key boundary conditions.

title: Mobile coupon-clicks inside vs outside a mall: implications for location-based targeting
abstract: Purpose This paper considers mobile coupons issued outside and inside a shopping mall with multiple stores. It aims to study the implications of coupon-click effects on optimal location-based mobile coupon targeting (LBMCT) strategy. Design/methodology/approach The study first empirically examines the effect of consumers’ coupon-click behaviors on purchases and find that coupon clicks made outside the mall are associated with a stronger purchase response than inside-mall clicks for experiential-product stores, a pattern consistent with a traffic-conversion mechanism overlooked in prior literature. Then the study builds a mathematical model to investigate whether, when and where to issue coupons for different types of stores. Findings The analytical results identify the conditions regarding two new decisions – whether a store should issue coupons, and if so, where to target the coupons. The study shows that cross-store traffic spillovers from outside-mall coupons can induce free-riding and coordination failure, such that stores may choose not to issue coupons even when mutual couponing would make them better off. Research limitations/implications Future research could examine whether the findings generalize to other geographic and cultural contexts, to settings with multiple stores or malls, and to competitive conditions that influence coupon effectiveness. Practical implications Marketers should evaluate LBMCT by considering not only direct sales conversion but also traffic spillovers across stores. Because outside-targeted coupons can benefit neighboring stores, mall managers should coordinate coupon programs or design incentives when spillovers are strong, thereby reducing free-riding and overcoming coordination failure. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first in the LBMCT literature that develops an empirical analysis motivated game model to investigate retail stores’ mobile coupon issuing and targeting strategies for inside and outside of a shopping mall, and considers two coupon effects and two product types.

title: Navigating scarcity: sustainable supply network archetypes for water stress
abstract: Purpose This study examines how firms configure sustainable supply networks (SNs) under water scarcity. It explains how water dependence shapes capability-configuration bundles and introduces transformational capability as the capacity to orchestrate capabilities for architecture-level redesign of SNs. Design/methodology/approach An abductive multiple-case study compares 13 multinational manufacturers across four sectors. Evidence from 23 interviews, site observations and secondary sources was analysed using Gioia-inspired coding and cross-case pattern matching. Findings Three contingent sustainable SN archetypes emerge: (1) “Stable”, (2) “Continuous Improvement”; and (3) “Progressive”. They differ in the scope of water dependence, the breadth of capabilities and the scope for reconfiguration. Static capabilities support routine monitoring and efficiency; dynamic capabilities renew existing processes and relationships; transformational capabilities orchestrate combinations of the five capability clusters to alter product and material choices, sourcing, governance, location, infrastructure or network structure. This is most evident in the “Progressive Sustainable SN” archetype. Research limitations/implications The qualitative study focuses on multinational manufacturers. Future research in other sectors, such as energy, should test the archetypes and transitions across smaller firms, services and other contexts of natural resource scarcity. Practical implications Managers can diagnose water dependence, distinguish incremental adaptation from transformational reconfiguration and align capability investments with changes across operations, sourcing, products, governance and network design. Social implications The developed framework can inform decisions on industrial location, catchment stewardship and shared water resilience. Originality/value The study advances a contingency-informed SN configuration perspective through a nested framework of sustainable SN archetypes. The archetypes are theorised as distinct configuration–capability combinations rather than as descriptive groupings of known adaptation practices. It establishes transformational capability as a distinct sustainable SN capability, rather than a synonym for dynamic capability, and explains when capabilities trigger architecture-level redesign under water scarcity.
journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

title: Lobbying Priorities in Agenda‐Setting: Agenda Breadth, Direction, and Responsiveness Across Economic and Citizen Groups
abstract: ABSTRACT Interest groups are key actors in shaping political agendas. Yet, we know surprisingly little about how they determine their lobbying priorities at the earliest stage of the policy process. This study advances a novel conceptual framework for studying interest groups' issue prioritization in the agenda setting stage along three complementary dimensions: agenda breadth, agenda direction, and agenda responsiveness. Drawing on original survey data from 630 EU level interest groups, our results show that issue prioritization is driven primarily by the type of constituents a group represents. Economic interest groups tend to pursue broader lobbying agendas, focus on defending the policy status quo, and are more responsive to internal member pressures when prioritizing undesired issues. Citizen groups, by contrast, typically adopt narrower agendas, prioritize challenging the status quo, and respond more strongly to external issue salience when determining their lobbying priorities. Overall, the study advances our understanding of how interest groups navigate competition for political attention and contributes to broader debates on agenda‐setting in contemporary democracies.

title: An Analytical Comparison of Latent Growth Curve, Cross-Lagged Panel, and Latent Difference Score Modeling for Longitudinal Mediation Analysis
abstract: Latent growth curve, cross-lagged panel, and latent difference score models are widely used for longitudinal data analysis. Relationships among those models have been analytically investigated in the extant literature for the univariate and bivariate contexts. However, mathematical connections among these models where three time-varying variables (i.e., input, mediator, outcome) are involved in longitudinal mediation analysis have not been previously studied. To fill in the research gap, we analytically derived the mathematical connections between latent growth curve mediation models and latent difference score mediation models (LDSMMs), as well as those between cross-lagged panel mediation models and LDSMMs for longitudinal mediation analysis. The equivalence relationships among the longitudinal mediation models provided new insights into the connections and interpretations of these models. We provided numerical examples using both simulated and real longitudinal data to illustrate the equivalence relationships, and shared the data and code online. Implications for longitudinal mediation modeling were discussed.
journal_name: Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal

title: Improving the Validity of Post-Selection Inference in Lasso-Regularized Structural Equation Modeling for Model Respecification
abstract: Regularization is increasingly used in structural equation modeling (SEM) to search for potential post hoc model modifications, yet the validity of statistical inference after selecting parameters/models via regularization has received limited attention. We propose selective discrepancy inference for lasso-regularized SEM, particularly when the lasso is used for model respecification. The framework views regularization not simply as selecting SEM parameters, but as selecting Jacobian-defined covariance-change directions along which a constrained model may fail to reproduce the covariance structure. The inferential target is therefore a selected covariance-discrepancy coefficient, which quantifies how much the misfit left by the constrained model is explained by the selected modification direction after accounting for other selected directions and baseline parameter readjustment. A simulation study shows that the resulting confidence intervals achieve target coverage rates. An empirical example regarding measurement invariance testing illustrates how the approach evaluates lasso-selected model modifications. Example R code is provided.

title: Interpreting prior-dependent precision in renal tumor growth estimates

Associations between types of residential greenspace and depressive symptoms in older adults: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis
abstract: Residential greenspace may prevent older-adult depression, but it is unclear whether this depends on type of greenspace and population subgroup. We examined associations between six greenspace measures and depressive symptoms among 6,799 U.S. older adults in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (1-3 observations per participant in 2000-2012). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression scale. Time-varying residential address-linked exposures included street-view-based vegetation (grass, trees, other, and total), satellite-based Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and park access. In fully adjusted mixed-effects Poisson models, overall associations were null (symptom count ratios [CRs], 0.98-1.03 per SD increase). Associations varied by site, race/ethnicity, neighborhood socioeconomic status, and population density. In site-stratified analyses, fewer symptoms were associated with NDVI in New York, NY (CR=0.96, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), park access in Winston-Salem, NC (CR=0.95, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), and grass in Minneapolis, MN (CR=0.87, 95% CI: 0.79, 0.97). The greenspace metric most strongly associated with fewer symptoms differed across racial/ethnic groups. Greater street-level greenspace was associated with more symptoms in high-density areas. Greenspace-depression associations may therefore depend on greenspace type and context, suggesting that mental-health-oriented greenspace interventions should be tailored to local populations and environments.

title: Re: Science or Advocacy? The Global Rise of Policy Claims and Calls to Action in Population Health Research (1990-2024)

Odds of culpability associated with the presence of drugs in injured drivers
abstract: Responsibility analysis was conducted on almost 10,000 drivers injured over a 10-year period in Victoria, Australia as a result of a vehicular collision and in whom comprehensive toxicology testing in blood was conducted. Multivariable logistic regression models were fitted to compute unadjusted (OR) and adjusted odds ratios (aOR). In the multivariable model, adjustments were made for gender, age group, vehicle type, and whether the crash occurred in metropolitan or rural areas. The psychoactive drug-free driver was the control group. Drivers with ethanol (alcohol) present at any concentration (>0.01 % BAC) confirmed the well-known large increases in OR that occur with rising blood ethanol concentration, with an aOR of 16.4 (95 %CI 11.1–24.2). Drivers positive to methamphetamine and no other psychoactive drug also showed a large increase in the odds of culpability (aOR 17.2, 95 %CI 10.2–29.2). Drivers with Δ 9 -tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) in blood showed a modest increase in odds when all concentrations (> 1 ng/mL) were assessed (aOR 1.5, 95 %CI 1.1–2.0) that trended to a possible increased aOR 2.1 (95 %CI 0.9–4.9) when concentrations were 10 ng/mL or higher. Benzodiazepines in drivers also showed a significant increase in odds (aOR1.8, 95 %CI 1.2–2.8), as well as antidepressants (aOR 1.3, 95 %CI 1.0–1.6). Opioids such as codeine and oxycodone showed no measurable increase in the odds of culpability, whereas combinations of ethanol with methamphetamine or THC gave aOR of 22.6 (95 %CI 3.0–168) and 20.0 (95 %CI 7.3–54.5), respectively, as well as drivers positive to both THC and methamphetamine (aOR 14.6, 95 % CI 5.9–36.4). Drivers positive to one or more illicit drug, or a larger selection of psychoactive drugs in the absence of ethanol both gave similarly large increase in odds (aOR 4.0, 95 %CI 3.3–5.0). This study contributes to a better understanding of risks associated with driving in the presence of common psychoactive drugs.

title: From not being parented to not being a parent: Reproductive outcomes following early institutional psychosocial deprivation
abstract: Background: Severe psychosocial deprivation, reflecting a lack of stable and responsive caregiving, can have long-term developmental consequences, yet little is known about its relation to later family formation and parenthood. Participants and Setting: This study examined reproductive outcomes among 174 individuals placed in Swiss infant care institutions in the 1950s and compared them with 196 non-institutionalized individuals from the same region and period (overall M age = 67.52, range = 62.87–71.39). Institutionalized children experienced severe psychosocial deprivation, with documented caregiver interaction amounting to less than one hour per 24-h period. Method: Using a convergent mixed-methods design, several regression models investigated the differences in the likelihood of becoming a parent, age at first parenthood, and number of children, while qualitative content analysis of biographical interviews explored individual experiences of non-parenthood among formerly institutionalized individuals. Results: Results showed that formerly institutionalized individuals were significantly less likely to become parents than the non-institutionalized cohort ( OR = 0.53, 95% CI [0.33, 0.83], p = .006). Flexible parametric survival models revealed that formerly institutionalized individuals had a lower average hazard of entering parenthood ( HR = 0.78, 95% CI [0.61, 0.997], p = .047). Among participants who became parents ( n = 260), linear regressions showed that formerly institutionalized individuals did so on average 1.3 years earlier than the comparison group (β = −0.23, 95% CI [−0.46, −0.008], p = .04). Number of children did not differ between cohorts ( OR = 0.71, 95% CI [0.44, 1.15], p = .17). Qualitative findings indicated that childlessness was linked to relational instability, structural and fertility-related constraints, and self-determined or protective decisions not to have children. Discussion: Together, the findings suggest that early psychosocial deprivation, as a severe disruption of early caregiving, may have lasting implications for family formation, primarily by reducing the likelihood of having children.

title: Advancing a Model of Mindful Sexual Communication: Testing Sexual Communication as a Mediator of the Association Between Sexual Mindfulness and Sexual Satisfaction
abstract: Mindfulness and communication have powerful implications for sexual health. Sexual communication and sexual mindfulness - the ability to be aware and non-judgmental during sexual activity - are two constructs often associated with sexual satisfaction. To further explore these relationships, a model of mindful sexual communication was advanced. More specifically, a moderated mediation model was tested to explore the indirect effect of sexual mindfulness on sexual satisfaction through sexual communication, as well as the potential moderating role of interoceptive awareness (i.e., trusting the body and self-regulation). Data were collected from 205 young adult college students in a variety of relational contexts that had a recent sexual interaction. The results indicated that sexual mindfulness awareness was indirectly associated with sexual satisfaction via frequency and comfort of sexual communication, whereas sexual mindfulness non-judgment was only indirectly associated with sexual satisfaction via sexual communication comfort. Additionally, two moderated mediation models were supported for participants in committed relationships: trusting the body and self-regulation moderated the indirect effect of sexual mindfulness non-judgment on sexual satisfaction via sexual communication comfort. The results reveal that different aspects of sexual mindfulness function uniquely together with aspects of sexual communication and interoceptive awareness to predict sexual satisfaction, revealing preliminary support for a new theoretical model of mindful sexual communication. These findings and their implications for sexual communication and mindfulness are discussed along with practical applications for individuals and professionals.

title: More Than Just a Happy Ending? The Role of Orgasm Consistency for Sexual Satisfaction, Relationship Satisfaction, and Emotional Intimacy in Mixed-Gender Romantic Relationships
abstract: Orgasm consistency is defined as the frequency with which individuals achieve orgasm during sexual encounters with a partner, while orgasm discrepancy is defined as the difference between the orgasm consistency of two partners. Orgasm consistency has been linked to sexual and relational well-being, yet little is known about how orgasm discrepancy in partners were associated with these factors. This study examined whether orgasm consistency as well as orgasm discrepancy in couples was associated with sexual satisfaction, relationship satisfaction, and emotional intimacy. Data from 327 couples were analyzed using Dyadic Response Surface Analysis. Higher orgasm consistency was associated with greater sexual satisfaction and relationship satisfaction, particularly among men, and with higher emotional intimacy among women. Contrary to expectations, couples with higher levels of orgasm discrepancy reported higher relationship satisfaction than couples with lower levels of orgasm discrepancy. Findings suggest that higher orgasm consistency may serve as a sexual reward, while orgasm discrepancy may not be perceived as a cost. Gendered sexual scripts likely shape these patterns. Overall, models explained limited variance, indicating that other factors beyond orgasm consistency are critical for sexual and relational well-being.

title: The shape of the cultural transmission of shapes

Turning the Tide. Studying the Impact of People Management on Teacher Turnover Intentions: The Mediating Roles of Role Ambiguity and Emotional Exhaustion
abstract: Teacher turnover poses a significant challenge to educational quality worldwide, with turnover intention serving as a critical precursor to actual turnover. This study explores how people management—defined as the integration of the implementation of human resource management practices and leadership behavior—affects teachers’ intentions to leave their positions. Grounded in conservation of resources theory, we examine how people management can serve as a crucial resource in reducing turnover intentions by alleviating role ambiguity and emotional exhaustion, two key issues in the teaching profession. Role ambiguity arises from the increasing demands placed on teachers, while emotional exhaustion exacerbates intentions to leave. Our results show support for the (serial) mediating role of role ambiguity and emotional exhaustion, providing new insights into how people management impacts teacher retention. The findings contribute to the understanding of how people management activities can effectively support teachers, reducing turnover intentions and ultimately enhancing overall education quality.

title: Stochastic flexibility quantification for urban integrated energy systems: Definition, modeling, and computation
Accurate remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries via capacity curve modeling with attention fusion learning framework
Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
abstract: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuration confirm that an LSTM encoder with a 15-minute single-step control horizon provides the most robust and deployment-ready configuration, and cross-site and single-factor out-of-distribution tests show that generalization to unseen profiles is profile-dependent, with policies trained on high-activity sites transferring most reliably.

title: Adaptive dynamic planning method for electric vehicle charging stations considering active interaction with EV growth

Angular solar absorption and thermal energy storage seasonally modulate radiative cooling
abstract: Passive daytime radiative cooling materials (RCs) maintain low surface temperatures under sunlight and can reduce building cooling loads and urban overheating. However, RCs with static optical properties overcool in cold seasons, and adaptive RCs proposed to date rely on temperature/humidity to switch their optical/radiative properties. Further, they address either daytime or nighttime response and are subject to ageing and to false switching on mild sunlit winter days. Here, we propose a system to seasonally modulate RCs with angular solar absorption, achieved with L-shaped fins, and with thermal energy storage (TES), implemented with phase change materials (PCMs) and concrete mass. The L-shaped fins have solar-absorptive, equator-facing walls shaded by horizontal eaves, enabling high direct solar absorption only at the low solar elevations of winter, with RC film on all other surfaces. Coupled with TES, the system is an angular-dependent thermal-mass-enhanced radiative cooler (ATMRC). In field campaigns in Western Sydney, the finned RC samples reached winter daytime surface temperatures 6–9 °C above the static RC and up to 11 °C above the unfinned RC + TES, resolving the daytime overcooling that TES alone introduces. The ATMRC with the 8 °C PCM reduced winter dew and frost durations by 56% and 73%, respectively, relative to the static RC. The summer daytime penalty against the static RC was 2 °C. Ray-tracing yields seasonal absorbed fractions of 37% in winter and 21% in summer in Sydney. Effective adaptive RCs therefore require both TES against night overcooling and angular-dependent solar absorption for daytime modulation.

Can the European recycling target for plastic packaging be met? A scenario analysis for Finland
abstract: The European Union’s plastic packaging recycling target for 2025 is unlikely to have been met by most member states, so to achieve the more ambitious 55% target for 2030 will require significant changes to existing waste management and recycling practices. This study examines the factors affecting plastic packaging waste recycling and assesses, using 13 waste collection and recycling efficiency scenarios, the conditions under which Finland could meet the 2030 target. The findings indicate that the target is a multidimensional challenge shaped by multiple factors along the plastic value chain. At present, a substantial proportion of packaging waste is incinerated instead of material recovery. Priority should be given to business packaging by substantially improving the separate collection rates, with material recovery from mixed waste streams as a complementary measure. The paper also suggests targeted policies and interventions for improving plastic packaging recycling in Finland and beyond.

title: Microplastics Are Prevalent in Striped Bass and Shiner Surfperch Tissues across San Francisco Bay, California
abstract: Abstract The ingestion of microplastics by fish is widely documented, but the drivers of contamination and the movement of particles within organisms are still not well understood. We investigated microplastic contamination in sport fish caught from San Francisco Bay in California, USA. We compared microplastic contamination in striped bass (Morone saxatilis) and shiner surfperch (Cymatogaster aggregata). We observed an average of 5.9 ± 5.6 (Std Dev) microplastics per fish, with significantly higher overall contamination in striped bass but higher concentrations (microplastics/gram of tissue) in shiner surfperch. For each, we considered contamination relevant to their consumption by recreational anglers. For striped bass, where only the fillet is typically ingested, we found that contamination among tissues differed significantly (on average 3.8 ± 3.1 microplastics/fish fillets). Shiner surfperch, which are typically consumed whole, had an average body burden of 9.1 ± 1.2 microplastics/fish. Contamination varied significantly (p-value < 0.0001) among sampling locations for shiner surfperch, with the highest amounts observed near urban centers (no significant spatial pattern was observed for striped bass). Our findings show microplastics in tissues beyond the gastrointestinal tract, posing concerns for fish health and suggesting that fish caught from San Francisco Bay are a pathway for human consumption of microplastics.

title: Arsenate Adsorption by Amorphous Titanium (Hydr)Oxides: Governing Roles of Medium-Range Ordering and Surface Disorder
abstract: Abstract Amorphous metal (hydr)oxides are used for oxyanion removal from water, yet the structural features responsible for their adsorption performance remain poorly understood. This paper systematically investigated how the ordering range and associated structural characteristics of amorphous titanium (hydr)oxides influence the adsorption of arsenate, used here as a model oxyanion. Six materials were synthesized with ordering ranges spanning approximately 4 to 43 Å. As the ordering range increased, a transition from microporous–mesoporous structures to predominantly mesoporous architectures was observed. Characterizations revealed progressive structural ordering with increasing synthesis aging temperature. The most amorphous sample exhibited stronger water binding, providing indirect evidence of fewer surrounding hydration clusters than in more ordered samples. However, despite possessing the highest specific surface area, the most amorphous material did not exhibit the highest arsenate uptake. Instead, the material aged at 140 °C achieved the greatest adsorption capacity, exceeding that of the fully amorphous material by >20%. This adsorption maximum coincided with an intermediate ordering range, a transitional structural state, and a mesopore-dominated pore architecture. The results indicate that arsenate adsorption is not governed by surface area alone. Instead, the ordering range provides a useful descriptor linking atomic-scale structure, pore architecture, hydration behavior, and adsorption performance in amorphous metal (hydr)oxides.

title: Emerging Contaminants Are Associated with Seasonal Variations in Phytoplankton Community Diversity in a Eutrophic Lake
abstract: Abstract Emerging contaminants (ECs) are increasingly detected in eutrophic lakes, yet their ecological contributions to phytoplankton community variation relative to conventional environmental factors remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the spatiotemporal occurrence of typical ECs and associated phytoplankton community variation in Taihu Lake, China. Phytoplankton abundance was significantly correlated with water temperature and total phosphorus (P < 0.05). Among the EC groups, organochlorine pesticides (37.7%), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (16.7%), and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (16.1%) showed strong associations with the spatiotemporal variation in phytoplankton community composition. Organochlorine pesticides explained 18.8% and 25.9% of the α-diversity variation in spring and summer, respectively, and interaction analyses suggested potential combined effects among contaminant groups. Water quality factors and ECs jointly explained 67.9% of the community variation, with stronger associations observed in summer than in spring. Higher dominance of Cryptomonas ovata in Gonghu Bay during spring and Microcystis sp. in Western Bay during summer was associated with reduced phytoplankton community diversity under combined gradients of eutrophication and ECs. These findings highlight the covariation of phytoplankton communities with eutrophication and ECs and provide new insights into ecological risk assessment and algal bloom management in shallow eutrophic lakes.

title: Dynamic Hydrogen-Bonded Hydration Networks Mitigate Organic–Inorganic Fouling in Nanofiltration
abstract: Abstract Hydration layers are widely recognized as the molecular basis of antifouling membrane interfaces, yet their role is still largely viewed through a static barrier picture. The dynamic response of hydrated membrane–water interfaces to approaching foulants, particularly under organic–inorganic mixed fouling conditions, remains poorly understood. Here, using poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) (pSBMA)-modified nanofiltration membranes as a model zwitterionic interface, we reveal that fouling reversibility is strongly influenced by the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks at the membrane–water interface. Molecular simulations combined with sum-frequency generation spectroscopy demonstrate that pSBMA sustains a strongly hydrogen-bonded interfacial water structure with preferential water dipole orientation under silicate and alginate perturbation, thereby suppressing long-lived foulant residence near the membrane surface. Real-time surface plasmon resonance measurements further confirm weakened irreversible foulant anchoring and enhanced interfacial reversibility. As a result, pSBMA-modified nanofiltration membranes reduced flux decline during mixed-foulant filtration to ∼6% and achieved >91% flux recovery after physical cleaning, accompanied by lower organic and inorganic foulant residuals. Repeated filtration–cleaning tests with real secondary effluent further confirmed nearly complete flux recovery in complex water matrices. These findings revisit zwitterionic antifouling by shifting the focus from static surface hydration to the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding and regulating fouling reversibility.

title: Mechanistic Understanding of Breath-Borne Bacterial Inactivation Kinetics in Oxidant-Rich and Natural Air
abstract: Abstract Bioaerosols play a central role in respiratory infection transmission, but how atmospheric oxidants affect their viability, especially in human respiratory fluids, remains unexplored. Here, we investigated the inactivation of five bacterial species with distinct cell envelope architectures (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus, and Mycobacterium smegmatis) suspended in human exhaled breath condensate (EBC) droplets exposed to gas-phase hydroxyl radicals (•OH) produced by ultraviolet irradiation of H2O2. Compared with the other three exposure conditions, the •OH-generating (H2O2+UV) treatment caused the greatest viability loss, with 4-h survival ranging from 24.3% (E. coli) to 63.0% (M. smegmatis). Gram-negative bacteria were sensitive to both H2O2 and •OH, whereas Gram-positive species resisted H2O2 but were inactivated by •OH. M. smegmatis showed the highest tolerance. Inactivation accelerated in smaller droplets, and the size-dependent kinetics were characterized using Weibull and first-order models incorporating surface-area-to-volume ratio. Morphological, biochemical, and metabolomic analyses indicated that the observed inactivation differences were associated with bacterial envelope types and surface characteristics. •OH preferentially degrades outer membrane glycolipids in Gram-negative bacteria and oxidizes cytoplasmic membrane lipids in Gram-positive bacteria, while all species shared a core signature of nucleic acid oxidative damage. These findings provide a molecular understanding of bacterial inactivation kinetics in human EBC droplets and may inform the assessment of bioaerosol transmission risks.

title: Near-Complete Decomposition of Soil Microplastics over Transient Electrical Heating and Associated Benefits
abstract: Abstract Soil serves as a significant sink for microplastics, posing considerable risks to both the ecological and human health. The diverse composition and dynamic transformation of microplastics present major challenges for remediation as conventional strategies often fail to achieve efficient and complete decomposition. In this study, biochar was applied to microplastic-contaminated soil as a conductive material to initiate transient electric heating under a low-power input. This approach facilitated near-complete decomposition of soil microplastics (>95.0%) across the tested soil and microplastic types while preventing soil hardening. Specifically, electric heating enhanced interactions between soil microplastics and the biochar conductor, leading to the formation of highly aromatic carbon (HAC). The resulting HAC not only improved soil microecology but also supported the growth of pak choi (Brassica campestris L. ssp.). The newly formed HAC was found to upregulate the expression of auxin-responsive gene families, including Aux/IAA and GH3, in the roots. HAC enriched tryptamine in the rhizosphere, and tryptamine abundance was positively correlated with the relative abundance of Sphingomonas, a genus with a reported capacity to convert tryptamine-derived intermediates toward indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) biosynthesis. These findings demonstrate that transient electric heating offers a sustainable strategy for decomposing diverse soil microplastics and that the remediated soil remains safe and conducive for agricultural production.

title: Unveiling Phase-Dependent Fe–O Bond-Guided Nitrate Reduction at Biocathodes: Balancing Interfacial Reactivity and Iron Bioavailability
abstract: Abstract Iron oxides are widespread in anoxic water environments, yet how their structures regulate microbial nitrate reduction remains unclear. Here, we reveal that phase-dependent Fe–O bond characteristics guide denitrification in bioelectrochemical system (BES) by balancing lattice-iron bioavailability and interfacial electrochemical reactivity at biocathodes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that surface Fe–O bond covalency was associated with the thermodynamic barrier to lattice-iron release. α-Fe2O3, with the most negative ICOHP, exhibited the strongest Fe–O bonding and restricted iron release, thereby limiting microbial iron acquisition and downstream Fe–S cluster assembly. In contrast, γ-Fe2O3 and γ-FeOOH exhibited higher surface electroactivity but suffered from structural instability, evidenced by phase transformation, cell encrustation, and elevated microbial mortality. With mixed valence and balanced Fe–O bonding characteristics, Fe3O4 achieved the highest denitrification efficiency (17.8-fold enhancement over its abiotic control), which enabled direct Fe(II) uptake via the FeoAB system, bypassing siderophore-dependent acquisition and simultaneously activating both TonB-mediated iron acquisition and Fur-flavin-regulated respiratory pathways. This dual-pathway activation supported enhancement in biomass growth, intracellular electron transfer, and Fe–S cluster-dependent enzymatic activity. These findings help establish Fe–O bond characteristics as a key structural factor for Fe–N coupling and offer a structural perspective for rational design of iron-oxide-based nitrate-removal technologies.

title: Joint decision-making for contract duration and benefit sharing in energy performance contract: A China-based shared-savings building retrofit case

AI-driven granular LCA for apparel: Quantifying product-specific GHG emissions for sustainable design and circularity
abstract: Product-specific Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) for apparel is hindered by generalized data, failing to quantify unique environmental burdens crucial for sustainable production and consumption. This study addresses this challenge by proposing and validating an automated methodology using a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to extract product-specific details (e.g., fabric composition) from unstructured User-Generated Content (UGC) on consumer-to-consumer (C2C) platforms and subsequently calculate corresponding product-specific greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The study seeks to demonstrate the significance of AI-enabled product-specific information as a tool for deriving insights into sustainable production, cleaner manufacturing, and resource efficiency. Applying this framework to 3500 apparel listings from a major C2C marketplace, our VLM demonstrated high accuracy in extracting physical attributes like garment size (92.3%) and fabric composition (81.6%). The subsequent LCA quantified an average emission of 11.9 kg-CO 2 eq/item. More importantly, by analyzing the product-related parameters required for these computations, we attempted to extract and structure data on product attributes and user behavior from unstructured UGC, enabling more effective estimation of product-specific GHG emissions. Although challenges remain in precisely inferring complex user behaviors from unstructured data, the successful granularization of material composition highlights the significant impact of material selection, providing actionable insights for sustainable eco-design and circularity. Ultimately, by significantly enhancing information transparency across the value chain, our work directly aligns with emerging global policies like the EU Digital Product Passport (DPP), fostering data-driven decision-making for cleaner production goals.

title: Modeling of the condensate throttling system for variable load characteristic analysis of coal-fired units based on segmented self-adaption
Impact of process configuration on flexibility–cost trade-offs in amine-based post-combustion carbon capture systems
The use of biochar in agricultural soils: Impacts on vineyard productivity and the potential for carbon capture and sequestration
abstract: Background Viticulture is increasingly exposed to water deficit, heat and soil degradation, prompting interest in biochar as a soil amendment that may simultaneously improve productivity and sequester carbon. Methods This integrative review used a documented Scopus search (June 2026), targeted searches (September 2026), explicit eligibility criteria and a PRISMA-style flow diagram. All vineyard field trials were tabulated, meta-analyses were reported with effect and sample sizes, and each conclusion was graded by level of evidence. Results Significant yield gains were confined to three Tuscan vineyards amended with the same 500 °C orchard-pruning biochar on acidic to neutral, carbon-poor, non-irrigated soils (+16% to +67% per harvest, persisting ten years after application), and eight site-level comparisons, six in humid-temperate, cool or calcareous-alkaline settings, showed no significant yield response, whereas increases in soil water and topsoil organic carbon were more consistent. The most robust climate outcome is the persistence of the biochar carbon (inert fraction unchanged after 15 years, 65–89% remaining after 100 years), whereas N2O and CH4 reductions are not robust at field scale and remain undetected in vineyards. The previously cited 7.5 Mg CO2-eq ha-1 yr-1, the mean of all soil‑carbon practices in vineyards, rests on very few biochar observations, whereas a single 16.5 t ha-1 (dry) application stores 31–42 Mg CO2-eq ha-1 over 100 years before life-cycle emissions. Without a yield response, the break-even carbon price for biochar costing €200–500 t-1 is €90–243 per t CO2-eq, against a carbon-removal index of €135 (2026), and a single application requires 22–48 years of a vineyard's own prunings. Conclusions Carbon storage in the biochar itself is well supported, agronomic benefits are demonstrated only for a narrow pedoclimatic domain and require independent replication, and greenhouse-gas co-benefits, long-term microbial effects, economic viability and large-scale carbon farming remain plausible but poorly documented or speculative.

Regulatory quality, energy consumption, and environmental sustainability in a developing economy: Evidence from a Bayesian vector error correction model
abstract: Sustainable management of the environment is among the primary objectives of sustainable development. Although environmental regulation is widely studied in advanced economies, its effectiveness in developing nations like Nigeria, characterized by weak regulatory and enforcement institutions, remains underexplored. Based on the Stochastic Impacts by Regression on Population, Affluence, and Technology framework, and using ecological balance (EB) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions (COEs) as environmental indicators, this article investigates the impact of environmental regulations on environmental sustainability in Nigeria in an augmented framework that includes renewable energy consumption and gross domestic product as additional regressors. Using annual time series data from 1990 to 2022, the study employs the novel Bayesian Vector Error Correction Model, which improves the robustness of the parameter estimates by utilizing the Inverse Wishart Prior distribution. Robust postsimulation is conducted using the Gibbs sampling technique to generate 5000 iterations. The posterior mean estimates indicate that a one-standard-deviation improvement in regulatory quality (RQ) is associated with a decrease of 0.027 units in ecological deficit and a decrease of 0.111 units in COEs, though the credible intervals for the latter include zero. The results also show that higher RQ is associated with a decreased deficit between ecological footprint and biocapacity (i.e. improved EB) and CO 2 , indicating that effective regulatory frameworks may lead to more sustainable environmental outcomes. The results also demonstrate that the effect of regulating the environment is stronger on COEs compared to EB, implying that more stringent environmental regulations are necessary to promote EB than to reduce COEs. Nigeria's weak enforcement institutions amplify the urgency of reforms; hence, there is a need to improve RQ to ensure the efficient administration of environmental legislation in Nigeria. Relevant policy inferences and recommendations have been provided in the paper.

title: Exploratory geoplay in metaverse fieldwork: Avatar movement as learning data for geographic understanding
abstract: Geogames are increasingly recognized as playful systems based on real-world geographic data and spatial reasoning, yet open-ended geographic play remains underexplored. This study examines immersive virtual fieldwork as exploratory geoplay, where participants engage with geographic environments through autonomous observation, movement, and interaction rather than scores, competition, or fixed missions. We developed a multiplayer metaverse environment based on a life-scale 3D reconstruction of the Byobugaura Sea Cliff in Japan. Sixty-two participants explored it in two rounds: one unguided and one supported by light interpretive prompts. Avatar positions were recorded using the YAIBA behavior-logging system and analyzed through space-time clustering, PCA, trajectory-grid aggregation, and cluster-duration analysis. During unguided exploration, participants clustered around geomorphologically significant areas, while interpretive supports shifted visits toward breakwater and terrace zones. Cluster durations increased in the smaller sub-instance but remained stable in the larger main instance. Questionnaire responses reflected positive experiences and perceived behavioral changes. By framing avatar movement as learning data, while recognizing that movement does not directly measure knowledge acquisition, this study proposes exploratory geoplay as a model for studying locational attention and geographic inquiry within immersive environments.

title: Salinization and Development,
abstract: Abstract Climate change-intensified seawater intrusion creates a dual shock of transitory freshwater shortages and lasting soil degradation. We study its impacts on agricultural production in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta, a major rice exporter. Combining river salinity observations and detailed canal network data to map localized hydrological shocks, we find that salinity reduces rice yields but generates disproportionately larger declines in output and revenue. These losses are driven by a contraction in land under cultivation and limited substitution toward salt-resistant crops, pointing to constrained short-run adaptation. Using household and firm data, we further document reductions in own-farm employment alongside minimal transition to non-agricultural sectors, suggesting frictions in labor adjustment. Beyond income effects predicted by Engel curves, households reallocate expenditures toward healthcare and children’s schooling. The increase in schooling spending is driven by higher participation and may reflect shifts in opportunity costs, though we cannot rule out forward-looking responses.
