Smart strategies for a sustainable future: Bridging green finance, smart technologies, and sustainable energy efficiency to combat environmental degradation
abstract: Rising environmental degradation (ED) is a global phenomenon. While various environmental initiatives have been introduced across disciplines, mitigating environmental degradation remains a critical challenge. Recently, the world has emphasized the importance of smart technologies, green finance, and stringent government policies as additional tools for environmental sustainability; therefore, it is essential to clarify the empirical evidence on their effectiveness for environmental policymakers. This study evaluates income, population in large cities, smart technologies, green finance, sustainable energy efficiency, and government policy as environmental determinants for nine OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) nations from 2012 to 2023. Using panel quantile regression and fully modified ordinary least squares, the empirical findings reveal that the population of large cities and sustainable energy efficiency are positively associated with ED. Conversely, income shows an inverse connection and contributes to sustainability. In the context of smart technologies, this study focuses on digital transformation (DT) and artificial intelligence and finds a significant role for DT in environmental management. This study employs two proxies for green finance: green foreign direct investment and green bonds, both of which exhibit unusual behavior with respect to the intended theme. Finally, the moderating effect of green finance and smart technologies on sustainable energy efficiency doesn't support environmental management. This study also offers valuable suggestions for achieving long-term environmental sustainability.

title: Remittance outflows and environmental sustainability: The roles of financial development, energy transition, openness to trade, and natural resource rents in the world's largest remittance-providing economies
abstract: This study examines the environmental implications of remittance outflows, an area that has received far less attention than remittance inflows despite the growing importance of major migrant-providing economies in global sustainability efforts. It develops an integrated analytical framework incorporating remittance outflows, financial development, energy transition, openness to trade, natural resource rents (NRRs), and economic development to explain carbon emissions in the ten largest remittance-providing countries worldwide. Using annual panel data from 1990 to 2023, the study employs the second-generation cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag estimator to estimate long-run and short-run relationships, with augmented mean group and common correlated effects mean group estimators used for robustness and a supplementary instrumental-variable 2SLS analysis used as a diagnostic exercise. The results indicate a stable long-run equilibrium relationship among the variables. Remittance outflows have no statistically significant long-run association with carbon emissions, indicating no robust evidence of a direct conditional effect after controlling for the structural determinants included in the model. In contrast, the renewable energy consumption share significantly reduces carbon emissions, whereas financial development, trade openness, and NRRs increase emissions. Economic growth has no significant long-run effect after controlling for these structural factors. The findings are consistent with the Pollution Haven Hypothesis and Resource Curse Theory, while indicating that financial deepening alone does not guarantee environmental improvement. These results underscore the importance of accelerating renewable-energy deployment, strengthening green financial systems, integrating environmental safeguards into trade policies, and promoting sustainable natural-resource governance to advance Sustainable Development Goals 7, 13, and 17.

title: Identifying Key Controlling Factors and Improving Pedotransfer Functions for Saturated Soil Hydraulic Conductivity Using Principal Component Analysis and Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Saturated hydraulic conductivity ( K Sat ) is a critical soil property governing hydrological processes across scales, particularly at the soil surface, where it controls infiltration and water movement into deeper layers. Measuring K Sat in the field is challenging due to high variability, time‐intensive methods, costly equipment, and the need for skilled labor and large samples. Soil heterogeneity and land‐use effects further complicate extrapolation of K Sat values. This study aimed to (i) identify key‐driving factors that relate K Sat with hydro‐physical soil attributes and land use systems at a watershed scale, (ii) evaluate the performance of artificial neural networks (ANNs) in predicting K Sat by comparing them with multiple linear regression (MLR) models, and (iii) assess whether variables derived from principal component analysis (PCA) could improve model K Sat predictions. ANN and MLR models were developed for a watershed in southern Brazil, using an experimental grid of 178 points. Soil properties (bulk density, total porosity, micro‐ and macroporosity, organic carbon, particle‐size distribution, and K Sat ) were measured in the 0–20 cm layer, and land use was mapped from satellite imagery. PCA was applied to derive principal components (PCs), which were used as predictors in modeling. Results showed that incorporating PCs significantly improved ANN performance, with the best model (combining total porosity, soil texture, three PCs, and land use) achieving an R 2 of 0.70 and RMSE of 0.41 m h −1 , outperforming the corresponding MLR model. This indicates that K Sat variability is driven by both soil and land‐use factors and their orthogonal recombinations capturing the dataset's variance structure.

title: Spatial spillovers of local climate adaptation policy: Evidence from FEMA’s Community Rating System
Sustainable Value Creation and Board Gender Diversity in Multinational Enterprises: The Moderating Role of Degree of Internationalisation
abstract: ABSTRACT This study explores the empirical relationship between sustainable value creation (SVC), board gender diversity (BGD) and the degree of internationalisation (DOI) in multinational enterprises (MNEs). Using an unbalanced panel of 285 MNEs across 22 countries over the period 2016–2025 and employing high‐dimensional fixed effects (FE), system GMM and entropy balancing techniques, we find that the individual effects of BGD and DOI on SVC are negative and insignificant, respectively. However, the interaction term (BGD × DOI) has a positive and significant effect on SVC. Theoretically, our findings suggest that the rigorous monitoring associated with gender‐diverse boards shifts from being a coordination cost to a value‐enhancing asset as MNEs face the heightened complexity and information asymmetry of global operations. This study contributes to Sustainability, Corporate Governance and International Business literature by synthesising stakeholder and legitimacy perspectives to explain the contingent role of corporate governance in MNE sustainable value creation.

title: From Digital Readiness to Circular Performance: The Roles of Dynamic Capabilities, Ambidexterity, and Organizational Agility
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how organizational readiness (OR), dynamic capabilities (DCs), and organizational ambidexterity (OAM) influence organizational agility (OA) and drive circular economy performance (CEP) in manufacturing firms. Using a conceptual framework grounded in resource‐based and institutional theories, the research empirically explores how internal capabilities and strategic enablers facilitate effective circular economy adoption. The study surveyed 207 respondents from Japanese manufacturing firms engaged in CE and sustainability practices and analyzed the data using validated theoretical constructs with covariance‐based structural equation model (SEM). The study found a positive association between DR, DC, and CEI. CEI was strongly associated with OA, which in turn enhanced CEP. CEI also significantly mediated the impacts of DC and DR on OA, whereas the moderating effect of OAM between CEI and OA was not supported. The research scope is limited to one area in the Japanese context, and applying a cross‐sectional methodology lacks the possibility of understanding. Further research is recommended to apply longitudinal techniques and to examine the framework's applicability across different economic and geographical settings. The research suggests practical perceptions for policymakers and business owners to develop proper circular economy initiatives, build capabilities, and improve their CEP. This study contributes by examining the underexplored link between OA and CEP in Japanese manufacturing firms. It proposes a validated framework highlighting DR and DCs as drivers of CEI, their effects on agility and performance, and the moderating effect of OAM.

title: Does Eco‐Efficiency Pay in a Fragmented Food Industry? A Simultaneous‐Equations Analysis of Accounting‐Based Resource Productivity and Profitability in the Italian Dairy Sector
abstract: ABSTRACT This study asks whether eco‐efficiency and environmental investment relate to firm financial performance in the Italian dairy industry, and whether that relationship is reciprocal rather than one‐directional, across the 2020–2024 energy‐ and input‐price cycle. Using audited AIDA accounts for the population of 466 limited companies in ATECO division 10.5 (463 firms with usable accounts, 2278 firm‐years; 324 industrial processors and 138 artisanal dairies), it measures eco‐efficiency through an accounting‐based resource‐productivity proxy (revenue per unit of tangible capital), complements it with process‐modernisation capital and recorded green‐innovation intensities and with external life‐cycle benchmarks, and estimates a two‐equation simultaneous system by three‐stage least squares with equation‐specific instruments that pass over‐identification tests, firm‐clustered standard errors and controls for cooperative governance, PDO area and product segment. The sector is extremely fragmented (Herfindahl–Hirschman index 0.013), and one third of its firms are producer cooperatives. The estimates are consistent with a reciprocal relationship: Resource productivity is robustly associated with higher return on assets across pooled, fixed‐effects and first‐difference instrumental‐variable estimators, whereas the feedback from profitability to resource productivity holds in levels and within firms but not in first‐difference instrumental‐variable estimates, so the reciprocal reading is supported but not established. Process‐modernisation capital shows no contemporaneous association with margins, recorded green innovation is negligible (zero in 90.6% of firm‐years), and cooperatives are as resource‐productive as investor‐owned firms but retain none of the gain as margin, in line with the member‐price‐maximisation logic of cooperative governance. Unlike neighbouring shock‐hit food chains, dairy delivered growth with margins. The paper contributes a full‐population, audited‐accounts test of the eco‐efficiency–performance relationship in a cooperative‐dense, fragmented food industry, documents a measurement inversion in balance‐sheet innovation proxies, and derives implications for environmental strategy, green‐capital allocation and the territorial dairy system.

Occurrence and Environmental Weathering of Agricultural Microplastics on Beaches across Japan: Insights into Surface Mineralization and Metal Binding
abstract: Abstract We investigated the coastal occurrence and environmental weathering of microplastics derived from polymer-coated fertilizers (PCFs) across Japan. A field survey along the Japanese coastline revealed that PCF-derived microplastics are widely distributed on beaches throughout the country, indicating that agricultural microplastics have dispersed far beyond agricultural landscapes. Compositional analysis showed that these particles consist predominantly of polyolefins (∼70%) and polyurethanes (∼30%) and commonly exhibit oxidative degradation accompanied by iron enrichment. Bulk elemental analysis demonstrated positive correlations between iron and multiple heavy metals. Micro-X-ray fluorescence mapping using a focused 20-μm beam showed that chromium is heterogeneously distributed on the plastic surface and spatially associated with iron, while X-ray absorption spectroscopy indicated its occurrence in ferrihydrite-like phases or as chromite. Although detailed spectroscopic evidence was obtained from a single selected particle, the widespread occurrence of PCF-derived microplastics and their observed metal enrichment suggest that similar geochemical processes may occur at other coastal sites. By linking nationwide field observations with process-level characterization, this study shows that microplastics have the potential to transition from inert debris to geochemically reactive substrates after coastal deposition.

Recent environmental change shapes biotic homogenisation of Orthoptera and Mantodea communities in semi-dry grasslands
abstract: Semi-dry grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems in Europe. However, many grassland remnants are undergoing gradual habitat degradation due to climate change, atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and the relaxation or abandonment of traditional management. While declines of specialised insects have repeatedly been reported, the extent to which these drivers promote long-term community reorganisation and biotic homogenisation remains poorly understood. Using a nationwide resurvey of 221 semi-dry grassland patches across Germany, spanning two to three decades, we investigated long-term changes in Orthoptera and Mantodea communities. We quantified changes in species richness, community composition, and beta diversity, and related these patterns to major global change drivers. Despite an increase in total species richness, these communities became increasingly homogenised, as indicated by declining beta diversity. Community reorganisation was characterised by pronounced winner-loser dynamics, with highly mobile generalists and thermophilous species expanding, whereas threatened species, low-mobility habitat specialists, and species associated with High Nature Value farmland declined. Winner species richness increased particularly in warm and dry regions, under elevated atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and outside protected areas. By contrast, low-mobility habitat specialists and threatened species persisted most successfully in structurally heterogeneous habitats. High shrub cover was negatively associated with both winners and losers, indicating an overall deterioration of habitat suitability. Our findings demonstrate that environmental change does not necessarily reduce species richness but can profoundly reorganise communities through selective filtering of species. Maintaining habitat heterogeneity with appropriate management strategies is therefore crucial for buffering biodiversity loss under ongoing global change.

title: Environment-conditioned vegetation carbon-production performance informs restoration assessment across China
Low Soil Organic Matter Stability Exacerbates the Vulnerability of Karst Areas to Rocky Desertification
abstract: ABSTRACT Karst rocky desertification represents a severe form of land degradation and has traditionally been attributed to geological and hydrological constraints. However, soil organic matter (SOM), a key regulator of erosion resistance, is highly responsive to management practices, yet its contribution to rocky desertification remains poorly understood. This study investigated three representative soil types (limestone soil, yellow soil, and yellowish‐brown soil) in the karst region of southwestern China to elucidate SOM‐related mechanisms underlying the high erosion susceptibility of limestone soils. Compared with other soil types, SOM in limestone soils exhibited lower hydrophobicity, higher polarity, and greater carbohydrate abundance, indicating a potentially more labile SOM pool that is vulnerable to leaching and degradation. In addition, SOM stabilization in limestone soils was more strongly associated with exchangeable and carbonate‐bound Ca than with Fe‐ and Al‐associated mineral phases. Given the high mobility of Ca under humid karst conditions, Ca‐mediated organo‐mineral associations may be inherently unstable. Spectroscopic analyses further revealed that SOM in limestone soils had higher apparent molecular weight, lower aromaticity, and shorter aliphatic chain lengths, which may limit its accessibility with mineral surface. Collectively, these findings challenge the conventional view that greater higher SOM content necessarily indicates enhanced soil stability. The susceptibility of limestone soils to rocky desertification may be closely linked to both the intrinsic instability of SOM and the fragility of Ca‐mediated stabilization mechanisms. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms driving karst soil degradation and highlight the potential importance of improving SOM quality for mitigating karst rocky desertification.

title: Optimal Policy Rules in HANK
abstract: Abstract We characterize optimal policy rules in a business-cycle model with nominal rigidities and heterogeneous households. The policymaker has access to two instruments: the short-term nominal rate, and lump-sum transfer payments. A policymaker with a traditional dual mandate that targets aggregates uses the same policy rule as is optimal in the textbook New Keynesian model. We then consider a policymaker with a distributional objective. The optimal policy rule now contains an additional term, reflecting the effects of the policymaker’s instruments on consumption inequality. Since, in our model, monetary policy only has very limited distributional effects, this additional term does not materially change optimal monetary policy. Fiscal stimulus payments, on the other hand, have strongly progressive effects and are thus well-suited to cushion the distributional effects of cyclical fluctuations.

title: Real exchange rates in the European price revolution
abstract: The European price revolution that began in the 16th century is one of the earliest episodes of widely-recognized inflation. I use inter-city real exchange rates (measured in silver) to assess how extensively it spread and how rapidly long-run PPP was restored. Real exchange rates appear to be stationary with half-lives similar to those in modern data: Thus there was a shared price revolution. But I also find that debasements contributed significantly to local-currency inflation. Tracking these relative prices also reveals some notable differences across cities that are worthy of further study.

Agricultural Frontier Expansion and Land Concentration: Insights From Colombian Municipalities
abstract: ABSTRACT Existing literature argues that expanding the agricultural frontier fosters land concentration, but most evidence is based on single regions within countries. This paper uses countrywide panel data for Colombia and a Propensity Score Matching (PSM) strategy to compare municipalities with evidence of post‐1964 frontier expansion with otherwise similar municipalities without such expansion. We show that approximately 8% of Colombian municipalities can be classified as frontier municipalities. Furthermore, we document pronounced regional differences in land concentration (measured as the share of rural private cadastral area held in ≥ 500‐ha holdings), with an upward trend in many frontier regions. Consistent with these patterns, our PSM estimates indicate that frontier municipalities experienced an increase in land concentration that was at least nine percentage points higher than in comparable non‐frontier municipalities. We also provide empirical evidence consistent with forced displacement being one plausible channel in the relationship between frontier exposure and higher land concentration in Colombia. These findings support the view that frontier expansion is associated with higher land concentration and imply that, in the absence of broader structural reforms, frontier‐expansion policies are unlikely to reduce land inequality.

Does Managerial Ability Remain Valuable During Economic Shocks?
abstract: ABSTRACT Managerial ability is often viewed as a source of competitive advantage, but its value may diminish when economic conditions change. We examine whether managerial ability remains valuable during monetary policy shocks and whether financial markets recognize this adaptive capacity. Firms led by more able managers experience more favourable stock price reactions to both expansionary and contractionary monetary policy surprises. Exploiting plausibly exogenous CEO turnover, we provide evidence consistent with a causal interpretation. More able managers also facilitate more stable adjustment, with firm growth and capital structure exhibiting lower volatility, thereby avoiding costly fluctuations in investment and financing decisions.

title: Financial Constraints, Wages, and Macroeconomic Implications
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates how firm‐level financial constraints affect individual wages and aggregate labor market dynamics during financial recessions. We derive testable predictions from competing theoretical mechanisms and assess them empirically using German administrative worker data matched to firm balance sheets. Embedding these microlevel estimates in a macroeconomic model with labor and financial frictions, we demonstrate how small ceteris paribus effects align with large aggregate dynamics. Tighter financial conditions amplify wage and unemployment volatility, weakening the tight link between wage rigidity and the volatility of unemployment discussed in the literature. Financial constraints reduce the effectiveness of hiring subsidies during recessions.

title: Environmental Disclosure Research Revisited: A Bibliometric–TCCM Synthesis of Theoretical Integration and Methodological Diversification
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the evolution and determinants of corporate environmental disclosure research through a systematic review of 117 peer‐reviewed articles published from 2016 to 2026 in Scopus. Using the PRISMA 2020 protocol and the SPAR‐4‐SLR framework, a bibliometric analysis was conducted with Bibliometrix and VOSviewer, complemented by the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Method (TCCM) approach to map the intellectual structure, thematic development and research gaps. The findings indicate growing research output, rising markedly after 2023, with China leading in publication output and the United Kingdom attracting the greatest citation impact. Legitimacy, stakeholder and institutional theories dominate the field but are often used in parallel rather than integrated, while governance mechanisms and firm‐level characteristics show inconsistent associations across contexts. Thematic analysis identifies environmental reporting as the core theme, whereas disclosure quality, green innovation and performance outcomes remain underexplored. Future research should prioritise theoretical integration, disclosure quality measurement and methodologically diverse designs.

title: Artificial intelligence in human resources: Examining the mechanisms and boundary conditions shaping perceived recruitment performance impact in hotels

From Flight Shame to Flight Governance: How Climate-Linked Digital Discourse Reveals Pathways for Aviation Commons
abstract: Grounded in commons theory and Ostrom’s institutional analysis framework, this study examines how climate-linked digital discourse frames aviation’s role in degrading the atmospheric commons, with Reddit serving as the empirical setting. The study used a qualitatively driven, computationally assisted design based on 3,756 cleaned Reddit comments collected from climate-linked discussions between January 2023 and January 2026. Within this sampled corpus, thematic analysis identifies four recurrent patterns: (1) Frequent flyers capture the atmospheric commons , (2) Air travel stays normalised despite rising commons awareness , (3) High-speed rail and ground modes offer commons-compatible substitutes and (4) Technological fixes face energy and feasibility limits in aviation . Model-based sentiment and emotion analysis, validated against manual audits, shows a largely negative profile marked by uncertainty, disgust and anger, especially around unequal use, weak accountability and unverifiable claims. The study develops a three-layer framework linking climate-linked digital discourse, proposed governance responses and material substitution pathways.

title: Scorecard Integration and Cross-Functional Coordination: Joint Effects on Managerial Commitment to ESG Goals
Large language models for tech mining and technology opportunity analysis: A diffusion of innovation perspective on detecting evolutionary stages of innovative practices using ChatGPT
abstract: Technology opportunity analysis (TOA) traditionally examines technological developments to identify opportunities, but typically conceptualizes these opportunities at the level of technologies or fields. This study advances practice-level TOA by conceptualizing technology-enabled innovative practices as technology-process-industry configurations and using their evolution to identify technology opportunities. It extends TOA by integrating diffusion of innovation theory and operationalizing its constructs to explain how opportunity spaces evolve. A seven-stage evolutionary model tracks how configurations emerge, diffuse and consolidate over time, identifying an opportunity window where configurations remain vacant, exploratory, emerging or promising. To investigate this perspective and respond to recent calls for generative AI in informetrics, the study develops an AI-enabled Tech Mining framework based on large-scale analysis of full-text scientific articles. ChatGPT-4o operates within an LLM+ architecture, combining prompt engineering with a rule-based expert system. The framework is benchmarked against expert coders, near-graduate students, a fine-tuned BERT classifier and alternative LLMs, and applied to 129,566 articles (2019–2024). The resulting dataset of 43,632 practices across 11 enabling technologies is analyzed using supervised machine learning to identify plausible vacant configurations. The study shows how controlled LLM workflows can make theory-informed opportunity analysis scalable and support a more managerial understanding of technology opportunities.

title: Analyzing Consumer Loyalty to Ultra‐Fast Fashion: An Integrative Analysis Based on the Stimulus‐Organism‐Response Model
abstract: ABSTRACT The ultra‐fast fashion industry generates massive online sales, partly because of its ability to attract the custom of Generation Z (Gen Z). Given that this generational cohort typically has low brand loyalty, this paper examines how the dimensions of the stimulus‐organism‐response (S‐O‐R) model explain Gen Z's loyalty to the ultra‐fast fashion industry. For this purpose, the analysis presented in this paper relies on both a linear and an evolutionary view of the S‐O‐R model. Based on data from 208 questionnaires completed by consumers of ultra‐fast fashion, two analytical phases were conducted: (1) partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) and (2) qualitative comparative analysis (QCA). The results of the first phase suggest that consumer sustainability consciousness is associated with brand loyalty directly and under mediation, whereas social media peer communication is associated with brand loyalty only under mediation by brand equity. The second phase shows the relevance of brand equity in explaining both high and low brand loyalty. The configurations explaining high brand loyalty or low brand loyalty show that the relationship of each outcome with consumer sustainability consciousness and social media peer communications reflects psychological mechanisms that allow consumers to overcome the cognitive dissonance between their attitudes and behavior.

title: EXPRESS: What if Society Collapses? Re-envisioning Management Scholarship through Radical Hope
abstract: Contemporary strategy and organization research rarely takes the possibility of systemic collapse, i.e. a path-dependent and irreversible breakdown of ecological and social systems, into account. Instead, it assumes that the world will endure in a recognizable form. In this essay, we question this assumption and ask what it would mean for strategy and organization scholarship if collapse were considered a real possibility. Drawing on Lear’s concept of radical hope in the face of cultural devastation, we argue that taking collapse seriously opens the possibility of rethinking the ontological, epistemological, and axiological foundations of our profession. We propose adopting a multifocal perspective inspired by radical hope to engage simultaneously with the dynamics of collapse in the present and with the uncertain forms of social organization that may emerge beyond it in our research, teaching and outreach activities.

Acupuncture for healthy-ageing-relevant outcomes in older cancer survivors: a scoping review with implications for future research and practice
abstract: Older cancer survivors face multidimensional challenges to healthy ageing and independence. Acupuncture has growing evidence for pain and symptom management, but its role in promoting healthy ageing remains unclear. This scoping review mapped evidence across four healthy-ageing-relevant domains, including physical function, psychological distress, cognition, and medication use, and identified knowledge gaps. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through June 30, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated acupuncture among adult cancer survivors; studies restricted to younger populations were excluded. Findings were extracted and narratively synthesized across the four domains. Of 986 records identified, 39 articles representing 37 studies were included. Most were randomized controlled trials (n = 21, 56.8%), and breast cancer was the most frequently studied (n = 22, 59.5%). Most studies assessed healthy-ageing-relevant outcomes as secondary outcomes in symptom-focused studies, with pain being the most common primary outcome (n = 9, 24.3%). No study specifically targeted older cancer survivors (age 65 or older). Physical function (n = 28, 75.7%) and psychological distress (n = 17, 45.9%) were the most frequently studied domains, whereas cognition (n = 8, 21.6%) and medication use (n = 10, 27.0%) were less frequently evaluated. Acupuncture showed promising improvements in functional outcomes and anxiety/depression compared with usual care or waitlist, whereas findings were more mixed with sham or active comparators and other outcomes. Acupuncture is promising to support healthy ageing related outcomes among cancer survivors; however, rigorous controlled clinical trials focusing on older adults are lacking. Future prospective trials focusing on addressing these important and novel outcomes will inform evidence-based integration of acupuncture for older adults impacted by cancer. Acupuncture may complement survivorship care to support healthy ageing, particularly by addressing functional limitations and psychological distress.

Bridge fuels and climate policy integration: The case of low-carbon hydrogen in the European Union
abstract: Hydrogen is central to climate neutrality in the European Union (EU), particularly in hard-to-abate sectors. The EU promotes fossil-based low-carbon hydrogen (LCH) as a bridge fuel supporting the development of a renewable hydrogen economy, despite risks of insufficient emission reductions and diverted investments. Climate policy integration (CPI) research has not addressed hydrogen and lacks a benchmark for bridge fuels. Earlier studies permitted a constrained role for natural gas, whereas recent work deems fossil fuels inherently incompatible with CPI, but without examining the transitional role of bridge fuels. Analyzing 182 legal acts and communications, this article provides the first systematic CPI assessment of the EU hydrogen framework. It provides a CPI benchmark for bridge fuels with three jointly necessary conditions (significant emission reductions, temporal limitation, support for target technologies), assessed through the thickness and quality of the policy mix across four indicators (policy goals, policy instruments for emission reductions, funding/financing, and procedural instruments). The hydrogen framework reaches a medium level of CPI. Its policy mix is thick but lacks quality, applying the conditions of bridge fuels only selectively. The framework thus commits neither to a net-zero pathway nor to an end date for fossil-based LCH. Conceptually, the article shows that the compatibility of fossil-based technologies with CPI depends on the climate policy paradigm underlying the benchmark. Under a purely emission-based decarbonization benchmark, they are not inherently incompatible with CPI. Where fossil-free alternatives exist, however, they should align with CPI only as temporally limited bridge fuels, following a defossilization paradigm.

Microbial Influence on Corrosive Processes at the Cast Iron-Bentonite Interface during 3.5 Years of Incubation at 37 and 70 °C
abstract: Abstract Bentonite-based geotechnical barriers constitute currently an integral part of international disposal concepts of high-level radioactive waste in claystone and crystalline rock. Elevated temperature, canister corrosion, and metabolic activity of microorganisms can influence their performance. To study these effects on processes at the cast iron-bentonite interface, microcosms were incubated with two different bentonites (B27 and GMZ-001), synthetic Opalinus Clay pore water with a high water-to-bentonite ratio and cast iron plates at 37 and 70 °C over a period of 3.5 years. No microorganisms or nutrients were added to those naturally occurring in the applied materials. Cast iron surfaces in contact with GMZ-001 bentonite appeared strongly corroded, and secondary layer-like structures formed at both temperatures. Furthermore, an accelerated release of iron into the pore water, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up were observed. In contrast, incubation with B27 bentonite at 37 °C resulted in less corroded cast iron surfaces covered with iron sulfides, which seemed to passivate the surface and led to lower iron release, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up. Respective B27 microcosms were dominated by metabolically active sulfate-reducing bacteria that induced iron sulfide formation. This study shows that the corrosion behavior of cast iron and changes in geochemical parameters like pH and pore water composition depend on the applied bentonite, naturally occurring microorganisms, and temperature.

title: Nonlinear Ozone-Phytoplankton-Sea-Ice Coupling Regulates Fine-Scale Gaseous Elemental Mercury Enhancement in the Arctic Marginal Ice Zone
abstract: Abstract Arctic marginal ice zone (MIZ) is a key summertime source of elevated atmospheric gaseous elemental mercury (GEM), but controls on its spatial variability remain unclear. Multiscale spatial statistics, machine learning, and quantile regression were applied to MOSAiC in situ observations (June-September 2020). GEM exhibits strong fine-scale spatial autocorrelation at 10 km (Moran’s I = 0.876). Random forest model (R2 = 0.85) with SHAP attribution identified ozone (O3), chlorophyll a (Chla), and open water fraction (OWF) as dominant GEM predictors. Quantile regression revealed that nonlinear coupling among OWF, Chla, and O3 strengthens under high GEM concentrations. By further combining spatial analysis with quantile regression modeling, a GEM-sensitive region was identified (OWF = 0.156–0.404, Chla = 1.17–1.57 μg/L, O3 = 9.2–19.7 ppb); within this region, both the O3 × Chla and O3 × OWF interactions exhibited significant positive correlations. The positive effect of O3 × Chla persists across all regions, while the O3 × OWF coupling varies dynamically with the retreat of sea ice. O3 indirectly favors GEM accumulation via regulating phytoplankton, and sea-ice melt exerts stage-dependent modulation of atmospheric oxidizing capacity. This study identifies O3 as a critical MIZ mercury regulator, and embedding O3-mediated pathways in models improves GEM projections under Arctic warming.

Predicting economies of scale in Brazilian municipal expenditure: Panel econometrics and interpretable machine learning
abstract: Municipal size is a persistent question in urban planning and public finance because small jurisdictions may face high per capita costs, whereas larger jurisdictions may face congestion and administrative complexity. This study compares panel econometric and interpretable machine-learning models for real municipal operational expenditure per capita in Brazil. The analysis uses 49,228 municipality-year observations for 5,568 municipalities from 2013 to 2021 and evaluates prediction through municipality-holdout, temporal-holdout, and state-block designs. Histogram Gradient Boosting performs best for unseen municipalities and held-out states, while a municipality fixed-effects-style predictor performs best for later-year prediction of municipalities already observed in the panel. The results indicate strong economies of scale among small municipalities followed by a broad low-cost range rather than one universal optimum. Controlled econometric and spatial-error models imply minima near 143,000 to 176,000 residents, while a reduced-form pooled OLS model excluding grants implies about 232,000 residents. The strongest boosting models show no clear interior upturn within the evaluated grid, with predicted expenditure remaining within 10% of the minimum above approximately 48,000 to 53,000 residents. Grouped SHAP results rank population first, followed by grants and local economic capacity. Residual Moran tests show that unexplained expenditure differences remain spatially clustered. The findings support spatially informed expenditure benchmarking and caution against consolidation policies based on one fixed population threshold.

A decision support framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration through process-based ecosystem modeling and optimization
abstract: Wetland restoration is increasingly recognized as a nature-based climate solution, but effective planning requires balancing nonlinear ecological responses with economic and implementation constraints. We propose a conceptual and computational framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration that embeds process-based ecosystem modeling within restoration optimization. Restoration strategies are represented as portfolios combining discrete intervention choices with continuous decisions on implementation intensity and spatial allocation. A vertically resolved ecohydrological model simulates soil organic carbon dynamics and decomposition-driven CO$_2$ and CH$_4$ emissions, allowing environmental outcomes to arise from the interaction between restoration decisions and ecosystem processes.The framework is illustrated through a benchmark analysis and an application to the Ebro Delta. The benchmark shows that alternative objective specifications select distinct interior and corner solutions from the same ecological trade-off. In the Ebro Delta application, imposing a budget constraint reallocates restored area from the deep-rooted vegetation type toward the less expensive shallow-rooted type, while maintaining high vegetation densities and compliance with the methane target, although the CO$_2$ target is exceeded. Global sensitivity analysis identifies the density and spatial allocation of the deep-rooted vegetation type as the main drivers of restoration performance.The results show that restoration outcomes depend not only on total vegetation cover but also on portfolio composition and implementation intensity. The proposed framework provides a flexible methodology for integrating process-based ecological models into restoration planning under alternative environmental objectives and resource constraints.

title: Seasonal ice cover regulates the environmental fate and retention of nano-TiO2 in freshwater lakes
Maintenance matters: Insights from guidelines and practice on nature-based stormwater solutions
abstract: Nature-based stormwater solutions (NBSS) support urban stormwater management while providing additional ecosystem services. Their hybrid grey–green design sets them apart from conventional drainage systems requiring specific maintenance to ensure long-term performance. This study combines a global practitioner survey and a review of maintenance guidelines aiming to characterize shortcomings in NBSS management, focusing on failure mechanisms and maintenance practices. Based on 22 responses, survey results show that, in the absence of maintenance, systems are mainly affected by sediment buildup, litter, and green waste accumulation, as well as excessive vegetation growth, and invasive species. Maintenance (e.g., visual inspections, litter removal) is performed regularly, from monthly to annually, consistent with guidelines. Vegetation management typically follows a seasonal frequency (∼three months). Our review of 35 guidelines indicates that maintenance practices are very diverse and context-dependent, depending on the type of NBSS and socio-ecological-technological context, reflecting a potential barrier to mainstreaming of best practices. No universal maintenance frequency can be established as it strongly depends on NBBS and local context (e.g., climate, available resources). Systematic data collection on failures, their occurrence, and impacts is however essential to support predictive local maintenance strategy.

title: Bismuth-based photocatalysts for sustainable water remediation and solar hydrogen generation: State-of-the-art and future directions
abstract: The rapid increase in environmental pollution and global energy demand has intensified the search for sustainable technologies capable of simultaneously addressing wastewater contamination and clean fuel generation. Photocatalysis has emerged as a promising strategy because it utilizes solar energy to drive redox reactions under mild operating conditions. Among various photocatalytic materials, bismuth-based photocatalysts have attracted significant attention due to their narrow band gaps, excellent visible-light absorption, layered crystal structures, chemical stability, and tuneable electronic properties. The review discusses the structural and functional characteristics of major bismuth-based systems. Emphasis is placed on advanced modification strategies such as heterojunction construction, metal/non-metal doping, and oxygen-vacancy defect regulation, all of which significantly improve charge separation efficiency, light harvesting and surface reaction kinetics. Recent ternary and Z-scheme systems have demonstrated excellent capability for degrading organic pollutants while concurrently enhancing hydrogen production rates under visible-light irradiation. The review further analyzes the photocatalytic mechanisms governing reactive oxygen species generation, interfacial charge migration and proton reduction pathways. Despite major progress, several limitations remain, including photo-corrosion, charge recombination, low quantum efficiency and challenges in scaling laboratory results to practical reactors. Future perspectives highlight defect-controlled nanostructures, noble-metal-free cocatalysts, real wastewater applications and pilot-scale solar reactor development. Overall, bismuth-based photocatalysts offer strong potential as multifunctional materials for integrating environmental remediation with renewable hydrogen production, supporting the transition toward sustainable energy and water treatment technologies.

Dual Regulation of Monomer Transport Enables Ultrahigh Mg2+/Li+ Selectivity in Polyamide Nanofiltration Membranes
abstract: Abstract Nanofiltration membranes are promising for lithium recovery from salt-lake brines, yet their Mg2+/Li+ separation performance can be further improved. Here, we present an organic-phase engineering strategy that systematically tailors the carbon-chain length of alkane solvents, from n-hexane (C6) to 2-methylundecane (C12), to simultaneously regulate piperazine enrichment at the water–organic interface and trimesoyl chloride diffusion kinetics. This dual regulation transforms conventional rapid and random interfacial polymerization into a more confined and homogeneous growth process. The resulting polyamide membranes exhibit a reduced negative surface charge and a narrower and more uniform pore-size distribution. These structural features substantially enhance Mg2+/Li+ separation, with the C12 membrane achieving a Mg2+/Li+ selectivity of up to 306.6 in the mixed-salt solutions. To assess performance under realistic conditions, a two-pass nanofiltration process was evaluated using simulated salt-lake brine. The C12 membrane increased lithium purity from 2.4% to 97.7% while reducing the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio from 40 to 0.024. This study provides new insight into the kinetic regulation of interfacial polymerization through organic-phase engineering and demonstrates an effective membrane design strategy for high-selectivity lithium extraction from complex brines.

title: Novel Multi-Isotope Am and Cm Signatures Trace Temporal Changes in Nuclear Inputs in a Baltic Sediment Core
abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic radionuclides have been present in the environment since 1945 due to civil and military uses of nuclear energy. This study represents an extensive characterization of Am and Cm isotopes (241Am, 242mAm, 243Am, 244Cm, 245Cm, 246Cm), and 237Np, in a Baltic Sea sediment core directly impacted by discharges from the Studsvik nuclear research facility (Sweden). Distinct isotopic signatures were identified throughout the sediment core, enabling discrimination between inputs from atmospheric nuclear weapons testing (1952–1965), Sweden’s nuclear-weapons-related activities during the 1970s, and subsequent releases associated with civil nuclear-energy development. The findings demonstrate that higher actinides provide powerful isotopic fingerprints for resolving complex nuclear contamination histories and attributing release sources in environmental archives. This study further establishes the utility of actinide isotopic tracers beyond U and Pu and presents the first environmental application of the 243Am/241Am ratio in a system with well-constrained inputs from distinct nuclear sources.

Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating
abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth’s core. Here we use a new high-pressure method – microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells – to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 μ Ω cm measurement of liquid iron’s resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today’s lowermost mantle is fully solid.

title: The Interplay of Green Intellectual Capital, Artificial Intelligence, Frugal Innovation, and Triple Bottom Line Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT The study analyzes the critical role of green intellectual capital (GIC) in enhancing SMEs' economic, social, and environmental performance, with frugal innovation (FI) mediating these relationships. The study also investigates the moderating effect of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption on the relationship between GIC and FI. The hypotheses were tested using PLS‐SEM. Data were collected from 318 manufacturing SMEs operating in three Pakistani cities. Our findings indicate that GIC significantly influences firms' economic, social, and environmental performance in an emerging economy and that FI mediates these relationships. Furthermore, AI adoption strengthens the relationship between GIC and FI. To our knowledge, no previous study has systematically examined GIC, FI, and AI adoption alongside economic, social, and environmental performance, particularly in the context of manufacturing SMEs in an emerging Asian economy. First, this study examines the mediating role of FI in the relationship between GIC and triple bottom line (TBL) performance. Second, it analyzes the moderating role of AI adoption in the relationship between GIC and FI, highlighting the role of technology adoption in strengthening this relationship. Finally, it extends the resource‐based view (RBV) to a technological context by examining how GIC, FI, and AI adoption affect TBL performance.

title: Greenhushing as Strategic Adaptation: Net‐Zero Commitment Retreat Among S&P 500 Firms Amid Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Backlash
abstract: ABSTRACT Greenhushing has emerged as a strategic corporate response to political and regulatory uncertainty, yet less is known about how firms recalibrate previously established sustainability signals when external conditions change. Drawing on signaling theory, this study examines changes in corporate climate and ESG commitments during the political transition to the second Trump administration. Using qualitative content analysis of corporate disclosures and public communications, we identify 32 large US firms that modified, weakened, or withdrew previously stated commitments between September 2024 and August 2025. Among these firms, 13 (41%) were associated with political or regulatory pressure, 8 (25%) linked changes to rising AI and data‐center demand, and 11 (34%) pointed to profit‐driven refocusing, market uncertainty, or broader regulatory ambiguity. The findings reveal clear sectoral differences in how firms recalibrated sustainability signals. Financial institutions exhibited the most direct and visible retrenchment, particularly through withdrawals from net‐zero alliances and changes in ESG‐related communication. Technology firms more often retained long‐term climate commitments while reducing the visibility, prominence, or certainty of interim targets. Other sectors showed less visible but still consequential forms of retreat, including target modification and the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) delisting. Case studies of BlackRock, Meta, and Microsoft further identify three distinct pathways of greenhushing: politically induced retrenchment, selective undercommunication amid rising emissions, and more cautious or conditional sustainability signaling in response to reputational and regulatory risk.

title: Business Responses to Competing Institutional Logics in the Climate Change Field: An Experiment
abstract: ABSTRACT We examine how competing institutional logics shape corporate responses to climate change. We theorize the climate change field as a competitive issue field where a dominant market logic of short‐term profit maximization confronts an emerging environmental logic prioritizing emissions reduction. We model shareholders as carriers of normative and coercive forces and competitors as carriers of mimetic forces, and test four hypotheses through a vignette experiment. Participants predicted the amount an oil and gas manager would invest in reducing emissions. Results show that environmental logic consistently increases expected emissions‐reduction investments relative to market logic. When shareholders' and competitors' logics conflict, participants expect managers to follow shareholders rather than competitors. Adding divestment threats as a coercive force did not produce a statistically detectable incremental effect beyond normative pressure alone. We identify shareholder‐expressed environmental logic as a potentially important lever for organizational decarbonization, creating opportunity for future research to examine its practical impact.

title: Integrating Sustainability and Resilience in Multinational Supply Chains: Evidence From Post‐COVID‐19 Strategic Adaptation in Singapore
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainability and resilience have become central strategic concerns in contemporary supply chains, yet their integration remains insufficiently understood in empirical research. Existing studies show that the relationship between resilience and sustainability is neither uniformly complementary nor uniformly conflictive but depends on the practices and decisions under consideration. This study examines how multinational companies in Singapore integrated sustainability and resilience into their supply chain strategies during and after the COVID‐19 disruption. Drawing on sensemaking as the theoretical lens and an abductive grounded‐theory approach, we conducted in‐depth interviews with senior supply chain professionals from multinational companies operating in Singapore. The findings identify five interrelated strategic domains through which firms redesigned supply chains after disruption: supply chain focus and visibility, inventory and sourcing, collaboration and communication, technology integration, and sustainability orientation. Rather than treating sustainability as a separate concern, managers linked it to supplier configuration, nearshoring and local sourcing decisions, information sharing, technology‐enabled visibility, and longer‐term partnership development. At the same time, the evidence indicates persistent tensions between efficiency and buffering, flexibility and standardization, and short‐term continuity and longer‐term sustainability commitments, consistent with recent work on sustainability–resilience trade‐offs in crisis settings. This study contributes to the emerging literature on sustainable supply chain resilience by showing how managers interpret disruption, navigate complementarities and trade‐offs, and integrate resilience and sustainability within Singapore's highly trade‐dependent and regionally connected multinational supply‐chain environment. It also offers practical insight into how firms can align resilience‐building with broader business and environmental strategies.

title: Social determinants and poly-victimization among street-connected children in South Asia: A scoping review
Planting Density Effect on Soil Functions With Specific Response to Rhizobacteria in Drought‐Prone Maize Field in the Yunnan Plateau
abstract: ABSTRACT Soil multifunctionality (SMF) governs terrestrial biogeochemical cycles and ecosystem services, yet whether belowground SMF exhibits saturating density‐dependent responses analogous to the aboveground constant final yield law remains unclear. In a two‐year field experiment across five planting densities (D1–D5) in drought‐prone maize farmland on the Yunnan Plateau, we found that SMF displayed a distinct nonlinear saturating response. It increased sharply at low‐to‐moderate densities (D1–D3) before reaching an intrinsic saturation plateau at higher densities (D3–D5). This pattern extends the constant final yield law from plant productivity to soil biogeochemical functioning. Notably, plant growth‐promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) inoculation did not alter this saturating trajectory but instead elevated the saturation plateau. PGPR resulted in negligible effects at low‐to‐moderate densities yet increased SMF by 472% and 957% at high densities (D4 and D5), respectively. Mechanistically, PGPR restructured bacterial communities under the high‐density conditions by enhancing α‐diversity, which optimized taxonomic composition and increased co‐occurrence network complexity. Concurrently, it boosted extracellular enzyme activities and the functional potential of carbon‐ and phosphorus‐cycling processes while maintaining functional redundancy. We conclude that planting density sets the baseline saturation threshold of SMF, whereas PGPR acts as a modulator that raises the saturation ceiling without overriding the underlying density‐driven pattern.

title: Half‐Century Loss and Transformation: Dramatic Spatio‐Temporal Evolution of China's Tidal Wetlands Ecosystem Revealed by Satellite Observations (1972–2025)
abstract: ABSTRACT Anthropogenic activities and natural processes have accelerated the degradation of China's coastal tidal wetlands in recent decades. Quantifying long‐term spatio‐temporal evolution of these wetlands is critical for informing coastal conservation. While prior studies have documented spatio‐temporal evolution in China's tidal wetlands, a comprehensive analysis spanning China's entire coastline over a half‐century period (1972–2025) remains unquantified. Therefore, in this study, by leveraging long‐term Landsat images (1972–2025) and a frequency statistics method, we quantified the evolutionary trajectories of tidal wetlands over the period 1972–2025 from macro‐scale to micro‐scale. Results showed that: (1) China's existing tidal wetlands covered an area of 8995 km 2 in 2025, primarily located in the coastal provinces of Jiangsu, Shandong, Liaoning, and Fujian. Spatially, their distribution showed a marked north–south disparity, with greater coverage in the northern regions. (2) From 1972 to 2025, China's tidal wetlands had experienced a substantial net loss of 45%. Tidal wetlands' area had decreased in all coastal provinces and municipalities except Shanghai, with Tianjin showing the most dramatic reduction (78%). Furthermore, landward boundaries had demonstrated significantly greater change intensity than seaward margins. (3) The tidal wetlands of the Jiangsu Radial Sand Ridges had maintained relatively stable areal extents and experienced slow spatial changes. In contrast, the tidal wetlands of Bohai Bay had shown substantial reductions in total area. Concurrently, their landward boundaries had undergone progressive seaward shifts, fragmenting once‐contiguous wetlands into isolated patches, while seaward boundaries had been alternately influenced by erosion and sedimentation processes. This study provides a robust scientific foundation for evidence‐based management and strategic planning of coastal zones in China.

Private debt versus bank debt in corporate borrowing
abstract: Using administrative bank loan-level data matched to private debt deals, we study the interaction between private and bank debt for a large segment of dual borrowers. These firms use private debt for investment and bank credit lines for liquidity insurance. Private debt carries higher spreads and commonly features flexible, equity-like terms that are associated with greater reliance on bank credit lines. Relative to bank-only borrowers, dual borrowers obtain more and larger credit lines and draw them more intensively following liquidity shocks. Our findings suggest that private debt substitutes for bank term loans but complements banks’ provision of liquidity through credit lines.

title: Tax evasion at the top of the income distribution
abstract: We study tax evasion at the top of the U.S. income distribution using micro-data from audits and enforcement initiatives. Leveraging enforcement that revealed noncompliance, we find that recent individual random audit data fail to capture sophisticated evasion via offshore accounts and pass-through businesses. Consequently, estimates based solely on these data under-state evasion by the highest-income Americans. We construct new distributional estimates of US noncompliance. Circa 2006–2013, accounting for sophisticated evasion (holding estimated non-sophisticated evasion fixed) increases the share of unreported income belonging to the top 1% of the distribution by 9 to 33 percentage points.

title: Constructing Hybrid Futures: Fossil-Green Interpath Governance in a Global South Resource Periphery
abstract: Amid accelerating environmental crises, economic geography has increasingly turned to green path development. Yet existing research underplays how actors strategically shape the coevolution of fossil and green paths, particularly in Global South resource peripheries where industrial trajectories emerge simultaneously. This article advances the interpath linkages framework by examining how actors govern interpath relations during the critical phase of resource mobilization. It makes three distinct conceptual contributions. First, it embeds interpath dynamics within a Global South perspective, conceptualizing how triple structural pressures (foreign leverage, developmental stress, and efficiency imperatives) reshape resource formation beyond Western-centric transition models. Second, to understand how industrial futures are negotiated, it introduces the framework of interpath governance, capturing how path advocates, systemic actors, and hybrid firm actors deploy antagonistic and moderating modes of agency across spatial scales to assemble, neutralize, or contest interpath linkages. Third, it unveils concrete strategies through which interpath dynamics unfold in investment, market, knowledge, and legitimacy arenas. Developed through qualitative research in Namibia, where major offshore oil discoveries coincide with ambitious green hydrogen initiatives, the findings demonstrate how interpath governance operates under acute context pressures to harmonize seemingly opposing industrial futures. Overall, the article advances an agency-centered understanding of fossil-green co-evolution, highlights how interpath governance shapes hybrid energy trajectories, and thus contributes to debates on green path creation and the structural constraints on sustainability transitions in a Global South resource periphery.

Countercyclical Risk Aversion: Evidence from 10 Million Auto Insurance Transactions in China
abstract: A fundamental idea in modern asset pricing is that risk aversion may be time varying and countercyclical (Campbell and Cochrane, 1999). Existing evidence is relatively scant and based mostly either on experimental/survey data or on stock market data directly. We aim to test this key assumption using a large panel of real-world transaction data. Risk aversion is imputed from Chinese auto insurance policies, including 10 million transactions from 2011 to 2017. We find that individuals' risk aversion is indeed time varying and countercyclical. The risk aversion measure behaves reasonably and also exhibits seasonal, "zodiac year," and calendar-event patterns.

title: U.S. Banks’ Exposures to Climate Transition Risks
abstract: Abstract We propose a new approach to estimate banks’ credit exposures to transition risks that combines sectoral effects of climate policies from general equilibrium (GE) models with historical information on loans’ default risks. At worst, estimated exposures reach 14% of bank loan portfolio values. Accounting for historic loan payoff structures reduces exposures to 0.5%–2%. Exposures can increase by 3–5 percentage points due to aggregate economic shocks. Analyses surrounding climate transition events suggest our estimates can serve as an upper bound on banks’ transition risk exposures. Highlighting our measure’s novelty, emissions explain at most 60% of variation in banks’ exposures.

Performance Incentives in Education
abstract: Abstract We conduct a field experiment studying how financial incentives for meeting grade-based performance goals affect university students. We find that incentives reduce performance, particularly among low-ability students assigned ambitious goals. Survey data suggest this arises from a mismatch between assigned goals and ability: incentives distort expectations and reference points, moving students away from the performance targets they would otherwise set for themselves. The negative effects are concentrated among groups with the largest distortions. Allowing students to choose their goals mitigates negative effects but does not eliminate them. Our results caution against incentives in education and identify a novel backfiring mechanism.

title: Peer Effects in Labor Market Training
abstract: This paper shows that group composition shapes the effectiveness of labor market training programs for jobseekers. Using rich administrative data from Germany and a novel measure of employability, I find that participants benefit from greater average exposure to highly employable peers through increased long-term employment and earnings. The effects vary significantly by own employability: jobseekers with a low employability experience larger long-term gains, whereas highly employable individuals benefit primarily in the short term through higher entry wages. An analysis of mechanisms suggests that within-group competition in job search attenuates part of the positive effects that operate through knowledge spillovers.

title: The Effect of Retirement on Mental Health
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we disentangle the total local average treatment effect of retirement on mental health among elderly women in Europe into the indirect effect mediated through grandparental childcare and the direct effect through all other mechanisms. Applying a semiparametric estimation strategy, our estimates point to a positive direct effect of retirement on mental health and a negative indirect effect through grandparental childcare that partially offsets these gains. The results highlight the usefulness of causal mediation studies for policy analysis and illustrate the importance of allowing for full effect heterogeneity in settings with treatment-mediator relationships.

title: Beyond the Enrollment Gap
abstract: Abstract High-achieving, low-income students persist in higher education at lower rates than their high-income peers, raising questions about what drives these post-enrollment gaps. Most financial aid research examines the U.S. setting, despite many countries combining modest tuition with living cost support. I study a generous French merit-and-need grant using a regression discontinuity design. Because eligibility is communicated too late to affect enrollment, I can cleanly identify effects on already-enrolled students. I find precisely estimated null effects on persistence, degree completion, and graduate degree enrollment. These results suggest that high-achieving students may be less sensitive to financial aid than lower performing peers.

title: Resource‐driven agricultural clusters: Coagglomeration effects of the High Plains Aquifer
abstract: Abstract Quantifying the regional economic impacts of crop production is critical for assessing the broader implications of access to natural resources and government policies. However, most existing estimates rely on input–output models with restrictive assumptions, and competing theories of economic mechanisms provide little guidance on the sign or magnitude. We estimate local economic spillovers by exploiting a large increase in crop production that occurred due to the expansion of irrigation in counties overlying the High Plains Aquifer after World War II. While crop production was directly impacted by access to groundwater, we find that livestock product sales also increased significantly, reaching a 235% increase in sales compared to counties outside the aquifer. The primary spillover to non‐farm sectors was an increase in sales in the wholesale sector, perhaps driven by sales of agricultural‐related products. These findings provide evidence of coagglomeration incentives, where clusters of agricultural industries find it optimal to produce within the same region.

title: Climate Risk Exposure and European Banking Sector: A Forward‐Looking Transition Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether banks' financial vulnerability and characteristics predict their future climate‐transition risk exposure. Using the Climate Risk (CRISK) methodology of Jung et al. (2025) for 126 listed European banks over 2007–2024, it shows that financial vulnerability captured by Systemic Risk has weak power to predict climate vulnerability, while significant predictive relationships emerge among smaller, Less Significant Institutions and during financial distress. An event study of the 2022 Climate Stress Test announcement by the European Central Bank suggests a dampening effect on climate‐transition risk among Supervised banks. The evidence indicates that climate vulnerability extends beyond fragility measures.

title: Consistency of MLEs for partially observed diffusions, with application in market microstructure modelling
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a tractable sufficient condition for the consistency of maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs) in partially observed diffusion models, stated in terms of the stationary distribution of the associated fully observed diffusion, under the assumption that the set of unknown parameter values is finite. This sufficient condition is then verified in the context of a latent price model of market microstructure, yielding consistency of maximum likelihood estimators of the unknown parameters in this model. Finally, we compute the latter estimators using historical financial data taken from the NASDAQ exchange.

Moral behavior and polarization
abstract: Abstract An individual that follows partial Kantian universalization polarizes and overdraws its strategy in order to compensate for those individuals that she thinks do not choose the same strategy as she does. Within a generalized Alger-Weibull approach with heterogenous homo moralis individuals, the present paper is the first to formalize this polarization incentive. We show that the polarization incentive can be drawn back to an implicit and so far unknown ’preference for dominance’. Applying our new insights to a public good game it turns out that total public good provision may be reduced by an increase in the degree of morality.
