Bypassed Environmental Impact Assessment: quantitative and qualitative evidence of biodiversity loss in French land-use projects
abstract: Environmental impact assessment (EIA) is an essential instrument for anticipating and mitigating the ecological effects of development projects before they are authorized. Yet when national jurisdictions make these assessments contingent on technical parameters such as surface-based thresholds, some projects are deemed insignificant regardless of their ecological context. In this paper, we ask what proportion of projects consuming natural land in mainland France undergo an effective assessment. Combining spatial analysis of 14,915 planning permits issued in 2022 and 2023 with national land cover data, and comparing eligible projects with the opinions and decisions issued by environmental authorities, we estimate that approximately 89% of permits are granted without any project-level environmental assessment, and that permits not subject to systematic EIA collectively account for over 33% of the natural and semi-natural surfaces consumed over the study period. The open and semi-open land cover class, which includes the grassland and heath formations that are among the most rapidly declining ecosystems in Europe, is the class most exposed to these authorizations. A directed content analysis of ten complete screening dossiers identifies five recurring argumentative patterns in prefectural reasoning. A regionally stratified random sample of 100 screening decisions establishes their prevalence: all five recur, 77% of exemption decisions mobilize at least three of them, and 94% contain no substantive treatment of cumulative effects or connectivity. These results show that neither systematic thresholds nor the case-by-case screening procedure functions as an effective ecological filter, and argue for an assessment grounded in ecological context and governed by transparent and documented criteria.

title: Structural decoupling in China's environmental damage-assessment standard system: a dual-network diagnosis of governance lock-in risks
Reclamation Period and Straw Type Alter Soil Organic Carbon Composition via CAZyme Families in Coal Mine Agroecosystems
abstract: ABSTRACT Soil organic carbon (SOC) stabilization is crucial for effective ecological restoration in coal‐mining areas, yet the mechanisms underlying straw‐mediated carbon sequestration remain poorly understood. This study investigated how equal‐carbon but different‐mass incorporation of maize (S + M) and wheat (S + W) straw incorporation, across reclamation chronosequences (1, 10, 30 years; R1, R10, R30), associates with SOC composition, microbial communities, and carbohydrate‐active enzymes (CAZymes). Results showed that straw type and its input mass, together with reclamation duration, significantly shaped SOC dynamics. The S + W treatment under long‐term restoration (R30) yielded the highest content of both labile (14.93 g·kg −1 ) and recalcitrant (2.55 g·kg −1 ) SOC. Specifically, S + W preferentially enriched recalcitrant SOC, whereas S + M enhanced labile SOC components. These shifts were associated with distinct microbial community structures and CAZymes profiles. Co‐occurrence network analysis revealed tighter microbial interactions in early restoration (R1). Notably, methyl carbon was identified as the primary driver of community assembly, strongly linked to the abundances of Ascomycota, Chloroflexi, and Firmicutes. Our findings demonstrate that reclamation period and straw type with differential input mass potentially mediate SOC stability via microbial‐mediated pathways, highlighting the importance of targeted straw management, particularly wheat straw in long‐term restoration, for enhancing carbon sequestration in reclaimed mining ecosystems.

title: Channeled Attention and Stable Errors
abstract: Abstract People persist in mistaken beliefs even in settings with high stakes, abundant data, and repeated opportunities to learn—settings where standard arguments imply they should correct their errors. We develop an attention-based framework for understanding why errors persist. When a person channels his attention through the lens of his potentially misspecified model, exposure to data is not the same as tracking the statistics necessary to tell him his model is wrong. A model is attentionally stable when the data the person deems relevant will, in the long run, fail to make the model look implausible. Models that erroneously rule things out—e.g., beliefs that a variable doesn’t matter or that a distinction doesn’t exist—tend to be attentionally stable because they divert attention away from data that would refute the models. Conversely, models that erroneously rule things in are less likely to be stable. Whether an error is discovered depends on the structure of the decision problem but is not tightly linked to its level of harm; arbitrarily costly errors can persist while trivially inexpensive ones may be detected. Nevertheless, no error is robust both to changes in the decision environment and to shocks that expand attention: every channeled-attention error is vulnerable to some perturbation that would reveal it. We use the framework to analyze the stability of psychological biases and empirical misconceptions, as well as to explain why fresh eyes catch mistakes, why people use overly coarse rather than overly fine categorizations, and why people recognize errors in others that they miss in themselves.

title: When Insurers Exit: Climate Losses, Fragile Insurers, and Mortgage Markets
abstract: Abstract This paper uses a range of natural experiments to show how mispricing of climate risk in mortgages and property insurance creates large taxpayer exposures and leads to excess credit flows to risky areas. Our central finding is that the government-sponsored enterprises’ (GSEs) policies for evaluating property insurers are a crucial source of this mispricing. We assemble a comprehensive new dataset on both mortgages and insurance to analyze these dynamics in Florida from 2009-2018. We begin by documenting a breakdown in the quality of insurance provision, with new under-capitalized and under-diversified insurers dominating insurance markets. These fragile insurers have high rates of insolvency, which we show causally increases mortgage defaults after natural disasters. We find that the GSEs’ reliance on third-party ratings of insurers leads them to accept insurance from companies at high risk of insolvency without pricing for it. This creates large taxpayer exposures, with an estimated 25% of the GSEs’ expected losses in Florida coming from insurance fragility. Most starkly, we show that private lenders strategically respond to the GSE mispricing. Mortgage denial rates are sensitive to insurance quality in the jumbo segment where loans are retained, but not in the conforming segment where loans are offloaded to the GSEs. This suggests that, all else equal, fewer conforming mortgages would have been originated if lenders screened insurance fragility as they do in jumbos.

title: The Children's Climate Vulnerability Index: An Integrated Approach to Assessing Climate Risk—Evidence From India
abstract: ABSTRACT Children are particularly vulnerable to climate‐related risks due to their biological sensitivity, their dependence on societal systems, and their limited ability to adapt to the stressors posed by the environment. This study assesses the climate risk and the resulting vulnerability of children at the state level in India with the Children's Climate Vulnerability Index (CCVI). Drawing on the IPCC vulnerability framework, the index combines measures of household‐reported and perceived climatic and environmental exposure, child‐specific sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. The CCVI is applied to four Indian states—Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand—that represent different climatic regimes and socioeconomic contexts. Results show substantial variation in children's climate vulnerability despite similar levels of exposure; sensitivity is the main driver of vulnerability in all states. Health, nutrition, and education‐related sensitivities consistently outweigh the impact of climatic hazards, while adaptive capacity has limited power to offset these pressures. By linking vulnerability patterns to child development outcomes, the study shows that children's climate risk is shaped more by developmental and institutional conditions than by hazard intensity alone. The findings underscore the need for child‐focused, multi‐sectoral adaptation strategies that combine action with health, nutrition, education, and social protection policies.

title: The Effect of News‐Based Measures of Biodiversity Exposure on Corporate Green Revenue Disclosure
abstract: ABSTRACT Biodiversity loss has emerged as a significant challenge for firms. As firms face increasing pressure from stakeholders to address nature‐related risks, green revenue disclosure has become a potentially important strategic means of communicating environmentally oriented business activities. Using 12,055 firm‐year observations from S&P 1500 firms from 2005 to 2023, this study examines whether and when a firm with biodiversity exposure (defined as a news‐based measure of biodiversity exposure risk based on textual analyses of 10‐K statements) is associated with green revenue disclosure. The study finds that firms with biodiversity exposure are more likely to disclose green revenue. However, this likelihood masks substantial variation; the negative association emerges with environmental investment. In firms with higher corporate social responsibility (CSR) committees, stronger CSR external audit practices, and environmental partnerships, biodiversity‐exposed firms are associated with greater green revenue disclosure, consistent with the view that continuous CSR monitoring strongly affects such disclosure. The study then traces the consequences of this green revenue disclosure pattern and finds that predicted green revenue reporting is meaningful for reducing the overall cost of capital and improving a firm's efficiency. This study contributes to emerging biodiversity literature by showing that biodiversity exposure is not directly associated with green revenue disclosure; rather, its effect depends on environmental accountability, partnerships, and investment.

title: Burnout as evaluative imbalance: pluralising worth in performance management systems
Experience and quality of life: Future research agenda
Family Firm Origin and Corporate Social Responsibility Decoupling
abstract: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue Why does the extent of decoupling between corporate social responsibility (CSR) disclosure and actual CSR performance vary across family firms? Drawing on the imprinting theory, this study investigates whether and how the initial institutional imprints rooted in family firm origin affect firms' CSR decoupling. Research Findings/Insights We find that family firms restructured from state‐owned enterprises (SOEs) engage in less CSR decoupling than those founded through entrepreneurial activities. Mechanism analyses reveal that restructured family firms (RFFs) exhibit superior corporate governance relative to entrepreneurial family firms (EFFs), indicating that institutional imprints are essential mechanisms for interpreting disparities in family firms' CSR decoupling. However, differences in resource endowments, political connections, and founders' competencies do not appear to account for this gap. Additionally, greater internal ownership balance and executive team recomposition attenuate the influence of these imprints, thereby narrowing the difference in CSR decoupling between RFFs and EFFs. Theoretical/Academic Implications This study identifies organizational origin as an enduring source of behavioral heterogeneity among family firms. The finding extends imprinting theory by demonstrating that governance arrangements inherited from predecessor organizations can persist after ownership restructuring and shape subsequent CSR practices. The study also advances CSR decoupling research by providing an origin‐based explanation for gaps between CSR disclosure and CSR performance. Practitioner/Policy Implications This study provides practical guidance for firms' managers on strengthening formal institutional arrangements. It also offers insights for regulators and policymakers on promoting substantive CSR activities and ensuring reliable and transparent CSR disclosure.

title: The Ethics of Employability: Accountability, Justice, and Responsibility in Racialised Graduate Labour Markets
abstract: Abstract Persistent racialised inequalities continue to shape graduate outcomes in the United Kingdom, despite decades of policy reform, institutional initiatives, and employability-focussed interventions. Racially minoritised graduates consistently experience ethnic penalties in hiring, earnings, and career progression, even when controlling for educational attainment and institutional prestige, with UK-born and international racially minoritised graduates facing structurally distinct but compounding forms of disadvantage. Yet, dominant employability frameworks have positioned employability as an individual responsibility, centred on skills, capitals, and adaptability, thereby obscuring the structural injustices embedded in higher education and labour markets. This paper reframes employability as an ethical domain of pressing importance for both higher education and business ethics. Drawing on an integrated theoretical architecture comprising normative foundations of justice (distributive, procedural, recognition, and epistemic), race-centred lenses (Critical Race Theory, intersectionality, and Bourdieu’s theory of capitals), an accountability spine, and the capabilities approach, it develops the Ethical Employability Framework (race-centred), which redistributes responsibility across universities, employers, and the state within the UK. The framework exposes how employability discourses can function as a form of “misframing”, legitimising inequality by shifting responsibility onto graduates while neglecting systemic exclusion. The paper’s theoretical contributions are hierarchically organised: it reframes employability as an ethical construct; integrates race as a constitutive theoretical concern through a race-centred explanatory architecture; develops an accountability spine that operationalises shared institutional responsibility; adopts the capabilities approach as the evaluative standard for substantive flourishing; and maps these elements into a coherent multi-level framework connecting normative theory to institutional practice. In doing so, the paper advances a justice-oriented agenda for employability scholarship, policy, and practice that places racially minoritised graduates at its centre.

title: Job Demands‐Resources, Well‐Being and Work‐Life Boundaries: The Pervasiveness of Social Networking Platforms
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper integrates job demands‐resources theory with boundary theory to advance theoretical understanding of the pervasiveness of work‐oriented social networking (SN) and its implications for HRM. Drawing on rich qualitative interviews with 67 managers, we highlight the impact of work‐oriented SN on job demands, resources, work‐life boundaries, and well‐being. The findings extend HRM scholarship on well‐being and job demands, boundary management and social media, by revealing three dimensions of work‐life boundary‐blurring in work‐oriented SN contexts: professional‐personal, accessibility‐inaccessibility, and control‐autonomy. The findings generate practical recommendations for aligning SN practices, well‐being policies, and informal cultural norms.

title: How Can Talent Managers Create Organizational Value Throughout the Hype Cycles of Emerging and Innovative Industries?
abstract: ABSTRACT Talent managers in emerging industries face a distinctive challenge: they must build and reconfigure talent management (TM) systems to build organizational value while stakeholder expectations, legitimacy, regulation, and capital availability continually fluctuate. Drawing on interviews with 14 experienced executives across the emerging Canadian recreational cannabis and solar industries, media and scholarly related industry research, we examine how TM challenges and responses vary across hype cycle inflection points. Extending Makram et al.’s (2017) talent value framework into a dynamic industry context, we theorize hype cycle inflection points as an organizing mechanism for talent architectures in emerging industries. Our findings show that TM value processes are temporally reweighted as industries move from innovation trigger to inflated expectations, through disillusionment, and toward stabilization. We contribute to HRM/TM scholarship by showing that talent architectures in hype‐driven emerging industries are not best understood as fixed bundles of best practices or as universal organizational stages, but as contingent configurations that must be rebalanced as external expectations, legitimacy, regulation, and resource availability change. We further identify stage‐specific talent logics: rapid capability acquisition, accelerated scaling, defensive stabilization, capability consolidation, and strategic optimization. The findings advance research on contextualized TM, temporal dynamics, and organizational value by explaining when and why different forms of talent become strategically valuable in emerging industries.

title: A Psychometric Evaluation of Single‐Item Measures
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐item measures are increasingly used in human resource management research due to practical constraints such as survey length, anticipated respondent burden, or repeated measurement. Information concerning which psychometric properties single‐item measures can and cannot meaningfully demonstrate is fragmented and incomplete in the HRM literature. This manuscript provides a comprehensive psychometric evaluation of single‐item measures, drawing on classical test theory, item response theory, and generalizability theory. Logic, math, and previous psychometric research inform the assumptions, practical considerations, and tradeoffs involved in assessing the factor structure, reliability, and validity of single‐item measures. Single‐item measures are incapable of empirically demonstrating latent factor structure or internal consistency, and common workarounds for these issues involve relying on untestable and untenable assumptions. In contrast, some forms of reliability (e.g., temporal consistency, inter‐rater reliability) and validity (e.g., criterion‐related validity, aspects of construct validity) are more conceptually and mathematically appropriate for evaluating single‐item measures. Content validity, including content coverage and clarity of item wording, is a critical consideration when developing or using a single‐item measure. This manuscript concludes by offering practical guidance for researchers and practitioners, including a checklist to aid decisions about when the use of single‐item measures is justified.

title: Sulfur-Vacancy-Enabled Dual-Site MoS2 Enhances H* Utilization for Mo–H-Mediated Deep Dechlorination
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical dechlorination using molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) offers a cost-effective solution for treating chlorinated organic contaminants, yet its catalytic potential remains limited by the unclear roles of Mo and S sites in mediating hydrogen utilization and C–Cl bond cleavage. Herein, we engineer sulfur-vacancy-rich MoS2 (Sv-MoS2) electrodes to expose coordinatively unsaturated Mo sites and enable an efficient Mo–H*-mediated dechlorination pathway. Using florfenicol as a model chlorinated antibiotic, Sv-MoS2 achieved near-complete dechlorination with ∼15-fold faster kinetics than pristine MoS2, reaching a rate constant of 9.26 h–1 at low energy consumption (0.0083 kWh g–1). Mechanistic analyses combining CV, EPR, in situ Raman spectroscopy, kinetic isotope effects, and DFT calculations reveal a dual-site H* utilization mechanism: S sites primarily generate H*, while vacancy-exposed Mo sites stabilize Mo–H* species that selectively drive C–Cl bond cleavage. In contrast, pristine MoS2 follows a direct electron transfer-dominated pathway and shows limited deep dechlorination. The Mo–H*-mediated pathway on Sv-MoS2 substantially lowers the energy barriers for sequential C–Cl cleavage while promoting productive H* utilization over H2 formation. The Sv-MoS2 electrode further exhibits robust performance under variable pH, natural organic matter, coexisting anions, and repeated cycling. This work clarifies Mo/S site synergy in MoS2 electrocatalysts and establishes a dual-site design framework for efficient, selective, and sustainable electrochemical hydrodechlorination.

Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
abstract: Abstract The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource 1 . However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs 2,3 . Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation.

title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
abstract: Abstract Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints 1,2 . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability 3 . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

title: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity
Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
abstract: Abstract In 2025, a Lancet Commission proposed distinguishing clinical obesity, defined by adiposity-related organ dysfunction, from preclinical obesity, defined by excess adiposity with preserved function, and recommended using anthropometric measures beyond body mass index (BMI) to confirm obesity status 1 . Here we report the comparative performance of this framework versus conventional BMI-based classification using prevalence, incidence and mortality data from 844,108 adults across four cohorts in China, the UK, the USA and Spain. Complementing BMI with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio data showed that BMI alone overestimated obesity in 1.2–3.1% and underestimated it in 5.2–8.6% of participants across cohorts. The combined anthropometric definition increased overall obesity prevalence by 3.3–7.4% relative to BMI-based classification. Clinical obesity accounted for 22.7–31.3% of total obesity, with an overall population prevalence of 5.6–10.9%. A large proportion of individuals (between 77.4% and 91.3%) with preclinical obesity at baseline showed no progression to clinical obesity over 10 years. Increased mortality risk was associated with the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, but not with BMI-only obesity. Clinical obesity was associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.69, 95% confidence interval 1.64–1.73), whereas preclinical obesity conferred only modest risk (1.19, 1.14–1.24). These findings support the global adoption of the Lancet Commission diagnostic framework to improve obesity care and policy.

title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
abstract: Abstract Plastic pollution is a defining feature of the Anthropocene 1 , and microplastics are dispersed by air and water into even remote terrestrial habitats 2–7 , yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals’ proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.
authors: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz

title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart
abstract: Abstract Disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because DNA synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, Pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative CMG (CDC45–MCM–GINS) helicase 1,2 . Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability 3–6 . Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment 4 . In human cells, the primase–polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress 7–10 , but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A 9,11 is not critical for fork restart in this system. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Ablating the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

title: Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses
The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL
abstract: . However, the molecular mechanism that underlies repriming remains poorly understood, and it is unclear how PRIMPOL is precisely targeted to stalled forks, where along single-stranded DNA PRIMPOL binds and how PRIMPOL is regulated to minimize error-prone DNA synthesis. Here, to dissect the molecular basis of repriming, we perform real-time single-molecule imaging in nuclear extracts that recapitulate genome maintenance. We directly visualize how stalled forks restart through repriming. We show that PRIMPOL is recruited to stalled forks through an interaction with the replicative helicase CDC45-MCM2-7-GINS (CMG). This facilitates primer handover from PRIMPOL to the high-fidelity polymerase ε, minimizing mutagenic DNA synthesis. At near-physiological concentrations, PRIMPOL reprimes leading strands in a CMG-dependent manner and polymerase ε extends those primers. This primary mode of repriming does not require DNA damage checkpoint signalling. PRIMPOL overexpression and checkpoint activation promote a secondary mode of repriming, whereby PRIMPOL restarts DNA synthesis far from CMG and polymerase δ extends those primers. Our data reveal a simple yet effective mechanism that directs PRIMPOL's activity to stalled forks awaiting restart, and suggest a strategy to inhibit the repriming pathway.

title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
abstract: Abstract TDP-43 nuclear depletion is a defining pathological feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia that induces widespread cryptic splicing defects in hundreds of transcripts 1–8 . Despite this, whether TDP-43 loss affects synaptic function has remained unclear. Here we show that TDP-43 loss induces a predegenerative state in which neurons remain structurally intact but suffer a substantial breakdown in synaptic communication. Genetic correction of a single cryptic splicing event in UNC13A was sufficient to rescue these deficits. We developed splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that correct UNC13A cryptic splicing in human cortical and spinal motor neurons and in a humanized mouse model. In human neurons this intervention restored spontaneous and evoked synaptic vesicle release, release probability at individual synapses and wider network synchrony. Together, this establishes UNC13A splice correction as a mechanistically defined and genetically validated therapeutic strategy relevant to roughly 97% of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and roughly 50% of patients with frontotemporal dementia with TDP-43 pathology.

title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials
abstract: Materials, at their essence, are networks defined by homogeneity: uniform bonds, fixed thicknesses, and discrete length scales. Mechanical metamaterials, while representing structurally more diverse microstructures, remain defined by the homogeneity of their unit cells, pore sizes, or repeating features. In contrast, as network science has revealed, real-world and biological systems -- from the Internet to the brain -- derive their function from broad, multiscale variability in connectivity and link length. Here, we introduce Scale-Rich (SR) metamaterials, a design framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials, achieving order-of-magnitude heterogeneity in ligament lengths, thicknesses, and connectivity. Governed by only two parameters, SR networks span orders of magnitude in structural features, overcoming prior constraints in metamaterial design. Translating these network models into physically realizable materials, we use simulations and experiments to show that SR metamaterials exhibit properties inaccessible to traditional single-scale systems, including highly tunable elastic anisotropy, delocalized nonlinear deformation with high energy absorption, and programmable acoustic wave control. This network-science-based paradigm establishes a minimal yet universal framework for engineering multifunctional materials whose mechanical and acoustic behavior emerge directly from scale diversity itself.

title: Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice
abstract: Nuclei in early mammalian embryos undergo epigenetic reprogramming that enables the zygote to develop into a complete organism. Whereas changes in chromatin state during this critical transition period have been extensively studied1–3, changes in the nucleus that houses chromatin remain poorly understood. Here, using direct organelle capture and biophysical manipulation methods, we find that nuclei attain profound softness and plasticity during the two-cell embryonic stage in mice, facilitating major zygotic gene activation. The prominent nuclear deformability is attributable to the rapid clearance of lamin B1 from the nuclear envelope by the autophagy factor LC3. Nuclear stiffening by lamin B1 retention or its overloading results in incomplete activation of zygotic genes and impaired development. However, embryos that maintain nuclear deformability escape from this transcriptional interference. High-resolution microscopy and sequential three-dimensional fluorescence in situ hybridization analyses revealed an accumulation of active RNA polymerase II and coordinated positioning of key genomic loci near the deformable nuclear envelope. An engineered molecular tether that stiffens the nuclei restricts these nuclear activities and suppresses expression of key zygotic gene activation genes. Together, our study identifies a distinct physical nuclear state that embryos acquire at the beginning of life that supports the initiation of the zygotic transcription program. A distinct physical nuclear state acquired by embryos at the beginning of life supports the initiation of the zygotic transcription program.

title: Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes
Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
abstract: Abstract The scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Ga) has hindered our understanding of Earth’s early evolution, fueling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. Currently, the only unequivocally documented >3.9 Ga rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada 1–3. Here we report a newly discovered 3.95 Ga trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, where 3.95 Ga magmatic zircon records elevated δ18O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive εHf(t) (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27), indicating a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a Hadean depleted mantle. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the ca. 4.0 Ga Acasta rocks 2, the 3.95 Ga trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin 4. Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrates that its parental magma formed via low degree (8–16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740–820 ℃, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface‑altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
abstract: Abstract Accessing reversible four-electron iodine redox chemistry in aqueous metal–iodine batteries offers a promising route towards high-energy aqueous energy storage, but has conventionally relied on highly concentrated, corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes to stabilize reactive hypervalent iodine cations through interhalogen complexation 1–9 . Here we show a kosmotropic anion–polar anion–nucleophilic species (Nuc) electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions, enabling reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes. Polar anions establish a water-deficient, anion-enriched interfacial microenvironment, whereas kosmotropic anions regulate water–Nuc interactions to increase the availability of Nuc for stabilizing hypervalent iodine cations through Nuc–I + –Nuc halogen bonds. This electrolyte framework is validated across diverse Nuc and in both aqueous Zn–I 2 and Al–I 2 batteries. Moving beyond conventional interhalogen stabilization, these findings establish a distinct electrolyte chemistry framework and represent a mechanistic shift for reversible multi-electron iodine chemistry in aqueous environments.

title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti
Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
abstract: Abstract Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity 1–5 . We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells) 6 . Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1 ) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 ( Rgs2 ), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

title: NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation
abstract: Disconnects between in vitro and in vivo results in experimental biology have long been recognized as potential hurdles to understanding health and disease. A prototypical example of such a disconnect is the NLRP3 inflammasome, which mediates inflammation in diverse settings of disease and protective immunity1,2. Activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in vitro requires two signals: (1) priming by pathogen-associated molecular patterns such as bacterial lipopolysaccharides and (2) activation by molecules that disrupt cellular homeostasis1,3. By contrast, the NLRP3 inflammasome in vivo is activated by lipopolysaccharide alone. The mechanisms that underlie the difference between in vitro and in vivo activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome are undefined. Here we report that extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness is a determinant of NLRP3 activities and that in vitro systems using physiological ECM stiffness enable one-signal in vivo-like NLRP3 activities to occur in human and mouse phagocytes. Physiological ECM stiffness induced expression of the transcription factor NRF2, which was found to be necessary for one-signal NLRP3 activation. Mechanistically, we identify Panx1 as an NRF2-regulated gene that promotes NLRP3 activity. Macrophages derived from the stiff matrix of the bone—osteoclasts—had reduced NRF2 levels and impaired NLRP3 activity. Moreover, alveolar macrophages from patients with pulmonary fibrosis displayed reduced NRF2 activity. Finally, NRF2 was required for antitumour immunity induced by cancer vaccines consisting of NLRP3 agonistic adjuvants. These findings indicate that NRF2 may be a transcriptional checkpoint that controls NLRP3 inflammasome activity. The stiffness of the extracellular matrix is identified as a pivotal factor that influences activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in vitro and in vivo.

title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
abstract: Breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis1–3. Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival4–7. Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse. Single-cell epigenetic analyses reveal a conserved epigenetic signature across patients that may help identify those at increased risk for disease relapse in breast cancer.

title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China
abstract: Empirical research so far largely suggests that population policies around the world do not explain a majority of the global fertility decline1–10. Notably, even China’s total fertility rate declined little after implementation of the one-child policy in 1979 and 1980, but fertility then fell sharply by more than one-third during the early 1990s. Here we show that strengthening bureaucratic incentives under China’s one vote veto policy, which strictly prohibited career advancement for adherence failure, was instrumental in more effective implementation of the one-child policy, and in its delayed impact on fertility. Using provincial variation in implementation timing, we find that the one vote veto explains nearly half of China’s total fertility rate decline during the 1990s, driving fertility below the replacement rate. Increases in use of intrauterine devices (the most prevalent form of modern contraception in China) that were recommended by local officials were particularly salient. Overall, our findings suggest that population policy, when more strictly enforced due to stronger bureaucratic incentives, made a greater contribution to low fertility in China than suggested by past research. Stronger bureaucratic incentives under China’s one vote veto policy intensified enforcement of the one-child policy, accounting for nearly half of China’s fertility decline during the 1990s.

title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
abstract: Abstract Somatic evolution in ageing tissues underlies many cancers 1,2 . However, our quantitative understanding of the rules governing this pre-cancerous evolution remains incomplete. Here we exploit a unique collection of serial blood samples 3 , collected annually for up to a decade and beginning as early as 15 years before diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia, to provide a quantitative description of pre-cancerous evolutionary dynamics. Using deep duplex sequencing and evolutionary theory, we quantify the acquisition ages and fitness effects of the key driver events in acute myeloid leukaemia development. The first driver mutations are typically acquired in the first few decades of life, when the blood remains highly polyclonal. These early slow-growing clones subsequently acquire multiple further driver mutations that confer selective advantages up to 100-fold larger than the early drivers. These faster-growing clones harbouring multiple driver mutations can cause complete somatic sweeps of the blood decades before diagnosis, a feature strongly associated with future acute myeloid leukaemia. Our data show that the clonal dynamics of blood are consistent with a set of remarkably simple evolutionary rules that strike a balance between chance and determinism.

title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
abstract: Abstract The nuclear pore complex (NPC) regulates molecular traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm 1,2 . Its permeability barrier is formed by intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), whose physical state has long been debated 3–13 . Deciphering how FG-NUPs behave inside living cells is crucial for understanding how NPCs achieve both selective and rapid transport. By combining site-specific labelling with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy, here we show that FG domains exhibit nanosecond-scale, liquid-like segmental motion in live cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro. Experiments and molecular-dynamics simulations further show that importin-β, a principal nuclear transport receptor, and O-linked β- N -acetylglucosamine, a key post-translational modification of FG-NUPs, together stabilize the dynamic FG network. Finely balanced FG–FG and FG–importin-β interactions maintain FG-NUP liquidity and generate a radial organization in which importin-β is enriched near the NPC periphery and extended FG domains remain in the central channel, forming the transport barrier. This organization explains recent MINFLUX observations 14 of rim-biased transport trajectories and is supported here by direct MINFLUX imaging of importin-β in mammalian cells. Together, our results reconcile conflicting models of FG-NUP organization 4,5,7,9,15 and establish a framework for understanding how cellular context tunes intrinsically disordered proteins in health and disease.

title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
abstract: Abstract A new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image 1–4 of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features 3,5–7 , with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source 8,9 . Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
DeepMind's ultra-powerful AI for genome mapping wows scientists
Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer
abstract: Abstract Transcriptional addiction to the androgen receptor (AR) underlies metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer 1 , in which AR maintains oncogenic programs through domain-specific interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP (collectively p300/CBP) 2 . Here we describe a novel therapeutic modality, domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs), that rewire endogenous protein complexes by enforcing non-native domain–domain interactions. Our first-in-class AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1 induces synthetic proximity between the ligand-binding domain of AR and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, misconfiguring their native interface and locking the complex in a non-productive state. DALTAC-1 triggers a ‘super-inhibitory’ effect, suppressing AR-driven transcription and proliferation more potently than combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition. Mechanistically, DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, abolishing the histone mark H2B N-terminal acetylation and inducing neomorphic acetylation of AR and coactivators, ultimately collapsing the AR neo-enhanceosome. Chromatin profiling revealed redistribution of AR and p300/CBP towards palindromic androgen response elements, accompanied by disruption of cofactor and transcriptional machinery recruitment at oncogenic AR and ERG neo-enhancers. DALTAC-1 exhibits exquisite lineage selectivity, displaying potent activity in AR–p300/CBP dual-dependent cells and sparing AR-negative cells. In multiple in vivo models, DALTAC-1 induces deep and durable tumour regressions. Together, these findings establish DALTACs as a broadly applicable strategy to rewire disease-defining complexes through domain-topology alteration, expanding induced-proximity therapies, and the precise lineage selectivity of DALTAC-1 supports its translational potential in AR-driven prostate cancer.

title: A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2′,3′-cNMP produced by insect effectors
abstract: RNA-derived 2′,3′-cyclophosphate-terminated nucleotides act as immune signalling molecules in prokaryotes and eukaryotes1–3, but how plants perceive them remains unknown. Sucking insects inject digestive enzymes including RNases into the host plant to acquire nutrients. Here we demonstrate that NIB1, a glycine-rich RNA-binding protein in rice, senses 2′,3′-cyclic nucleotide monophosphates (2′,3′-cNMPs; 2′,3′-cAMP and 2′,3′-cGMP) and adenylyl-(3′→5′)-guanosine 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate (ApG>p) produced by a salivary T2 ribonuclease of green stink bug during feeding. Binding of the RNase products promotes formation of nuclear condensates containing NIB1, which recruit the core immune regulator Enhanced Disease Susceptibility 1 (EDS1) and activate defence, potentially contributing to the immune signalling of Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) proteins that also produce the nuclease products. Exogenous application of 2′,3′-cAMP, 2′,3′-cGMP or ApG>p elicits NIB1 and EDS1-mediated immune responses. Our findings unveil a conserved pathway in plants, in which glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins perceive the nuclease-generated second messengers to launch defence and point to a potential link between plant TIR nuclease activity and EDS1 signalling. The rice RNA-binding protein NIB1 detects 2′,3′-cyclic nucleotide products from insect saliva RNase, forming nuclear condensates that recruit EDS1 to activate defence, revealing a conserved messenger-based immune pathway in plants.

title: Proposed approach for diagnosing obesity outperforms old method
abstract: A framework for diagnosing obesity that was proposed in 2025 incorporates waist circumference and related measures and distinguishes clinical from preclinical obesity on the basis of obesity-induced organ dysfunction. In an international multi-cohort study of 844,108 adults, this framework outperformed conventional body-mass-index-based criteria in diagnosing obesity and stratifying mortality risk. A combination of body and organ-function metrics does better at classifying obesity than does body mass index.

title: New culprit in early Alzheimer’s: Blood–brain barrier blocks protective proteins
Proteins that form the nuclear pore barrier move like liquids
abstract: Nuclear pores control molecular traffic into and out of the cell nucleus. Measurements in living cells, together with molecular-dynamics simulations, show that flexible protein chains that form the selectivity barriers of nuclear pores are highly mobile, and that a sugar modification and the carrier protein importin-β help to preserve this dynamic state. The motion of the nuclear pore protein NUP98 is regulated by a transport receptor and a sugar modification.

title: Personal incentives for public officials drove a drop in China’s fertility
Cacti are severely threatened by drought in a warming world
abstract: Forecasts of the effects that climate change will have on biodiversity typically rely on long-term climate averages while excluding extreme events. Projections that include severe drought predict that a majority of the 993 cactus species assessed will see large losses of suitable climatic area: more than 25% of species could lose at least 80% of it by 2100. Models that ignore extreme events might underestimate the dangers of climate change for this plant family.

title: Getting a grasp on the global wildlife trade
Earth’s early history told by 3.9-billion-year-old rocks from northern China
abstract: Ancient rocks in northern China reveal that by 3.95 billion years ago, surface-altered oceanic crust had been buried rapidly to depths greater than 50 kilometres and partly melted. This crust was derived from a mantle reservoir that had been left behind when the crust separated from the early mantle as early as 4.3 billion years ago. Zircon crystals found in some of Earth’s oldest rocks suggest that the source rock was once buried about 50 kilometres into the mantle.

title: Extraordinary materials shaped by the principles of complex networks
Salty grains in Saturn’s outermost ring formed from the slow freeze of plumes from the moon Enceladus
Can green technologies deliver energy security in an unstable world?
abstract: As global energy markets grapple with a period of sustained political volatility, researchers are digging deep for solutions.

title: AI’s energy paradox: will the AI boom strain energy systems or be the source of solutions?
A guide to Nature Index tables

Beliefs and the Incentive Effects of Preferential College Admissions: Evidence from an Experiment and a Structural Model
