Extending security beyond the meter: Rethinking energy security and energy efficiency policy at the household level
Global impacts of national and regional trade policies on the carbon footprint of electric vehicle battery
The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: Cross-vector flexibility in sector-coupled low-carbon energy systems
Organic phase change materials: From passive thermal regulators to active multifunctional enablers in sustainable technologies
The recyclability gap in United States clothing and the climate value of closing it
Calibrated screening-level life cycle assessment of food products from ingredient data: Distribution-free uncertainty quantification across sixteen environmental impact categories
Solar-Driven Cu(II)–Cu(III) Redox Cycle on Decahedral BiVO4 for Scalable Water Purification
abstract: Abstract Conventional Fenton-like reactions rely on external oxidants to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS, e.g., high-valent metal-oxo species (HVMS)), a practice that is inherently unsustainable for water purification. Here, we propose a solar-driven Cu(II)–Cu(III) redox cycle that differs from the traditional view that HVMS generation originates from peroxide-mediated pathways. By tuning the anisotropic built-in field of decahedral BiVO4, photogenerated holes accumulate selectively on its {110} family, enabling hole-driven hydrated Cu(II) oxidation instead of water. This facilitates an oxygen atom transfer (OAT) from adjacent Bi–OH sites to the H-bonded Cu(II) center, stabilizing the Cu(III)-oxo center by forming the Bi–O–Cu(III)–O structure (Cu(III)). Meanwhile, electron-driven dissolved oxygen reduction maintains charge balance. The photosynthetic Cu(III) mediates antibiotic degradation with a rate constant of 0.174 min–1, representing a ∼16-fold enhancement in the degradation rate constant compared to traditional photocatalysis. Crucially, the solar BiVO4 sheet/Cu(II) system sustains consistent up to ∼85% moxifloxacin degradation efficiency in each cycle over 35 days. No total Cu was detected in the effluent of cycling experiments after pH adjustment (∼7.5). These findings provide a new solution to the long-standing challenge of achieving peroxide-free HVMS synthesis and scalable water purification.

title: Engineering High-Entropy Interfaces in a Single-Metal Cu System to Drive Concerted Nonradical Catalysis and Pollutant Sequestration
abstract: Abstract Nonradical direct electron transfer (DET) can make advanced oxidation less vulnerable to radical scavenging in complex waters, but requires catalysts with efficient charge transport, stability, and practical synthesis. High-entropy materials provide diverse local environments, yet their multimetal compositions and prolonged heat treatment limit implementation. We combined chemically induced self-internal heating (SIH) with chloride-induced interfacial reconstruction to prepare a single-metal Cu system with high-density grain boundaries (SM-HDGB). SIH formed a Cu-carbon precursor in 3.5 s through an internal pulse above 1200 °C. HCl treatment generated intergrown Cu, Cu2O, CuCl, and Cu2Cl(OH)3 domains spaced 2–10 nm apart, creating phase, oxidation-state, and coordination diversity described as empirical interfacial chemical-state entropy. SM-HDGB completely removed tetracycline within 10 min and increased the apparent rate constant 9.88-fold over the precursor, with little response to 10 mM coexisting anions. Electron paramagnetic resonance, scavenging, filtration, electrochemical, and in situ spectroscopic evidence supported predominantly surface-confined, catalyst-mediated DET. In packed-bed operation, SM-HDGB maintained more than 80% COD removal across four regeneration cycles (approximately 130 h), retained pollutant-derived organic products, and produced near-neutral effluent compatible with Chlorella growth. Laboratory-scale screening estimated at least 96.3% lower synthesis energy demand than conventional routes. Chemical-state-diverse single-metal interfaces can therefore couple rapid peroxydisulfate activation with stable continuous-flow treatment.

title: Organoid-Based Strategy for Exploration of Cancer-Related Early Signatures of Low-Dose Methylmercury Exposure
abstract: Abstract Methylmercury (MeHg) compounds are classified as Group 2B agents, possibly carcinogenic to humans by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), and as Group C possible human carcinogens by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA), but the carcinogenic implications of environmentally relevant low-dose exposure remain unclear. Here, we established a population-informed organoid-based strategy to explore the potential of low-dose MeHg exposure leading to cancer incidence. A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)-based analysis revealed nonlinear associations of blood MeHg with overall cancer history with increased predicted cancer probability around 5.39 μg/L for MeHg. Liver organoid experiments showed that low-dose MeHg did not cause overt short-term cytotoxicity but induced DNA damage and stress-response signatures after prolonged exposure. Transcriptomic analysis further linked low-dose MeHg exposure to cancer-related stress pathways, including reactive oxygen species (ROS) associated chemical carcinogenesis, p53 signaling, DNA repair, mitochondrial stress, and cell-cycle regulation. These results indicate that low-dose MeHg exposure could trigger early biological responses related to cancer-associated processes before apparent cytotoxicity occurs. This study supports organoid models as a human-relevant strategy for linking population exposure signals with tissue-level toxicological evidence in MeHg research and provides a potentially adaptable framework for evaluating subtle health effects of low-dose environmental pollutants.

title: Investigating the Relationships between the Structure and Cytotoxicity of Ionic Liquids in the Context of Cell Lines Being Affected
abstract: Abstract Current quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models of ionic liquid (IL) cytotoxicity are generally developed for specific biological systems and cannot be assumed to transfer across cell types. Here, we evaluated 81 ILs spanning eight cationic head groups and 13 anions in HEK293T, CaCo-2, and DF-1 cell lines. The alkyl side chain length was the dominant structural determinant within homologous series, whereas cation, anion, and functionalization effects were most evident among ILs with shorter alkyl side chains. Mechanistic assays with 1-alkyl-3-methylimidazolium chlorides revealed distinct 24-h cellular response profiles in HEK293T and DF-1 cells, including different patterns of membrane permeabilization, apoptosis, and mitochondrial membrane potential changes. Descriptor-cytotoxicity correlations were strong within homologous imidazolium series but were less transferable across other structural comparisons. These results show that structure-based models can be informative within a defined chemical and cellular domain, but the cell type and cytotoxic response must be considered when extrapolating the IL cytotoxicity and assessing the safety of ILs proposed as greener process media.

title: Unraveling the Effects of Early Life Air Pollution and Temperature Exposure on Children Being Overweight and Obese: Evidence and Intervention
Zeolite-Regulated Electron-Rich Cu–O–Ce Sites for Efficient Denitrification against Alkali/Heavy Metal Poisoning
abstract: Abstract Enhancing the wide-temperature-window deNOx activity of catalysts under alkali/heavy metal poisoning conditions remains a pivotal challenge in the field of environmental catalysis. To tackle this issue, we designed a novel CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst using an acid-rich zeolite-modulated electron-enriched metal site strategy. This strategy enables the contact between strong acid sites and Cu–O–Ce active sites, simultaneously regulating the efficient NH3–SCR temperature window and enhancing K/Pb poisoning resistance. Compared to CuCeOx, the engineered acid-rich interface significantly facilitates electron transfer from ZSM-5 to CuCeOx, generating electron-rich Cu–O–Ce active sites. These sites not only serve as adjacent adsorption and activation centers for reactants but also inhibit NH3 oxidation, and CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst achieves >90% deNOx efficiency over a wide temperature range of 180–410 °C (T90 = 180–410 °C). K deactivates the catalyst mainly by reducing surface acidity and promoting the accumulation of less-reactive nitrate species, while Pb primarily suppresses Ce4+ → Ce3+ reduction via inducing Cu2+ → Cu+ conversion and occupying CeO2 oxygen vacancies. Notably, the poisoned CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst still retains satisfactory deNOx performance, with the T90 = 230–380 °C. This work not only provides novel mechanistic insights into the deactivation pathways of NH3–SCR catalysts by alkali and heavy metal ions but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of high-performance, poisoning-tolerant NH3–SCR catalysts tailored for complex flue gas environments.

title: Partition-Buffered Leaching of 6PPD-Quinone from Tire Wear Particles
abstract: Abstract 6PPD-quinone (6PPDQ; N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine-quinone) forms on tire-derived solid surfaces, including those of intact tires and environmentally dispersed tire wear particles (TWPs), yet its leaching kinetics remain insufficiently characterized for confident use in watershed and coastal fate-and-transport models. Here, we conducted time-resolved saturated column leaching experiments to quantify 6PPDQ leaching from lab-generated TWPs and to derive a physically based parametrization. Across hour-to-month observation windows, TWPs exhibited sustained, nearly linear 6PPDQ release (α ≈ 1) and weak particle-size scaling of the characteristic time scale, inconsistent with whole-particle Fickian diffusion. We tested a mechanistic hypothesis that strong TWP-water partitioning buffers aqueous concentrations and limits 6PPDQ mass export. Using a well-mixed column reactor (WMCR) representation, we estimated the TWP-water partition coefficient Ksw for the columns. The regression yielded log10 Ksw = 4.37 ± 0.22. Building on this mechanistic interpretation, we derived a Newtonian first-order leaching term suitable for hydrologic and coastal modeling. A two-compartment formulation further indicated that the TWP concentration, cTWP, strongly controls the apparent fraction of 6PPDQ released to the dissolved phase. These findings may help explain variability across prior leaching studies while bridging inconsistencies between experimental and field measurements.

title: Missed Opportunities Forgo One-Third of Mass Timber’s Carbon Storage Potential
abstract: Abstract Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level perspectives can overlook operational choices that forfeit storage potential. Using stage-resolved life-cycle inventories, scenario-aware uncertainty analysis, and dynamic carbon accounting, we trace carbon flows across mass timber supply chains in the United States, from harvest slash and mill residue to wood products through end-of-life. Across modeled deployment scenarios, we show that management decisions, not technical limits, cut 1.4–2.6 gigatons (Gt) of CO2e storage by 2120, corresponding to roughly one-third of mass timber’s storage potential. Globally, storage losses from these choices could reach 3.8–12 Gt CO2e. We outline a storage-first pathway including slash pyrolysis, diversion of mill residue from bioenergy to wood panel markets, and reuse or pyrolysis at end-of-life. Together, these strategies redirect carbon into value-added, long-lived pools rather than short-lived fates, showing that release timing and supply chain routing choices can matter more than production decarbonization in shaping warming outcomes under mass timber deployment. If implemented, these choices recover forgone storage and aid in developing the built environment as a durable carbon reservoir.

title: Electron Transfer Pathways Stretching from the Extracellular to Intracellular Membrane in Biohybrids Enable Enhanced CO2 Upcycling to Malate
abstract: Abstract Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) empowers one-step conversion of CO2 to long-chain chemicals under mild conditions, enabling sustainable biomanufacturing and achievement of a circular carbon economy. Although the construction of biohybrids has been explored to enhance the inherently low efficiency of MES, whether the binding modes between nanomaterials and microorganisms dictating CO2 conversion efficiency remain elusive. To address this query, we constructed biohybrids with three distinct integration modes (namely, internalization, outer membrane-contact, and transenvelope) between nanomaterials and Shewanella, enabling to proceed CO2-to-malate conversion. Upon MES-driven CO2-to-malate conversion, the transenvelope biohybrid constituted by polydopamine and Shewanella achieved a marked gram-scale malate titer of 19.14 mmol/L, as a result of the distinctive transenvelope capacity of polydopamine stretching from the extracellular to the intracellular membrane. This transenvelope capacity imparts extended electron transfer pathways spanning from the cytoplasmic membrane to the extracellular space, significantly reducing interfacial barriers at the electrode-microorganism interface and greatly promoting NADH and ATP synthesis for malate synthesis, which can enhance NADH synthesis. This work proposes the construction of a transenvelope biohybrid to optimize microbial metabolism, offering an alternative for the efficient valorization of CO2 to carbon-negative long-chain chemicals.

title: Organophosphate Flame Retardants Induce Neurodegenerative Pathologies by Paralyzing HSP90AB1 Chaperone Function: A Multi-Scale Computational and Biophysical Study
abstract: Abstract This study integrated computational toxicology with biophysical and cellular validation to investigate the neurotoxic potential of 10 flame-retardant-related compounds. ADMETlab 3.0 predicted blood-brain barrier probabilities of 0.989 for bis(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate and 0.444 for diphenyl phosphate (DPHP), interpreted as screening predictions. Network topology analysis identified HSP90AB1 as a shared candidate hub target linking organophosphate flame retardants to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated a stable HSP90AB1 backbone in the DPHP complex (root-mean-square deviation ∼0.18 nm). Surface plasmon resonance measured an equilibrium dissociation constant of 1.49 μM. DPHP induced dose-dependent cytotoxicity in neuronal cells; the half-maximal inhibitory concentration was not determined within the tested range. HSP90AB1 overexpression mitigated DPHP-induced reactive oxygen species production and transcriptional upregulation of pro-apoptotic and pro-inflammatory genes. Single-cell virtual knockout identified candidate regulatory processes; Parkinson’s disease-related enrichment remained exploratory after multiple-testing correction. Together, the computational, biophysical, and cellular findings support HSP90AB1 as a candidate target of environmental neurotoxicity and motivate further investigation of DPHP.

title: Multitechnique Characterization of Dissolved Organic Matter from Naturally Acidic and Circumneutral Waters Reveals Molecular Controls on Organic Nitrogen Speciation
abstract: Abstract The molecular characteristics of dissolved organic matter (DOM) vary across seasons, catchments, and land uses, highlighting the need for generalized structure–function relationships that can predict intrinsic DOM bioavailability. This study characterized DOM from naturally acidic (pH 4.3–5.7) and circumneutral (pH 6.8–8.3) freshwaters over two seasons: winter-spring (WS) and summer-autumn (SA) using multiple characterization techniques (optical, fluorescence, targeted LC-MS/MS, 13C NMR, and FTIR). DOM from acidic environments was higher in aromaticity, more humic-like, with a higher C:N ratio but with a greater percentage of nitrogen in the form of amino acids (i.e., DCAA-N%). Seasonality was only observed for neutral samples, with differences between WS and SA dominated by a decrease in nominal molecular weight (MWn) in SA, likely driven by photochemical disaggregation. FTIR analysis indicates that neutral DOM has a higher amide group abundance than acidic DOM despite the lower DCAA-N%, suggesting the dominance of nonproteinaceous amide-N. Very strong dependencies were observed for dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) speciation against aromaticity (SUVA254) and an FTIR-derived ratio of deprotonated carboxylic:aromatic groups, describing the relative hydrophilicity–hydrophobicity of the DOM environment. These parameters largely explain the DCAA distribution and may provide a more generalized way of characterizing DOM that could be applied across different aquatic ecosystems.

title: Toward Dynamic Biointerface Toxicology of Micro- and Nanoplastics Using Organoids and Organ-on-a-Chip Models
abstract: Abstract Micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) toxicity depends on the exposure conditions under which particles encounter biological tissues, yet nominal material descriptors alone do not resolve these conditions. Environmental transformation, biomolecular adsorption, aggregation, and chemical release can alter particle delivery and biological interactions. This Review evaluates these processes alongside evidence from organoids and organ-on-a-chip models, distinguishing direct MNP findings from analogue studies and demonstrations of platform capability. We propose exposure identity as an analytical framework connecting particle history and state with tissue encounter and subsequent processing over time. The synthesis examines what available studies establish about tissue access, barrier responses, distal relay, and susceptibility, and where interpretation remains constrained by exposure characterization or unresolved mechanisms. Human-derived models provide opportunities to investigate tissue-specific responses, but neither biological complexity nor perfusion establishes environmental representativeness or predictive validity. We identify measurement and control requirements for separating particle transfer from chemical release and tissue-derived signaling, interpreting absent effects, and evaluating heterogeneous exposures. Priorities include traceable delivered-dose measurements, synchronized exposure and response sampling, targeted mechanistic tests, and independent validation for a defined use. The proposed framework organizes evidence and testable relationships while retaining uncertainty about generalization to human exposure and health outcomes.

title: Tire-Derived Organic Pollutants across Urban Land Uses: Associations with Traffic Exposure
abstract: Abstract Tire-derived organic pollutants (TDOPs), particularly N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its transformation product 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), are increasingly recognized as emerging urban contaminants. However, their distribution and potential drivers in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment remain poorly characterized. In this study, 19 TDOPs were quantified in 28 urban soil samples representing four land-use types in Metro Detroit, Michigan, United States. TDOPs were widely detected in all soil samples, and 16 compounds exhibited detection frequencies ≥75%. Very low 6PPD/6PPD-Q ratios and the relative enrichment of N,N′-diphenyl-p-phenylenediamine (DPPD) over 6PPD suggest substantial environmental transformation of 6PPD. No statistically significant differences in the concentrations of TDOPs among land-use types or associations with measured soil properties were detected. In contrast, 6PPD exhibited a strong positive association with traffic-derived exposure metrics. The maximum Spearman rank correlation coefficient was observed for the commercial traffic exposure metric at a distance-decay parameter of 800 m (ρ = 0.76), and the association remained significant after optimization-adjusted permutation testing (pperm = 0.00030) and false discovery rate correction (q = 0.0048). This study demonstrates the widespread occurrence of TDOPs in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment and identifies modeled traffic exposure as an important correlate of soil 6PPD concentrations.

title: Redox-Active Electrodes Enable Selective Ammonium Recovery and Reuse for Rare Earth Mining
abstract: Abstract Rare earth element (REE) extraction from ion-adsorption deposits relies on ammonium (NH4+) assisted in situ leaching, yet the spent leachant is typically discarded as wastewater rather than recovered for reuse. Here, we report a redox-active electrosorption platform that selectively recovers NH4+ from REE tailings wastewater and enables its direct reuse in the leaching process, establishing a circular approach to nitrogen management. This platform employs nickel-substituted copper hexacyanoferrate as redox hosts for reversible ammonium storage. Nickel incorporation modifies the redox and ion-transport properties of CuHCF while improving framework stability. The resulting Cu0.8Ni0.2HCF redox-active electrode exhibits a high capacity of 82.6 mAh g–1, superior cycling durability (>90% retention after 30 h), and remarkable ammonium selectivity over Na+ (9.2), Ca2+ (19.3), Mg2+ (25.5), La3+ (38.5), and Y3+ (42.2). Multiscale characterizations and calculations support favorable NH4+ host–guest interactions and ion transport within the framework. The recovered ammonium is directly reused for ion-adsorption-type rare earth leaching with extraction performance comparable to fresh leachants. Life-cycle assessment and techno-economic analyses demonstrate reduced environmental footprint and favorable economic feasibility. This study established a redox-active electrosorption platform that shifts nitrogen management from a linear “treatment-discharge” model toward a circular “recovery-reuse” pathway.

title: Contrasting Dynamics of Particle-Bound Organophosphate Esters Reveal Distinct High-Altitude Contaminant Transport Processes over the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Abstract Particle-bound semivolatile organic compounds (SVOCs) reaching high-mountain regions are commonly interpreted in terms of temperature-driven gas-particle partitioning and precipitation scavenging. To investigate these competing dynamics, we report year-round, synchronous measurements of particle-bound organophosphate esters (OPEs) in PM2.5 at two contrasting Tibetan Plateau sites: a southern Himalayan receptor (QOMS) and an inland background site (NAMORS). ΣOPEs averaged 111 ± 125 pg m–3 at QOMS and 20 ± 17 pg m–3 at NAMORS, exhibiting a counterintuitive warm-season maximum. This warm-season peak coincided with a 72–91% decline in hygroscopic secondary inorganic aerosols, indicating that trans-Himalayan transport sustains substantial particle-bound OPE inputs during the monsoon despite intense wet deposition. Furthermore, chlorinated congeners with stronger particle association (TCPP, TDCPP) dominated at both sites (TCEP/TCPP = 0.09–0.46). This contrasts with the highly volatile TCEP-dominated profiles reported for Arctic aerosols. Such a difference is consistent with an orographic modulation favoring particulate-phase retention during the shorter trans-Himalayan ascent. However, the lack of simultaneous gas-phase data and potential differences in regional emission histories must also be acknowledged. Back-trajectory clustering and principal component analysis both point to South Asian source regions as the principal control at QOMS. Consequently, correlations of OPEs with temperature and precipitation are better read as proxies for monsoon transport intensity than as evidence of local thermodynamic partitioning. Continued transboundary input suggests that particle-bound OPEs may contribute to deposition and subsequent accumulation in the alpine cryosphere, highlighting the urgent need to incorporate transboundary transport pathways into regional contaminant assessments.

title: Biomass Hydrothermal Reduction Enables Direct Copper Recovery from Wastewater
abstract: Abstract Recovering copper (Cu) from strongly acidic copper wastewater (SACW) is essential for resource sustainability and environmental preservation, but conventional technologies bear high economic costs and generate secondary pollution. Here, we demonstrate a biomass waste-mediated hydrothermal reduction process that simultaneously removes and recovers Cu as metallic Cu from SACW. The process operates under mild conditions (180 °C, 7 h) and achieves over 99% removal of Cu(II) across a wide concentration range, directly reducing Cu(II) to metallic Cu(0) without incorporation into hydrochar. Notably, the liquid products from biomass hydrothermal treatment, particularly 2-furoic acid, served as electron donors for Cu(II) reduction, with its C2/C3 atoms potentially providing electron transfer channels that drive the stepwise reduction of Cu(II) to Cu(0). In a 5 L pilot test with two types of industrial wastewater, the technology achieved >99% Cu(II) removal (residual <0.5 mg/L) and recovered metallic Cu with a purity of 99.9% after simple calcination. Life-cycle assessment and technoeconomic analysis highlight superior economic and environmental benefits when treating high-concentration copper-containing wastewater, establishing a sustainable, generalized hydrothermal reduction platform for efficient Cu recovery from industrial wastewaters. This work establishes a chemistry-driven paradigm for sustainable wastewater treatment, enabling efficient circular recovery of high-value resources from acidic metal-containing wastewaters.

title: Emerging Hexafluoropropylene Oxide Trimer Acid Potently Targets Farnesoid X Receptor and Triggers Hepatic Cholestasis
abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) hepatotoxicity is a critical global health threat, and disrupted bile acid metabolism is considered a key driver of PFAS-triggered liver injury, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Herein, we explored the hepatotoxic mechanisms of emerging hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA) and dimer acid (HFPO–DA) via farnesoid X receptor (FXR), assessed their health risks, and further compared their effects against perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). In rat, HFPO-TA exerted more potent hepatotoxicity than PFOA and HFPO–DA, triggering typical cholestasis through impaired biliary excretion and altered bile acid pool. Mechanistically, all three PFASs promoted the intracellular bile acid accumulation by inhibiting FXR transcriptional activity, with potent HFPO-TA > PFOA > HFPO–DA. Accordingly, HFPO-TA, HFPO–DA, and PFOA can directly bind to FXR though entering the ligand-binding domain via hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions to stabilize an antagonizing conformation. Notably, HFPO-TA bound FXR with 3.25-fold higher affinity than endogenous chenodeoxycholic acid and 50-fold higher affinity than PFOA, accompanied by elevated receptor-bound concentrations (RBCs). RBC-based risk assessment revealed moderate risk in 28.3% of HFPO-TA-exposed residents. Overall, HFPO-TA directly binds to FXR to induce hepatic cholestasis; such FXR-mediated cholestasis poses notable health risks and warrants broad vigilance toward PFAS liver hazards.

title: Non-Targeted Characterization and Hazard-Based Prioritization of Disinfection Byproducts and Co-Contaminants in U.S. Drinking Water Distribution Systems
abstract: Abstract Higher-carbon (>C2) disinfection byproducts (DBPs) remain poorly characterized in drinking water distribution systems (DWDSs) despite evidence that they may contribute substantially to drinking water toxicity. Here, we applied liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry and non-targeted analysis to characterize >C2 DBPs and co-contaminants across 12 U.S. DWDSs spanning a range of pre-oxidation and disinfection strategies. For each DWDS, we analyzed finished drinking water and distribution system samples collected at locations representing short, medium, and long distances from the treatment plant. We identified multiple classes of >C2 DBPs, including non-halogenated and halogenated hydroxybenzoic acids, halohydroxybenzaldehydes, halonitrophenols, (halo)phenylacetamides, (halo)fumaric acids, and several emerging nitrogenous DBPs. In addition, we also detected various co-contaminants such as pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and industrial chemicals. DBPs and co-contaminants exhibited system-specific occurrence and spatial patterns, and non-halogenated hydroxybenzoic acids emerged as an overlooked and widespread class of DBPs. To support prioritization efforts, hazard data from EPA’s Hazard Comparison Module was used to develop and implement hazard-weighted prioritization metrics. This approach identified (halo)hydroxybenzoic acids, halonitrophenols, DEET, triazine herbicides, and 2-hydroxyquinoline as high-priority contaminants, indicating that both emerging DBPs and co-contaminants may contribute to mixture-level hazards in distributed drinking water. Overall, this work expands the known >C2 DBP landscape and provides a framework for prioritizing drinking water contaminants detected by non-targeted analysis.

Ecosystem services in shellfish reef restoration and coastal policy: A global scoping review
abstract: Shellfish reefs can contribute to nature-based solutions (NbS) that can support coastal protection, water quality, and biodiversity, yet the extent to which their ecosystem services (ES) are reflected in coastal policy remains unclear. This global scoping review maps the scientific evidence on ES associated with shellfish reefs and examines their relationships with restoration approaches, policy instruments, and governance frameworks. Specifically, we (i) classify reported ES, (ii) examine associations between restoration approaches and reported ES, (iii) assess the representation of policy instruments and governance dimensions in the reviewed literature, and (iv) identify knowledge gaps relevant to coastal management and planning. We used a predefined search strategy, eligibility criteria, and structured full-text coding to map evidence across shellfish taxa, geographic regions, restoration approaches, and policy dimensions, identifying areas of concentrated and limited representation within the retrieved literature. Within the 151 included studies, regulating and supporting services were reported more frequently than provisioning and cultural services. Although approximately three-quarters of studies included explicit policy content, links to operational instruments—such as spatial planning, permitting, and incentive-based mechanisms—were less frequently reported. Monitoring and stakeholder engagement were inconsistently documented, potentially limiting the usability of the published evidence for decision-making. These findings reveal gaps in how connections between ecosystem-service evidence, restoration, and coastal governance are documented in the literature. Greater attention to socio-ecological objectives, consistent restoration monitoring, and the reporting of links between ES outcomes and policy instruments could strengthen the relevance of this evidence for coastal decision-making. Broader documentation from less frequently represented regions, including parts of the Global South, would improve the geographic breadth of the evidence base.

Environmental accountability: avoidable methane and VOC contamination in Alberta’s oilpatch
abstract: Purpose This study examines how the Alberta government’s October 2000 withdrawal of the Long-Term Inactive Well Program and its replacement with the Licensee Liability Rating system enabled two decades of avoidable methane and volatile organic compound (VOC) contamination. It analyzes how accounting-based regulatory choices, co-participation between government and corporations and the withholding of environmental information facilitated the indefinite deferral of decommissioning and reclamation, producing major environmental and health consequences. Design/methodology/approach A total of 7,380 pages of internal government records obtained through a series of freedom-of-information (FOI) requests were integrated with well-level production data for 599,002 Alberta wells covering 1961–2018. After extensive cleaning and organization, these materials were used to reconstruct regulatory decision-making and to generate tables and spatial mapping of cumulative contamination patterns. Our analyses qualitatively interpret the documentary evidence to illuminate the accounting-implicated regulatory choices that shaped Alberta’s non-producing well problem and their environmental consequences. Findings The LLR’s design – originating in a proposal authored by a Canadian Natural Resources Ltd. employee and using reclamation costs supplied by the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers – shifted regulatory focus from the timely decommissioning of non-producing wells to the management of financial risk to the orphan fund. This shift enabled wells to remain undecommissioned for decades, generating an estimated 2.3 million well-years of avoidable contamination. By 2018, nearly 10% of Alberta’s landmass lay within 500 m of a non-producing undecommissioned well, including First Nations reserves that had few such wells three decades earlier, and the regulator’s own internal calculations indicate that the 15 largest oilpatch corporations would, at current rates, require an average of 288 years to decommission their existing inventories of inactive wells. Originality/value This study is the first to integrate FOI-obtained regulatory records with privately purchased well-level data to map the cumulative, avoidable environmental consequences of accounting-implicated regulatory changes. It contends that in co-participatory settings of resource extraction and environmental degradation, where governments and corporations are structurally aligned through royalty dependence, accounting academics can and should seek to uncover, analyze and publicize environmental information that governments and corporations prefer to keep hidden and to place such information into the hands of audiences capable of mobilizing it within accountability struggles.

title: Exploration Across Incompatible Technologies: How Firms Organize Flexibility for Innovation
abstract: ABSTRACT Firms often face multiple emerging technologies that evolve in parallel yet share limited architectural compatibility. In such settings, firms may concentrate innovation on one trajectory or pursue flexibility by maintaining engagement across multiple trajectories. We theorize that flexibility can improve innovation performance, but that these benefits depend on organizational structures that facilitate deep, trajectory‐specific learning and effective coordination. We argue that focused subsidiaries enable deep expertise within individual technologies, external collaborations provide access to complementary expertise beyond firm boundaries, and organizational modularity reduces the coordination burdens associated with pursuing multiple trajectories. Using 40‐year longitudinal data from the flat‐panel display industry, we find that the benefits of a flexibility strategy for innovation performance are substantially greater when firms have more focused subsidiaries, engage in more external collaboration, or exhibit higher organizational modularity. These findings are consistent across three complementary dimensions of innovation performance: patent impact, patent monetary value, and new product introductions. When these organizational arrangements are limited, the relationship between flexibility and innovation performance is substantially weaker. Our study demonstrates how organizational design enables firms to realize the innovation benefits of flexibility across architecturally incompatible technological trajectories.

title: Multi-model insights into racial and ethnic heterogeneities in early COVID-19 transmission and severity in the U.S.
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic was marked by unequal disease burden across racial and ethnic groups in the US. Using a multi-model ensemble framework, we retrospectively assessed the impact of racial and ethnic heterogeneities in COVID-19 transmission and disease severity on mortality during the winter 2020–2021 surge in California and North Carolina. Models incorporating race and ethnicity projected mortality more accurately than null models, while the ensemble outperformed all individual models on average by weighted interval scores. Eliminating transmission heterogeneities produced larger mortality reductions than eliminating severity differences alone, particularly for Latino populations in California (55% reduction) and Black populations in North Carolina (28% reduction). Reducing severity heterogeneity also lowered mortality, with the greatest benefit among Black populations in both states (21% and 16% reductions in California and North Carolina, respectively). Eliminating both transmission and severity heterogeneity yielded the largest reductions overall, predicting 49–70% lower mortality across racial and ethnic groups in California and 23–40% in North Carolina. Mitigating transmission inequities also produced indirect benefits for non-targeted populations, highlighting the broad impact of reducing disparities in exposure risk and access to protective resources.

Synthetic textile upcycling to produce functional adsorbents: state-of-the-art, challenges and outlook
abstract: The use of waste materials as low-cost adsorbents for treating water pollutants offers many advantages as they contribute to reducing waste disposal costs and aiding sustainable resource management. Synthetic textile wastes pose environmental threats, hence their upcycling to adsorbents for treating water pollutants presents a good option for sustainability and circularity. The synthetic textiles are employed in their pristine, chemically functionalized, or morphologically tailored forms, including fiber felts, electrospun membranes, 3D-printed monoliths, and activated carbon (AC). This review critically examined up-to-date research, common target pollutants, performance and trends regarding the upcycling of synthetic textiles to produce functional adsorbents for water treatment. Generally, adsorption performance towards organic and inorganic pollutants including emerging contaminants is controlled by surface area/porosity, surface functionality/chemistry, morphology, crystallinity, wettability, and stability. For metals and dyes, performance depends almost entirely on functionalization, e.g., coatings, grafting, carbonization. For hydrocarbons and oils, hydrophobic pristine textiles already perform well, however, performance is further improved via surface functionalization. For emerging contaminants such as microplastics and PFAS, synthetic textiles are largely underutilized, with current evidence dominated by microplastic-vector studies and composite materials rather than purpose-designed textile-based adsorbents. Noteworthily, the upcycled adsorbents serve potentially lower-cost and more circular alternatives in location-specific applications, rather than universal replacements for AC or ion exchange resins. Consequently, synthetic textile-derived adsorbents are economically promising, however, rigorous cost analysis, regeneration, real wastewater systems, and scale-up operations remain a major missing piece and a clear priority for future research. Additionally, comprehensive leaching and chemical screening are required prior to deployment. Moreover, spent adsorbents and regeneration liquors must be managed through metal recovery, eluate treatment, or controlled destruction, consistent with for example, EU textile collection and EPR policies. Standardized testing should quantify hydraulic performance, breakthrough behavior, dynamic capacity, mass transfer, mechanical stability, material shedding, bed utilization, and regeneration durability to enable reliable adsorbent comparisons.

title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca 2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes
abstract: Lysosomal Ca 2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca 2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca 2+ -imaging–based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca 2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca 2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca 2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca 2+ stores, diminished Ca 2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca 2+ transport, and Tmem184b -deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca 2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

title: Atmospheric O 2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990
abstract: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O 2 ) and CO 2 observations, we find that the ocean carbon sink increased by 0.63 ± 0.19 petagrams of carbon per year per decade (Pg C year −1 decade −1 ) (a mean of 2.8 ± 0.4 Pg C year −1 ), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year −1 , accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
abstract: Whether genomic data can be used to effectively predict adaptation in natural populations is unknown. Here, we tested the efficacy of genomic prediction of complex trait evolution by monitoring genome-wide allele frequencies and pigmentation variation in genetically diverse populations of Drosophila melanogaster during evolution in both field mesocosms and a controlled, lab-based setting. At two points during trait evolution, we produced a high-powered, well-resolved genotype-phenotype map that exhibited marked stability across independent populations. Although we were able to use this map to correctly infer the direction of pigmentation evolution in both the lab and field settings, the particular loci responding to selection were largely unpredictable based on the direction of trait evolution itself. Our results hold implications for the promise, and limitations, of genomic prediction.

title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.

title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
abstract: Nitrate pollution is widely perceived as a signature of human inputs. Here we show, with machine-learning reconstructed global maps, that climate aridity is also a dominant driver, systematically elevating nitrate concentrations across land-use gradients and creating unexpected hotspots beyond major agricultural and urban centers. Across ~2.9 million river segments worldwide, nitrate concentrations exceed ecological and health thresholds across ~33 and 2% of global land area, affecting ~5.6 billion (73%) and 0.5 billion (6%) people, respectively. Ecological threshold exceedance occurs mostly in headwaters, and about half of the health threshold exceedance occurs in middle-income countries and sparsely populated landscapes. These findings cast nitrate pollution as an aridity-amplified risk, suggesting that aridification may increase nitrate exposure even without additional human inputs. They call for regulatory standards that reflect risks across broad concentration ranges.

title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity
abstract: The rapid ice loss in West Antarctica since the 1990s has led to substantial ice surface lowering, regional bedrock uplift, and gravity reduction, as measured by geodetic observations. The bedrock (crustal) motions and gravity changes result from glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), a process controlled by Earth’s viscoelastic properties and deglaciation history. In this study, we present GIA models with geodynamically consistent three-dimensional mantle viscoelastic structures and reconstructed ice history for Antarctica from 1900 to 2020, which explain both the observed Global Navigation Satellite System crustal motions and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity changes in West Antarctica. This study demonstrates that a mantle rheology including a weak asthenosphere and temperature-dependent viscosity is consistent with both mantle convection at million-year timescales and ongoing decadal GIA occurring in West Antarctica.

title: Californians approve controversial $8.4 billion immunology initiative
Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris
abstract: The star β Pictoris is orbited by a dusty debris disk, within which planet formation is occurring. The outer disk is sufficiently far from the star that volatile molecules are expected to freeze into solid ices. We observed the β Pictoris disk in the near-infrared using the James Webb Space Telescope. The spectrum shows features due to amorphous water ice (<7% crystallinity) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) ice in both the 12 CO 2 and 13 CO 2 isotopologues. We infer that the CO 2 ice is intimately mixed with the water ice at a ratio of 1:10. This implies that the ices formed in cold conditions, likely in the interstellar medium. Frequent collisions within the debris disk are required to explain the observed uniform distribution of icy dust grains.

title: ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering drive extracellular vesicle budding from cilia
abstract: Cilia-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate cell-cell communication and remove signaling molecules from cilia. The Hedgehog receptor Smoothened (SMO) is selected for packaging into ciliary EVs by ubiquitin chains, but how cargo selection is coupled to EV budding remains unknown. In this work, working in mouse kidney cells, we found that the ubiquitin reader endosomal sorting complex required for transport–0 (ESCRT-0) orchestrates both cargo selection and EV biogenesis. Unlike the conventional ESCRT pathway, SMO secretion did not require the ESCRT-III membrane scission machinery. Instead, ESCRT-0 condensed at the ciliary tip, where it clustered ubiquitinated SMO to drive EV biogenesis. Disrupting ESCRT-0 condensation blocked SMO secretion, and combining forced recruitment of ESCRT-0 with optogenetic clustering of SMO was sufficient to reconstitute EV budding. Thus, ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering constitute a minimal module for ESCRT-III–independent reverse-topology budding.

Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss–like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.

title: The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA)
abstract: The Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA, https://caninecancergenomeatlas.org/ ) is an open, accessible comparative oncology resource that harmonizes whole-exome data across 10 canine tumor histotypes. It aggregates 667 tumor-normal pairs with curated single-nucleotide variants, insertions and deletions, structural variants, and copy number aberrations. Cohort-depth stratification distinguished primary, exploratory, and descriptive analyses. Selection analyses identified 39 cancer drivers, including recurrent TP53 , PIK3CA , PTEN , SETD2 , MAP3K14 , and FAT4 alterations; copy number events included MYC amplifications and PTEN deletions. Direct comparison with matched human cancers revealed conserved and species-enriched oncogenic mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic contexts. The CCGA standardizes alignment, variant calling, and annotation through consensus pipelines and provides downloadable data and interactive analyses. This reusable framework advances precision veterinary oncology and strengthens translational bridges to human cancer, supporting comparative and translational research.

Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids
abstract: Electron hydrodynamics is an emerging framework that describes dynamics of interacting electron systems as conventional fluids. Although evidence for hydrodynamic-like transport has been reported in a variety of two-dimensional materials, precise quantitative measurement of the core parameter, electron viscosity, remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate that magnetoresistance in Corbino-shaped graphene devices offers a simultaneous ohmmeter and viscosometer capability, allowing us to disentangle the individual ohmic and viscous contributions to transport, even near viscous-ohmic crossover. In both monolayer and bilayer graphene, the effective electron-electron scattering rate scales linearly with temperature, deviating markedly from the T 2 dependence expected in conventional Fermi liquids. Instead, it is consistent with a recently identified tomographic fluid regime, theoretically predicted to be generic for two-dimensional electron systems.

title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly
abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a “molecular glue,” stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain–containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This “produce-and-trap” mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

title: Tracking danger on the peaks
abstract: The Earth is warming, but not all regions are warming equally. In high mountain areas, temperatures are generally increasing by 1.5 to 2 times the global average, sometimes with devastating consequences. A small or gradual change in the mountain cryosphere—perhaps progressive thawing of frozen ground or a flood from a small glacial lake—can suddenly turn into a cascade of catastrophes with enormous ramifications. Monitoring systems for the cryosphere in high mountain areas have traditionally been designed to look at individual components and changes. What are the temperature and depth of the permafrost, or how much area is covered by snow, and what is the related avalanche danger? Many of the monitoring and warning systems were designed for historical patterns of snowfall or rainfall, and a river gauge may no longer be adequate if there is greater flow in the rainy season, or increased sediment that could damage the gauge.

title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants
abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

title: Long-term local circulation of an Andes virus lineage in northern Patagonia is linked to the M/V Hondius outbreak
abstract: In 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. Analyses revealed an unexpected relationship to an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Retrospective investigation clarified the 2018 outbreak could involve person-to-person transmission and a common ANDV lineage spanned HPS cases from 2018 to 2025 in a geographically defined area in northern Patagonia, without widespread community transmission of ANDV. Route reconstruction for the index cases in the cruise ship outbreak identified geographically plausible exposures to viruses of this lineage in Argentina, but their timing was inconsistent with the expected ANDV incubation period. The infection source for the cruise ship outbreak cannot be resolved with current information, highlighting the need to expand viral surveillance in the ANDV endemic region.

title: Early epidemiological and spatial assessment of the Bundibugyo virus outbreak 2026
abstract: A Bundibugyo virus outbreak was first reported on May 15th, 2026 in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with multiple cases reported across health zones during the early phase of the outbreak and suggestions of circulation weeks prior to detection. We pair highly resolved case and testing records with human mobility data to investigate the early outbreak dynamics of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD). We show that human movement was a principle driver of early spatial expansion between May 10th and June 1st when the number of health zones and health areas reporting positive cases increased by 12 and 49, respectively. The early doubling time was estimated at ~10 days. Our work shows the rapid spatial expansion and growth of BVD with implications for intervention strategies.

title: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome outbreak linked to cruise ship travel in April–May 2026
abstract: In April 2026, a hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) outbreak caused by Andes virus (ANDV) occurred on a cruise ship. ANDV genome sequences were obtained for 10 of the 13 identified cases during a cross-country investigation established to share initial raw data for joint analysis with reciprocal quality control. The genomic data, symptom onsets, and plausible contact patterns strongly support a tightly linked outbreak cluster compatible with a single or very few zoonotic spillover events prior to embarkment followed by human-to-human transmission onboard. The outbreak represents the international displacement of a virus already known to be capable, under specific conditions, to transmit among humans, and does not suggest emergence of a unusual viral strain.

title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space
abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment
abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

Labor Market Tightness and the Reversal of Inequality Trends in Germany
abstract: Germany experienced a sharp rise in wage inequality over the two decades leading up to the Great Recession. However, a remarkable trend reversal occurred in 2010—well before the introduction of the minimum wage in 2015—when wages at the bottom of the distribution began to grow more rapidly than those higher up. This paper attributes the reversal to an increasingly tight labor market after the Great Recession, supported by strong domestic demand, and operating through several interrelated and mutually reinforcing channels. Consistent with this hypothesis, job-to-job transition rates and between-job wage growth rose markedly after the recession, especially for workers at the lower rungs of the job ladder. Concurrently, workers increasingly moved from low-paying to higher-paying firms, compressing the worker-weighted distribution of firm wage premia. Tighter labor markets also reduced assortative matching between workers and firms, lowered the skill premium, and weakened firms’ monopsony power.

Whether and when: Women's work, birth spacing, and parity progression in late‐nineteenth‐century Derbyshire
abstract: Abstract Women's labour force participation features prominently in discussions of low birth rates and the Second Demographic Transition, and has also been hypothesized to have played a role in falling marital fertility during the First Demographic Transition. Historical data have been lacking, however, to assess these theories robustly and to distinguish between the effects of women's work on birth intervals and parity progression. This paper uses a split‐population cure model to analyse stopping and spacing by couples in late‐nineteenth‐century Derbyshire, using linked census data to demonstrate the association between women's occupations before marriage and subsequent marital fertility. Combining these linked census records and the 1911 census fertility survey, complete birth histories have been reconstructed for women who married from the 1880s onwards. The results suggest that couples in this period were controlling their fertility from the beginning of marriage via a combination of stopping and spacing, and that spacing births played a greater role in the low fertility of female textile workers than it did amongst some other occupational groups. These results provide more concrete evidence for the importance of women's labour force participation and birth spacing during the fertility transition in England and Wales.

title: The Financial Economics of Spaceflight
abstract: We present a financial economics analysis of the global Space Economy, which has surged in value and scale since 4Q2024. The combined market valuation of private and publicly traded space companies now exceeds $4.0 trillion after SpaceX’s $75 billion June 2026 IPO. Space companies made 2025 capital investments totaling $25.7 billion, despite revenues of only $87.9 billion and net losses of $20.1 billion. Commercial products and services represent three-fourths of space economy revenues, while government orders account for one-fourth. We categorize the space economy along an entrepreneurial spectrum. Massive recent declines in launch costs have transformed demand for space services. (JEL H5, L1, O3, O32, O38)

Impatience and Present Bias Do Not Determine Weight Loss in Obesity: Evidence From Lab‐in‐Field and Survey Data
abstract: A substantial body of behavioral economics literature links obesity to time preferences, notably impatience-a time-consistent preference for earlier rewards-and present bias-the disproportionate overweighting of immediate payoffs that leads to dynamic inconsistency. Unlike much previous literature, which asks whether time preferences predict weight in broader populations, we examine whether they predict subsequent weight loss among adults who already have overweight or obesity. Using clinically measured outcomes and incentivized preference data from 287 adults with obesity and pre-diabetes enrolled in a 12-month randomized lifestyle-intervention trial, we find that neither impatience nor present bias predicts reductions in body fat or BMI. These findings are robust to alternative measurement strategies and are not explained by the impatience-related attrition that we uncover. To strengthen external validity, we replicate the null relationship using self-reported time preference measures in a nationally representative sample of 7277 adults with overweight or obesity. As baseline impatience meaningfully reduces the likelihood of trial completion, we conclude that impatience affects adherence to medically recommended programs but does not directly impede weight-loss success among those who remain engaged. Interventions targeting impatience or self-control alone may therefore be insufficient to promote weight loss in clinical populations.

title: Not Just for Tech Giants: The Economic Payoff of LLM‐Measured AI Adoption in Nontechnology Firms
abstract: ABSTRACT Technology firms dominate AI narratives, but the economic implications of AI in traditional industries remain underexplored. We develop a firm‐level AI adoption indicator using ERNIE, a Chinese large language model. Using this measure, we find that AI adoption significantly enhances the value of nontechnology firms. Mechanism analyses show that AI adoption improves productivity, innovation performance and financing conditions. The effects are stronger for firms with greater dynamic capability, favourable information environments, competitive positions, larger size, private ownership and eastern regional locations. Our study provides evidence on the economic consequences of AI and a novel AI adoption measure for future research.

Ancestral Distance and the Cultural Foundations of State Capacity
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the role of long‐term population relatedness in shaping global variation in state capacity. It argues that longer periods of ancestral separation are associated with greater divergence in intergenerationally transmitted civic norms governing voluntary compliance with state institutions. Ancestral distance may also hinder the international diffusion of effective state institutions, contributing to persistent cross‐country differences in state capacity. The empirical analysis shows that countries with greater ancestral distance from the global frontier of effective state institutions exhibit lower state capacity. Dyadic regressions further indicate that ancestral distance is associated with greater divergence in state capacity. To examine a potential cultural foundation of this relationship, I exploit variation in cultural backgrounds among second‐generation immigrants residing in the same country. I find that immigrant populations with greater ancestral distance exhibit larger differences in self‐reported attitudes towards voluntary tax compliance. Taken together, the findings suggest that ancestral distance is an important historical predictor of cross‐country disparities in state capacity, consistent with a role for divergence in civic norms and barriers to institutional diffusion.

title: Liquidity, Collateral Quality, and Interest Rates a
abstract: Abstract This paper analyzes how collateral quality shocks affect banks' liquidity management and the risk‐free rate. We develop a model where banks manage liquidity through near‐cash assets and marketable securities subject to idiosyncratic and/or aggregate shocks. Collateral quality deterioration leads to nonmonotonic changes in liquidity holdings: moderate declines reduce cash holdings via lower market returns, while severe declines cause precautionary hoarding and market freezes. Reduced collateral quality depresses the risk‐free rate. Liquidity regulation and negative interest rate policies can mitigate these effects. Our findings highlight the risks of collateral quality shocks and the importance of policy complementarities in addressing liquidity issues.

title: The Added Bonus of Foreign Investments: Global Mutual Funds and Multinational Firm Returns
abstract: Abstract This paper uses global mutual funds to study foreign information dissemination across countries into multinationals’ stock prices. To invest internationally, these funds collect information from foreign countries where they invest. Such foreign information helps funds invest in U.S. multinationals operating in those same foreign countries. Global funds overweight and outperform on the selected multinationals’ stocks. They exploit market‐level, industry‐level, and firm‐specific foreign information. The trading activities of these funds accelerate the incorporation of foreign information into the selected multinationals’ prices. Our findings suggest that global mutual funds are important mechanisms for information dissemination into multinationals’ asset prices in global markets.
