Multimarket Contact and Long-Term Oriented Language in Competition
abstract: Corporate disclosure has long served as a strategic tool for managing the perceptions of audiences that shape a firm’s access to resources. Prior research has largely focused on why firms use disclosure to engage capital-market constituents such as investors and analysts, leaving open the question of when and why firms disclose for competitive purposes. Focusing on the temporal orientation of competitive strategy communication, we examine how multimarket contact (MMC) shapes firms’ use of long-term oriented language (LTL). We argue that greater MMC raises the risk of cross-market retaliation, strengthening firms’ incentives to signal a restrained competitive posture through LTL, particularly when competitive capacity is visibly constrained by poor financial performance or analyst downgrade revisions. Using a sample of 36 U.S. manufacturing firms across six industries from 2015 to 2024, we find evidence generally consistent with our predictions.

title: Authenticity in marketing: A conceptual model and meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Authenticity drives customer decision-making and firm success, yet research remains fragmented due to the diversity of conceptualizations, mediators and outcomes, and empirical contexts investigated. Utilizing the entity–referent correspondence framework, we distinguish true-to-fact, true-to-ideal, and true-to-self authenticity as antecedents of overall perceived authenticity. This conceptualization of authenticity types applies to a range of entities including brands, experiences, individuals, places, and products. Our meta-analysis, utilizing 406 independent samples and 173,577 customers, demonstrates that the most integrative model (comprising the three authenticity types and overall authenticity) performs best. It uncovers causal chains linking authenticity to mediators (positive affect, positive beliefs, relationship quality) and outcomes (satisfaction, word-of-mouth, repurchase intentions). To evaluate generalizability, we include offer-related (hedonic vs. utilitarian, durable vs. consumable, services vs. goods, human vs. non-human), market-related (online vs. offline, high vs. low coproduction), and country-specific (emerging vs. developed markets, individualism vs. collectivism) moderators. The results offer managerial guidance for aligning offerings with customer expectations.
journal_name: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science

title: The Role of Supply Chains in Climate Disclosure
abstract: ABSTRACT We examine the role of supply chains in shaping the public disclosure of climate information. We leverage a unique empirical setting enabled by CDP—the leading platform for corporate climate risk reporting—which allows customers to demand climate‐related information from their suppliers. Using a large international sample of customer–supplier pairs, we find a positive association between customers’ information demand and suppliers’ public disclosure on the CDP. While the estimated association is modest on average, it exhibits substantial cross‐sectional variation reflecting the disclosure incentives of both customers and suppliers as well as their relative bargaining power. We also find descriptive evidence consistent with one potential implication of the documented association for corporate decision‐making: shifts in supply network relationships toward greener and more transparent suppliers. Overall, our findings contribute to ongoing debates on how to foster climate disclosure.

title: Effortful vs. Opportunistic Consumption of Discretionary Time: How Time-Reporting Decisions Influence Extra-Role Effort
abstract: Employees often work under incomplete contracts, performing both contracted in-role tasks and valuable but noncontracted extra-role activities. Once employees have completed in-role tasks, discretionary time remains, which they may allocate to extra-role activities or consume opportunistically. This study examines how managers’ time-reporting decisions, as a less intrusive form of control, affect subordinates’ effort-allocation decisions. I propose two opposing predictions. First, managers’ control implementations may signal distrust, resulting in more opportunism and thus less extra-role effort. Second, I identify value signaling as a novel theoretical mechanism through which time-reporting decisions may increase extra-role effort. The main experiment manipulated two factors: the type of time report (aggregated versus disaggregated) and its implementation source (managerial choice versus random assignment) to isolate signaling effects from monitoring effects. Results reveal that when managers choose not to implement disaggregated time reporting—that is, reports that make discretionary time salient—subordinates significantly reduce their extra-role effort. Structural equation modeling shows that value signaling outweighs distrust signaling in driving employees’ effort-allocation decisions. In contrast, when the time-reporting format is randomly assigned, effort remains unchanged, underscoring the signaling role of managerial choice. An additional online experiment shows directionally consistent results with the main experiment. These findings reveal a hidden cost of not controlling and contribute to the literature on incomplete contracts, slack resources, and input-based controls in modern work contexts. This paper was accepted by Ranjani Krishnan, accounting. Funding: This work was supported by the Bijzonder Onderzoeksfonds UGent [Grant BOF/STA/202009/047]. Supplemental Material: The data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.00955 .

title: Redeploying the Jockeys: The Intermediary Role of Venture Capital in Entrepreneurial Labor Markets
Deregulation, Market Structure, and the Evolution of U.S. Banking
Colleagues That Work Together Move Together: How Co-Moving Among Newcomers Affects Individual and Team Performance
abstract: As teams and team membership become more dynamic, colleagues from the same prior team increasingly transition together to a new team as a cohort: a phenomenon known as co-moving. Drawing on theories of shared team experience and team receptivity, we develop a multilevel, multi-theory, and multi-period model to examine how co-moving affects individual and team performance. We theorize that co-movers carry forward proximal shared team experience which they can leverage immediately to support their own performance relative to solo movers, who must build new working relationships. However, we also theorize that co-movers’ proximal shared team experience hinders team performance, though these detrimental effects attenuate over time. We test our theory using archival data from the National Basketball Association, supplemented by qualitative interviews with individuals involved in professional basketball. Our findings reveal that co-movers exhibit better individual performance than solo movers on their new teams and in our robustness checks we find that greater shared tenure on the prior team further enhances this advantage. At the team level, teams with co-movers perform worse than teams with solo movers, and we find partial support that this disadvantage attenuates over time. Additional analyses show that co-movers’ individual performance advantage persists over time in the new team. The findings from our interviews illuminate how these processes unfold both on and off the court. Our research contributes to the literature on shared team experience and newcomer integration by highlighting a multilevel tradeoff: while co-moving benefits individuals, it can initially undermine collective performance.

title: Auditors’ (non)responses to public warnings of audit risk: evidence from short-selling campaigns
abstract: Using a novel setting, we examine auditors' responses to public warnings of audit risk and whether their non-responses are associated with auditor and client characteristics. Specifically, we focus on 243 short-selling campaigns from 2006 to 2020 in which short sellers make public, credible allegations of audit-related issues against listed companies. 48.3% of those companies' auditors do not take any observable actions in terms of raising audit fees substantially, terminating the engagement, issuing going concern opinions (GCO), or reporting internal control weaknesses (ICW) in the year after the short sellers' allegations. We further find that longer auditor-client tenure is the factor most consistently associated with auditors' non-response to public warnings of audit risk, a pattern arguably consistent with impaired independence. Additional analyses show that the litigation and reputation costs of auditors' inactions are minimal, further reducing auditors' incentives for responses.

title: Intertemporal Dynamics of Cost Asymmetry
abstract: ABSTRACT We study the intertemporal dynamics of asymmetric cost behavior in a competitive setting. Our analysis delves into the primitives of cost asymmetry and explores its dynamic evolution over time. The analysis yields the result that cost behavior is asymmetric by default and path‐dependent, transpiring as cost stickiness following prior resource expansion and taking the form of cost anti‐stickiness after previous resource contraction. The analysis further suggests that the magnitude of cost asymmetry, either stickiness or anti‐stickiness, is decreasing in demand uncertainty and competition intensity, increasing in adjustment costs and time discounting, and greater for small demand shocks than for large demand shocks. By highlighting cost asymmetry as a dynamic, rather than static, phenomenon, and by providing new, testable predictions regarding the direction and magnitude of cost asymmetry across firms and over time, our results offer theoretical grounding for the empirical cost asymmetry literature and may also help investors and other stakeholders interpret cost behavior in light of firms' recent history of expansion or contraction and their competitive environment.

title: Always on, always more: how a hustle mindset influences variety-seeking

title: Patience and Organization Studies: Festina lente
abstract: Modern organizations often valorize speed and immediacy, treating acceleration as the dominant temporal logic of organizational life. Challenging this logic remains difficult, however, because organization studies lacks a well-developed conceptual language for alternative ways of engaging with time. We propose patience as one such alternative. Building on recent work on Eigenzeit, we argue that organizations can partially uncouple from external temporal pressures and develop forms of relative temporal autonomy that enable the orchestration of differentiated temporalities. While Eigenzeit highlights how organizations establish and sustain a temporality of their own amid complex temporal demands, less attention has been paid to the pacing through which this temporality is enacted in everyday organizational life. We therefore foreground pacing as the practical means by which organizations enact and sustain their own temporality. Within this context, patience emerges as a particular mode of pacing grounded in purposeful deceleration. To make this mode of pacing analytically visible, we identify four manifestations of organizational patience: waiting, restraining, forbearing, and persisting. Drawing on insights from the sociology of time, organization studies, and philosophy, we show how these manifestations represent distinct ways of pacing organizational activities by holding time open, delaying intervention, staying with difficulty, and sustaining engagement over time. By reframing patience as a distinctive mode of pacing rather than passive inactivity, we show how organizations cultivate and sustain an Eigenzeit through practices that contribute to the orchestration of competing temporal demands. This perspective advances organization studies by illuminating how temporal orchestration is accomplished through everyday organizational interactions and how patience enables organizations to sustain resilience and meaningful engagement in the face of acceleration pressures.

title: Street Fights and Court Battles: Incumbent mobilization and the timing of regulatory bans against platform entrants
abstract: In this paper, we examine how incumbent-led mobilization against Uber’s platform entry in Europe relates to regulatory bans, public attention, and consumer-side uptake. Combining hand-coded data on taxi-sector tactics and frames with first regulatory bans, Uber app downloads, and Google search interest across 22 European countries from 2012 to 2020, we identify a differentiated temporal pattern. Private tactics are strongly associated with first-ban hazard in the short window following mobilization, whereas lawsuits are positively associated over a longer window. The frames incumbents deploy also matter: legitimacy-challenge frames portraying UberPop as incompatible with lawful and fair competition are more consistently associated with bans than compliance-dispute frames focused on tax or labor obligations. At the same time, private tactics and lawsuits coincide with immediate increases in app downloads and Google search interest, indicating an attention spillover from incumbent contestation. Lawsuit-related download elevations display marginally greater persistence than those associated with private tactics, although this difference is not stronger early after entry. Taken together, the findings show that incumbent mobilization in platform markets can be associated with regulatory bans and consumer-side uptake of the entrants they seek to exclude at the same time. The results establish temporal association, although the direction of influence within this process cannot be isolated.

title: Black pragmatism and organization studies
abstract: I argue for Black pragmatism’s usefulness to organization studies by intervening in debates about the normative foundations of stakeholder theory. Tracing three braided themes within Black pragmatism (tragicomic hope, critical temper, and democratic faith), I show how they both illuminate neglected aspects of the pragmatist themes of inquiry, abduction, and community that have influenced organization studies and extend those concepts to open new avenues of inquiry. I suggest that Black pragmatism reveals how the libertarian assumptions of stakeholder theory are inconsistent with its pragmatist commitments, and that this weakness even applies to recent attempts to center stakeholder theory upon marginalized stakeholders.

title: Media Review: The Experience of Everyday-Extremeness in Warfare
Consider the Dashboard: Exploring a visual medium of datafication
abstract: Dashboards are central to contemporary organizations aiming to ‘datafy’ decision making and management practices. As one of the primary media through which people engage with digital data in organizational contexts, dashboards shape how data is accessed and perceived. Despite their ubiquity, there is limited understanding of how dashboards mediate data visibility and influence observers’ perceptions of the data. Drawing on theories of mediation and diagrammatics, this paper analyzes the ‘generic form’ shared by all dashboards. It then identifies the modes of observation encouraged by dashboards, revealing how they position their observers. While grounded in theoretical arguments, the analysis incorporates empirical examples from a study on the datafication of Human Resource Management. The paper makes two key contributions. It emphasizes the critical role of visual forms in datafication processes, and it highlights the organizational implications of the use of a specific kind of visual medium: the dashboard.

title: Healing As Organizing in Solidarity Spaces: An Affective Perspective on Post-disaster Recovery
abstract: This paper examines how community-led solidarity initiatives enable healing in the aftermath of disaster. Drawing on a two-year qualitative study in post-explosion Beirut, it explores how solidarity spaces function as relational structures of repair – sites where material response and affective recovery are not separate processes but mutually constitutive ones. While post-disaster organizing research has emphasized resource mobilization and agility, and disaster studies has identified the importance of community-led recovery, neither has fully explored how organizing enables healing to unfold collectively. Addressing this gap, the study makes two contributions. First, it reframes solidarity spaces as generative holding environments: relational infrastructures that simultaneously contain suffering and enable the emergence of new social arrangements. Second, it conceptualizes healing as organizing: a distributed, collective, and enacted process through which communities transform suffering into agency. Healing, in this account, is not an individual psychological process nor an outcome that follows organizing; it is the very practice through which recovery unfolds, as participants become agents of their own material and affective transformation through acts of solidarity.

title: Utilising Green Lean Six Sigma to Improve Sustainability in the Bakery Sector
abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to improve sustainability and environmentally friendly practices in an Irish bakery by reducing carbon emissions and reducing the use of single‐use plastics. Green lean six sigma (GLSS) methodology was utilised to improve sustainability performance. The use of single‐use plastics decreased by 33.9% through the adoption of intermediate bulk containers, the installation of solar panels and the purchase of green electricity, contributing to a 5% reduction in the carbon footprint. A limitation of the study was that it was a single‐site case study, but the methodology and process to achieve waste reduction and improve sustainability are generalizable in terms of sustainability principles; the study can be benchmarked by both the food sector and other sectors. The findings contribute to both the literature and practice by highlighting the importance of developing sustainable procurement methods, enhancing supplier engagement and reducing Scope 3 emissions in sustainability programs. This study also demonstrates how an organisation can develop sustainability accounting measures and highlights the importance of deploying GLSS methods in the food industry, showing their applicability for improving sustainability and reducing waste.

title: Circular Business Model Innovation: A Systematic Review of Technology and Resource Strategy Choices
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite growing scholarly interest in circular business model innovation (CBMI), established frameworks are applied inconsistently: Few empirical studies specify how they conceptualise CBMs or the scope and degree of novelty of the business model changes reported, raising construct validity concerns that limit comparability across studies. We systematically review 101 empirical papers, following PRISMA, to examine how CBMI is conceptualised and theorised, how digital and material technologies enable it and how resource strategies are realised in practice. Although technology and resource‐strategy choices have typically been studied as independent enablers of circularity, our findings reveal interdependencies between technology and resource‐strategy choices and their association with CBM reconfiguration. We also find the reviewed studies are predominantly atheoretical, with material technologies more prevalent than digital ones, and resource strategies typically deployed in combination rather than in isolation, although these strategies compete for the same material flows, a tension the field has yet to theorise. This paper contributes to the CBMI literature by classifying CBMI's scope and degree of novelty, by proposing an integrative framework that aligns theoretical lenses with CBM conceptualisations and by outlining a future research agenda guiding scholarly and managerial decisions on technology and resource‐strategy choices.

title: Do Single Family Offices Invest Differently? Extending the Socioemotional Wealth Perspective to Entrepreneurial Investment Practices
abstract: Drawing on the socioemotional wealth (SEW) perspective and its dimensions captured in the FIRE framework, we theorize that single-family offices (SFOs) make unique tradeoffs between socioemotional and financial wealth in their entrepreneurial investment practices. Using coarsened exact matching (CEM) followed by a difference-in-differences-style matched observational comparison around the 2010 Dodd–Frank change, we find that SFOs collaborate with fewer syndicate partners, maintain narrower industry portfolios, and have longer investment horizons than institutional venture capitalists (IVCs). Among eponymous SFOs, the corresponding comparisons with IVCs show the same predicted directions. Our study contributes to the family business literature by theorizing how distinct SEW dimensions may be reflected in observable entrepreneurial investment practices by SFOs.

title: Discrimination takes its toll: unraveling employee service sabotage from a cognitive-appraisal perspective
abstract: Purpose Drawing on the cognitive appraisal theory and organizational justice theory, this paper aims to examine how organizational and customer unfairness and discrimination influence restaurant employees’ service sabotage through negative emotion and rumination, with personality traits as moderators. Design/methodology/approach Multiple quantitative studies were conducted with US restaurant employees. Study 1 examined organizational and customer discrimination separately using 300 respondents. Study 2 extended these findings with a time-lagged sample of 234 respondents by introducing perceived unfairness as an antecedent of discrimination and personality traits as moderators of the emotion–rumination process. Findings Results show that perceived unfairness contributes to perceived discrimination, which is indirectly associated with service sabotage through negative emotion and rumination. Organizational discrimination showed a more consistent pattern than customer discrimination. Personality effects were limited, with only extraversion moderating the emotion–rumination process. Originality/value Although service sabotage is well documented in restaurants, how discrimination leads to such behavior remains less understood. This study explains how perceived unfairness develops into discrimination, which is associated with negative emotion, rumination and service sabotage. By comparing organizational and customer sources, it reveals source-specific differences and the limited role of personality as a boundary condition.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Promotion focus, growth i-deals and service creativity: a regulatory focus perspective
abstract: Purpose Given that content- and timing-based idiosyncratic deals (i-deals) are inherently heterogeneous across employees and contexts, this study shifts attention to motivation-oriented growth i-deals. Drawing on regulatory focus theory (RFT) and the ability–motivation–opportunity (AMO) model, the study seeks to examine the antecedents, outcomes, chain mediating paths and boundary conditions of growth i-deals. Design/methodology/approach Multiwave, multisource and multilevel data were collected from 600 frontline employees in 100 hotel and mall teams in China. A cross-level moderated mediation model was tested using multilevel path analysis in Mplus and 20,000 Monte Carlo simulations. Findings Four key findings have been obtained. First, promotion focus is positively associated with growth i-deals. Second, growth i-deals positively predict three AMO variables (creative self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation and perceived participation opportunity) that further promote service creativity. Third, team-level servant leadership moderates the main effect of promotion focus on growth i-deals. Finally, team-level servant leadership moderates the indirect effects of promotion focus on service creativity via the chain mediation path of growth i-deals and three AMO variables. The main effect and the indirect effects are stronger when team-level servant leadership is high rather than low. Practical implications Hotel firms should attend to employees’ underlying developmental motives and effectively channel their developmental aspirations through i-deals. Furthermore, hotel firms should place greater emphasis on cultivating servant leaders by encouraging managers to exhibit servant leadership behaviors and providing leadership training. Originality/value This study broadens the scope of i-deals research from traditional focus on i-deals content and timing to the focus on i-deals motivation. Moreover, the study extends RFT and AMO model by investigating the antecedent, outcome, mechanisms and contingencies of growth i-deals, particularly in hospitality and related service settings.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: The AI engagement paradox: algorithmic congruence and its inverted-U effect on tourist experience quality
abstract: Purpose Despite widespread adoption of AI agents in restaurant and gastronomic tourism settings across Asia, practitioners consistently observe a counterintuitive pattern: increasing AI service involvement initially enhances but subsequently undermines tourist experience quality. This study aims to term this the “AI engagement paradox” and introduce algorithmic hospitality congruence (AHC), a new second-order construct to theorise and empirically confirm the inverted-U relationship between AI congruence and gastronomic tourist experience quality (GTEQ). Design/methodology/approach A sequential exploratory mixed-methods design was used across three Asian markets (Hong Kong, Singapore, Bangkok). Phase 1 comprised 24 semi-structured interviews using the critical incident technique to develop AHC construct items. Phase 2 involved a quantitative survey (N = 412). AHC was grounded in cognitive load theory (CLT). Polynomial regression with response surface methodology confirmed the inverted-U effect; partial least squares structural equation modelling validated the construct. Common-method-bias mitigation and endogeneity-robustness checks used temporal separation, Harman’s single-factor test with a marker variable and Gaussian copula endogeneity correction. Findings AHC comprising culinary AI precision (CAP), emotional service resonance and cultural contextual fit (CCF) demonstrated robust construct and discriminant validity. AHC exhibited a significant inverted-U effect on GTEQ. Cultural collectivism steepened the negative slope, while digital literacy shifted the tipping point rightward. Research limitations/implications This study delivers empirically grounded deployment guidance for hospitality operators in AI-integrated gastronomic settings. The validated 15-item AHC scale provides a diagnostic instrument for monitoring AI-experience alignment. Operators are advised to benchmark their AHC composite score against the estimated tipping-point zone (4.18–5.04 on a seven-point scale), differentiate deployment intensity by tourist digital literacy, apply conservative ceiling margins for high-collectivist segments and treat CCF as a foundational design requirement rather than a localisation afterthought. Digital literacy investment is reframed as a direct hospitality revenue strategy. Originality/value This is among the first studies to theorise and empirically confirm an inverted-U effect of AI congruence in gastronomic tourism. AHC is rigorously differentiated from five related constructs and grounded in CLT from the outset. The findings challenge the linear AI benefit assumption dominant in hospitality AI research and provide indicative deployment guidance for practitioners.

title: The sovereign reliance privacy framework: balancing privacy and personalization in AI-driven B2B banking
Innovation by different means: exploring perceived firm-innovativeness archetypes
abstract: Purpose By integrating four innovation signals (changes in the offering, social innovation, digital innovation, and marketing communications) into a unified framework, this study explores how different combinations of these signals shape customers' innovativeness perceptions in the service sector. Design/methodology/approach This exploratory study uses a large-scale dataset (N = 18,000) from the 2025 Spanish Innovation Index and employs a multi-stage design. First, we use regression analyses to examine the proposed relationships and identify each driver's relative importance. Second, we conduct a k-means cluster analysis to identify strategic archetypes. Finally, we utilize an interpretive analysis of “deviant cases” to illustrate cluster-specific managerial implications. Findings At the aggregate level, social innovation emerges as the most relevant driver of customers perceived firm innovativeness (PFI). Digital innovation is the second most important driver, followed by changes in offerings and marketing communication. Our analysis identifies four PFI archetypes: digital and technology-led innovators, social and close-touch innovators, core-offering-led innovators with a social-digital balance, and social-led innovators. Finally, it provides insights into the success factors of PFI and the barriers faced by deviant cases (the highest and lowest performers) within the same archetype. Practical implications The study suggests the need to move beyond generic benchmarking. Managers can identify their companies' strategic archetypes and begin to benchmark against their respective clusters. High PFI depends on consistent signals. Therefore, managers can use marketing communications to align the company's efforts with value-in-use narratives. Originality/value This study shifts the focus from isolated antecedents to a broader, pattern-based view of PFI by integrating four innovation signals into a unified framework. It offers an empirical contribution by combining these four antecedents and deriving clusters of firms, thereby suggesting an alternative perspective to the traditional rankings provided by innovation indexes.

EXPRESS: Royston-isms: Lifelong Provocations from a Noted Organization Theorist
abstract: Royston Greenwood (1944-2026) was a founder of Strategic Organization and one of the field’s most original, influential and appreciated organizational theorists. We pay tribute to his contribution to the field by highlighting and reflecting on some of his most insightful and pithy provocations that we label “Royston-isms.” These include both public reflections that distill his approach to scholarship and theorizing more generally (Where’s the organization? Know your rat. What’s the aha?), as well as more private and personal Royston-isms that he used in interactions with colleagues, co-authors, students and mentees (Is this institutional? Why are you studying that?! You don’t want to be just a methodologist. Just get on with it!). We show how these Royston-isms were enacted in Royston’s own work, we relate them to ideas from the philosophy of science, and we argue for their ongoing relevance to scholars of strategic organization.

title: The Dark Side of Mindfulness at Work: How Mindfulness Training Enlivens Machiavellian Incivility
abstract: Organizational mindfulness interventions are widely thought to enhance ethical awareness, self-regulation, and prosocial work behavior. Yet emerging research suggests that their effects may be more contingent than commonly assumed. In this paper, I theorize that mindfulness training can yield ethically problematic outcomes for employees who are high in dispositional Machiavellianism. Findings from a large multi-wave field experiment with both active and passive control conditions support this account. Results show that mindfulness training enlivened Machiavellians’ contempt, anger, and disgust (collectively termed affective condemnation ) for their coworkers. This, in turn, translated into higher levels of enacted workplace incivility—a subtle, deniable form of interpersonal mistreatment. By contrast, consistent with Machiavellians’ calculated and reputation-conscious proclivities, the corresponding conditional indirect effect on interpersonal deviance was not significant. These effects remained robust when accounting for generalized negative affect, other dark personality traits, and several theoretically distinct, plausible alternative mechanisms. By identifying Machiavellianism as a critical boundary condition, this research challenges the assumption that organizational mindfulness interventions are ethically neutral or unwaveringly prosocial. More broadly, it reveals that mindfulness training can exert ethically contingent effects by enlivening dispositionally grounded condemnatory affect, underscoring the importance of considering how employee personality shapes the ethical consequences of organizational mindfulness interventions.

Profiles also differed across social and psychological well-being. Our results emphasize the need for targeted interventions to improve satisfaction and well-being among distinct subgroups of the LGBTQA+ population.

title: Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Theory-Aligned Social Science Content Analysis: Evidence From Collaborative Learning Discourse
abstract: Theory-based content analysis is central to social science research, but coding context-dependent interactional discourse remains difficult to scale. This study examines whether fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) can support theory-aligned, episode-level coding of complex social interaction, using socially shared metacognitive regulation (SSMR) in collaborative learning discourse as a demanding empirical case. Using a human-coded dataset of 2,372 discourse episodes from undergraduate collaborative problem-solving, we adapted the large language model content analysis (LACA) framework through an AI-aligned codebook, prompt design, and supervised fine-tuning. Prompt-only and fine-tuned models were compared across episode-level classification and multilayer SSMR coding. Fine-tuned models substantially improved agreement with human coding and predictive performance relative to prompt-only baselines. Performance was strongest for episode-level classification and several higher-support coding layers, whereas errors remained concentrated in sparse, boundary-prone, and highly interpretive categories requiring social-intent reconstruction and temporally unfolding context. The findings extend recent work on LLM-assisted qualitative and content analysis by showing both the promise and limits of supervised, theory-aligned automation for multilayer social interaction coding. Overall, the study supports a human-centered approach to LLM-assisted content analysis, in which automated coding can support more stable coding tasks while human expertise remains essential for ambiguous, boundary-prone, and interpretively demanding judgments.

Quantitative Fish Biomonitoring by an Enhanced eDNA Metabarcoding Approach
abstract: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA)-based technologies have been increasingly employed in biodiversity surveys and ecological status assessments. However, most eDNA metabarcoding studies rely on relative read abundance, which limits their utility for quantitative environmental management and decision-making. To address this, we developed a quantitative calibration method incorporating dual internal standards: one added prior to DNA extraction and a three-concentration gradient added prior to PCR amplification, enabling independent correction of efficiencies for both steps. Results showed that within the tested aquatic matrices, DNA extraction efficiency had a greater impact on species quantification than PCR amplification efficiency. The dual internal standard calibration outperformed the single internal standard approach in both controlled laboratory experiments and field aquaculture ponds. The spiking of dual internal standards demonstrated excellent calibration across a wide range (2.4–54.1%), indicating that the method is broadly applicable and expandable without altering species detection. Field biomonitoring in the Yangtze River revealed that calibrated eDNA monitoring enhanced the spatial distribution patterns of an endangered species (Leiocassis longirostris) and a migratory species (Coilia nasus). Overall, calibrating DNA extraction and PCR amplification efficiency significantly improves the technical precision of eDNA quantification. While it strongly correlates with biomass under controlled conditions, in field applications, this dual calibration provides a robust analytical baseline that, when combined with ecological models, will be valuable for biodiversity conservation and ecological assessment. Pilot optimization of internal standard spiking volume is recommended for field surveys to balance sequencing cost and quantitative performance.

title: Long-Term PM2.5 Exposure Promoted Vascular Calcification through XBP1s-Associated Osteogenic Switching and Inflammatory Crosstalk
abstract: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a major environmental risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the mechanisms underlying long-term exposure-induced vascular calcification remain incompletely understood. Whether PM2.5 directly participates in mineral nucleation remains unclear. We found that PM2.5 accelerated the transformation of amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) into crystalline hydroxyapatite (HAP) and may act as a heterogeneous nucleation interface under simulated physiological conditions. Mice were exposed to environmentally relevant PM2.5 concentrations (5 or 35 μg/m3) for 180 days using a whole-body inhalation system. Long-term PM2.5 exposure increased arterial stiffness and promoted vascular remodeling and calcification. Mechanistically, PM2.5 increased XBP1s expression in mouse aortic smooth muscle cells (MOVAS), promoting proliferative and osteogenic phenotypic switching. Genetic deletion of Xbp1 markedly attenuated PM2.5-induced MOVAS proliferation, migration, osteogenic transformation, and mineralization. In addition, PM2.5-stimulated MOVAS acquired a pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype that promoted macrophage recruitment and M1 polarization, whereas Xbp1 deficiency attenuated these effects. We also established a human iPSC-derived blood vessel organoid (BVO)-macrophage coculture system and found that macrophages substantially amplified PM2.5-induced osteogenic remodeling and calcification. Collectively, these findings revealed the involvement of both physicochemical mineralization and XBP1-associated osteogenic and inflammatory responses in PM2.5-induced vascular calcification, providing new insights into the mechanisms underlying PM2.5-associated vascular injury.

title: Unignorable Role of Iron Redox and Microbial Adaptation in Mediating Arsenic-Induced Suppression of Carbon Emissions in Paddy Soils
abstract: Abstract Arsenic (As) contamination disturbs organic carbon (OC) cycling in paddy soils, potentially influenced by microbial adaptive evolution and redox-active iron (Fe). Here, the association of As with C emissions (CH4 and CO2), microbes, and Fe dynamics in flooded paddy soils was investigated via microcosm experiments across two As levels (20 and 200 mg kg–1). Results showed that As contamination markedly inhibited CH4 (>90%) and CO2 (>38%) emissions, accompanied by inhibited ferric reduction, decreased OC bioavailability, and shifted microbial communities toward As-tolerant and oligotrophic strategies. Correlation analysis and validation experiments demonstrated that Fe reduction covaried negatively with available As but positively with C bioavailability indicators (p < 0.001). The suppressed C emissions under low-dose As were closely linked to perturbed Fe redox cycling, while high-dose As appeared to amplify this inhibition through additional microbial toxicity and community restructuring. Exogenous zerovalent iron increased CH4 emissions by 0.92–19.54-fold through coupled changes in As immobilization, redox conditions, C bioavailability, and abundance of Fe-reducing bacteria and methanogens. This work indicated that Fe redox and microbial adaptation are important contributors to As-mediated suppression of C emissions, providing evidence for the As–Fe–C nexus and offering insights for balancing As remediation with C emission mitigation.

title: Spectroscopic Insights into Ion Pairing in Sulfate Electrolytes: Implications for Sorption in Aqueous Systems
abstract: Abstract Ion pairing, including contact, solvent-shared, and solvent-separated ion pairs (CIPs, SIPs, and SSIPs, respectively), affects aqueous reaction chemistry, sorption, and precipitation processes. Accurate characterization of ion pairing in aqueous sulfate electrolytes is essential for understanding their thermodynamics and hydration structure, yet comprehensive quantification across aqueous and mixed-solvent systems remains limited. We combine Raman spectroscopy with dielectric spectroscopy, using waveguide-based setups (WR-62 and WR-28, applied for the first time) and a broadband probe station (10 MHz–50 GHz), to characterize ion pairing and solvent–solute interactions in monovalent cation sulfate salts in water and water/methanol solutions. Dielectric spectroscopy resolved SSIP and SIP fractions, with SSIPs dominating Li2SO4 and Na2SO4. Raman spectroscopy quantified CIPs (K2SO4 > Na2SO4 ≈ Li2SO4), consistent with cation hydration and polarizability. Methanol increased SIP and CIP concentrations. Ion association stability constants and mean activity coefficients were calculated with Archer’s form of the Pitzer model, incorporating short-range binary and ternary ion–ion interactions. This approach predicts mean activity coefficients at elevated ionic strengths without double-counting ion-pairing contributions, enabling determination of stability constants and aqueous speciation. Resolving ion-pair speciation is important for accurate thermodynamic models of sulfate-bearing waters relevant to membrane separations and resource recovery.

title: A Scenario-Based Probabilistic First-Tier Screening of Potential Chemical Risk to European Groundwater Ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Groundwater supplies much of the freshwater used by humans while supporting highly specialized biological communities characterized by high endemism and limited taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic redundancy. Yet European Union groundwater legislation remains resource-oriented and addresses the ecological consequences of chemical contamination only indirectly. We conducted a continent-wide, first-tier screening of potential chemical risk to European groundwater ecosystems. Harmonized European surface water and groundwater monitoring data were combined with geostatistical interpolation and transport modeling to estimate contaminant concentrations at the groundwater table, while uncertainty in hydrogeological conditions, chemical fate, and preferential transport was propagated through Monte Carlo simulations. We compared a Surface Water Baseline scenario, based on model-derived groundwater concentrations and existing freshwater regulatory thresholds, with a Groundwater-Informed Conservative scenario integrating measured groundwater concentrations, groundwater-fauna toxicity data, and precautionary adjustments where groundwater-specific evidence was unavailable. Potential risk was summarized as the average frequency of exceedance (AFE) across contaminants and uncertainty realizations; its maps indicate the frequency and spatial distribution of threshold exceedances, not their magnitude or the severity of ecological damage. Mean AFE was low under the baseline scenario but increased 5-fold under the conservative scenario, revealing areas in the medium-to-very-high screening classes in the Pyrenean–Catalan sector, Sierra Nevada, and the eastern Balkan–Carpathian region. The framework provides a replicable basis for prioritizing monitoring, ecotoxicological testing, and management.

title: Gradient-Charge Oxygen Vacancy Pairs Enable Synergistic Activation of O2 and H2O for Low-Temperature CH3CN Emission Control
abstract: Abstract Acetonitrile (CH3CN) emitted from industrial production severely threatens atmospheric quality due to its persistence and high toxicity. While selective catalytic oxidation (SCO) represents the most promising technology for CH3CN elimination, the inherent competition between O2-activated oxidation and H2O-activated hydrolysis pathways has long prevented the simultaneous achievement of excellent low-temperature activity and high N2 selectivity. Herein, we report a Cu-modified TiO2 catalyst and propose a Cu-induced gradient-charge oxygen vacancy pair structure (Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti) as the most plausible active site configuration that enables activation of O2 and H2O via electron filling of their antibonding orbitals to promote the reaction during CH3CN oxidation. The electron-rich OVR site can adsorb both O2 and H2O, donating electrons to populate the π* antibonding orbital of O2 and the σ* antibonding orbital of H2O. Meanwhile, the electron-poor OVP site adsorbs O2 or H2O and serves as a reservoir to sustain a continuous supply of active species. The optimized catalyst induced by Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti structure achieves complete CH3CN conversion at 220 °C with 96% N2 selectivity. This work highlights the critical role of electron configuration in tailoring oxygen vacancy functions, providing a general strategy for developing advanced environmental catalysts for practical CH3CN emission control.

title: Nanoconfinement Controls Hydrogen Transport in Shales
abstract: Abstract Underground hydrogen storage (UHS) in sedimentary formations requires understanding how hydrogen migrates, persists, and is released under nanoscale confinement in fine-grained rocks that may act as reservoirs or caprocks. Here, we combine in situ small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) with molecular dynamics simulations to examine how wetting state controls hydrogen reversibility and postcycling pore occupancy in shale nanopores. SANS-derived pore-size distributions reveal a clear hierarchy: dry shale exhibits near-complete reversibility, decane-saturated shale shows partial recovery, and water-saturated shale displays minimal recovery, with persistent postcycling occupancy concentrated in pores <2 nm. Molecular simulations support a mechanistic interpretation in which this hierarchy arises from coupled nanoscale effects, including cavity-formation penalties, confinement-induced stress anisotropy, and fluid-specific interfacial free-energy barriers at mineral and organic surfaces. Water-saturated nanopores are associated with strong thermodynamic and mechanical constraints consistent with reduced hydrogen reversibility, whereas these constraints are substantially weaker in dry pores and intermediate in decane-filled pores. Together, the experimental and molecular simulation results provide a framework linking nanoscale fluid–rock interactions to hydrogen hysteresis and retention, with implications for subsurface hydrogen recoverability and containment in underground storage systems.

title: Maternal 6PPD-Quinone Exposure is Associated with Infant Neurodevelopmental Delay: Epidemiological Evidence and Mechanistic Insights from a Birth Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Tire-derived p-phenylenediamines (PPDs) and their quinone derivatives (PPD-Qs) have emerged as potential neurotoxicants, yet the associations of prenatal exposure with offspring neurodevelopment remain underexplored. Therefore, we conducted a nested case-control study within a prospective birth cohort (n = 1,317) and measured ten urinary PPDs/PPD-Qs at 6–16 weeks of gestation. In the primary adjusted model, higher urinary concentrations of 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) and N,N′-di(o-tolyl)-p-phenylenediamine (DTPD) were associated with higher odds of neurodevelopmental delay. Quantile g-computation further indicated that a simultaneous one-quartile increase in all components of the PPDs/PPD-Qs mixture was associated with higher odds of neurodevelopmental delay (odds ratio = 1.33, 95% confidence interval: 1.03–1.72). Random forest analysis identified 6PPD-Q as having the highest variable importance among the measured PPDs/PPD-Qs. Network toxicology analysis implicated dopaminergic, serotonergic, and glutamatergic neurotransmission pathways as potentially relevant to 6PPD-Q-associated neurodevelopmental toxicity. In bEnd.3 mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells, 6PPD-Q exposure induced transcriptomic alterations involving xenobiotic metabolism, inflammatory signaling, and neurotransmission-related pathways. These changes were accompanied by decreased mRNA expression of the blood–brain barrier tight junction–related genes ZO-1 and occludin. Collectively, these epidemiological associations and complementary mechanistic findings support the biological plausibility of 6PPD-Q-associated developmental neurotoxicity and warrant further investigation and independent replication.

title: Strategies for Eliminating Heavy Air Pollution in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region: Insights from Joint Practices during the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games
abstract: Abstract The 2022 Olympic Winter Games (OWG) and Paralympic Winter Games (PWG) marked the first time the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region implemented joint air pollution prevention and control measures for a winter mega-event. Notably, while Beijing maintained clean air (daily PM2.5 concentration ≤ 75 μg/m3, according to the Ambient Air Quality Standards in effect at the time) during the OWG, a heavy-pollution episode occurred during the PWG, with the 24-h average PM2.5 concentration peaking at 155 μg/m3. Combining field observations, dynamic emission characterization, and The Comprehensive Air quality Model with extensions (CAMx) simulations, we conducted a closed-loop study to investigate the underlying causes of this episode. Results show that while the industrial sector effectively regulated emissions, the mobile-source activity levels recovered rapidly after the Chinese New Year, outweighing the control measures implemented for mobile sources. This recovery increased total NOx emissions by 13% in the BTH region, driving nitrate-dominated PM2.5 pollution. During the study period, the PM2.5 nitrate concentration (normalized by the carbon monoxide concentration) was found to increase by 3 × 10–4 and 1 × 10–5 for each one-ton increase in NOx emissions in Beijing and the BTH region, respectively. To eliminate heavy PM2.5 pollution under the meteorological conditions observed during the PWG, NOx emissions would need to be further reduced by ≥1% in Beijing and ≥7% in the BTH region. This work underscores the urgent need to mitigate emissions from diesel trucks and nonroad machinery, especially under extremely adverse meteorological conditions in the BTH region.

title: Evaluating Pollution Prevention Effectiveness for Toxic Substances in Canada Using Advanced Difference-in-Differences Methods
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the effectiveness of pollution prevention (P2) activities using facility-level data from Canada’s National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) over 1993–2024. Leveraging recent advances in causal inference methodology that account for staggered treatment adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects, this Difference-in-Differences (DiD) analysis moves beyond conventional DiD to identify substantial heterogeneity in P2 impacts across time, sectors, regions, P2 activities, and substances. Key findings indicate analysis of staggered adoption matters, with cohort-specific release reductions ranging widely, and larger effects among earlier adoption cohorts (2001–2003 ∼0-76 vs 2021 ∼3%). P2 adoption is associated with an average 19% reduction in pollutant releases. In contrast, P2 activities are associated with a near-zero and statistically insignificant increase in waste. P2 is more effective for releases to water, and within specific sectors such as Mining and Quarrying and Conventional Oil and Gas extraction. Stronger effects are observed for activities related to Inventory Management/Purchasing, and in Ontario, Alberta, and Quebec, and for VOCs. Despite study limitations, the results suggest that P2 delivers net environmental benefits overall and highlight the importance of modern causal inference methods for evaluating P2 policies in settings with staggered treatment adoption, such as the NPRI.

title: Impacts of Biological Filtration on Disinfection Byproduct Control during Drinking Water Purification: A Critical Review
abstract: Abstract Biofiltration, particularly biological activated carbon and sand filtration, is widely implemented as a low-chemical, energy-efficient barrier to attenuate disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors. However, biofilters are living, time-evolving ecosystems that can transition from a net “sink” to a net “source” of reactive precursors. This review synthesized evidence that biofiltration exhibits selective removal: hydrophobic and high-molecular-weight C-DBP precursors are preferentially removed, whereas hydrophilic N-DBP (e.g., HANs, NDMA) precursors readily break through and may be newly produced. The authors clarified the mechanistic basis of precursor generation, highlighting (i) biofilm turnover that releases intracellular organic matter enriched in amines and nucleic acids, (ii) continuous production and sloughing of soluble microbial products and extracellular polymeric substances that elevate protein-like DON, and (iii) media aging and stratification that diminish removal efficacy. Regression analysis estimated sink–source transition for N-DBP precursor removal at approximately log10(bed volumes) = 5.38 (∼240,000 bed volumes), a practical reference in drinking water treatment plants. Furthermore, the authors identified critical operational tipping points, including oxidant pre-exposure, temperature fluctuations, and nutrient stoichiometry, that can trigger this functional inversion. Finally, a risk-oriented framework is proposed, advocating for precursor-specific monitoring (e.g., fluorescence signatures) and intelligent process control to stabilize biofilter performance against emerging genotoxic risks.

title: Global Analysis and Prediction of Bicarbonate in Groundwater under Climate Change
abstract: Abstract Bicarbonate (HCO3–) is a major contributor to the alkalinity of groundwater, and low concentrations can reduce buffering capacity and increase the potential susceptibility of water to corrosion-related quality deterioration, particularly in untreated groundwater systems with corrosion-prone infrastructure. Here, we use machine learning and a comprehensive data set of 28,902 groundwater samples from 80 countries to produce a global probability map of HCO3– concentrations below 80 mg/L and estimate the population residing within the Low-Alkalinity Corrosion Risk Potential Zone (LACRPZ). From 2000 to 2020, LACRPZ was mainly concentrated in Southeast Asia and South America, with approximately 704 million people residing within these zones, particularly in Oceania (52.92%) and South America (35.09%). Although the area of LACRPZ is projected to decline under future climate change, the resident population in LACRPZ is expected to increase. This study reveals the evolution of global groundwater bicarbonate concentrations and resident population, underscoring the importance of integrating bicarbonate into water safety management strategies.

title: Aldehyde-philic Portal Engineering of γ-Cyclodextrin MOF for Synergistic Capture of Toluene and Formaldehyde in Humid Atmospheric Environments
abstract: Abstract Efficient removal of multicomponent volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from real environments remains challenging, particularly under humidity. This study introduces an “aldehyde-philic portal modification” strategy that precisely anchors dopamine (DA) at γ-cyclodextrin-based metal–organic framework (γ-CD-MOF) outer rim via H-bonding to construct oligomeric polydopamine (o-PDA) structures. This pore design partitions the cyclodextrin cavity into an aldehyde-philic outer rim and arene-philic interior for efficient synergistic capture of formaldehyde and toluene in humidity. Exposed pyrrolic N sites on o-PDA enable γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 to preferentially bind CH2O, which then act as new sites to enhance subsequent C7H8 capture via CH−π interactions while hindering H2O binding to peripheral hydroxyls and preventing large-sized water clusters from blocking cavity openings. Furthermore, the hydrophobic inner cavity exhibits strong π–π conjugation with C7H8, facilitating its diffusion and establishing an “outer capture–inner fixation” pathway, significantly enhancing toluene capacity. At ∼40% relative humidity, the toluene working capacity of γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 in the multicomponent system increased by 106% over the single-component system, while the formaldehyde capacity remained unchanged. Consequently, the total working capacity of toluene and formaldehyde reached twice the sum of their single-component adsorption capacities, demonstrating marked synergistic coadsorption. This work provides a feasible approach for controlling multicomponent VOCs in complex humid atmospheric environments.

title: Turning Abandoned Mines into Carbon Sinks: Laboratory Demonstration of CO2 Hydrate Sequestration in Cold-Region Goafs under Permafrost Conditions
abstract: Abstract Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is a key technology for carbon neutrality, but conventional CO2 geological sequestration suffers from high injection pressure, limited stability, and restricted storage space. Hydrate-based CO2 sequestration offers high capacity, low cost, and intrinsic safety. This study proposes a novel in situ CO2 hydrate formation and sequestration method in coal mine goafs containing permafrost layers in cold regions. The natural low-temperature permafrost environment provides favorable conditions for hydrate formation, while goafs offer large storage space. To avoid hydrate plugging and improve engineering feasibility, a liquid-first CO2 constant-pressure supply and predissolution mode was adopted. We simulated goaf conditions at depths of 110–130 m and ∼1 MPa. Experiments tested three injection temperatures (293.15, 298.15, and 303.15 K) and five goaf temperatures (269.15–277.15 K) using tetrahydrofuran and tryptophan as promoters. Results proved efficient sequestration at a low pressure of 1 MPa. Under optimal conditions (injection temperature of 298.15 K, goaf temperature of 271.15 K), capacity reached 60.9 mmol of CO2/mol of water (mmol/mol) with an efficiency of 135.36 (kg·m–3)/MPa. The 26.7 h stability experiments under depressurization showed 4.21–16.09 mmol/mol dissociated initially, but 66.38%–90.77% CO2 remained sequestered. Further, one-month tests under the pressure-release condition revealed hydrate dissociation almost stopped after day 1, yielding a 65.32% permanent sequestration ratio. Crucially, under the pressure-maintained condition, the system continued to form CO2 hydrates over the 30-day period, resulting in an additional 31.04% CO2 storage. These results validate the feasibility and long-term stability of this novel approach.

title: Near-Real-Time Mapping of Seamless All-Hour Aerosol Optical Depth in China
abstract: Abstract Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is central to assessing aerosol climate forcing and air quality, yet persistent cloud cover and the absence of nighttime satellite retrievals preclude seamless, all-hour monitoring. Here, we develop an automated machine-learning framework that fuses a newly available gridded visibility data set with forecast AOD and spatiotemporal covariates to reconstruct AOD over China at an hourly 5 km resolution in near-real-time. Trained on geostationary satellite observations, the model achieves robust performance (Pearson correlation coefficient R = 0.95 in cross-validation) and outperforms reanalysis and forecast products while filling cloud- and darkness-induced gaps. Independent validation against MODIS and ground-based nighttime Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) measurements yields consistent accuracy (MODIS R = 0.61 and AERONET R = 0.76), confirming physical generalizability. The resulting seamless record exposes a pronounced diurnal cycle with a midday minimum and an early morning maximum, and documents a consistent year-on-year decline from 2020 to 2022 that aligns with China’s clean-air actions and COVID-19 lockdowns. During a record-breaking dust storm, the framework tracks aerosol dynamics during cloud-obscured and nocturnal phases, capturing an uninterrupted process-level account of the event. By delivering the day–night aerosol continuum at high resolution and low latency, this work bridges a critical observational gap in air-quality response, data assimilation, and diurnal aerosol-climate research.

title: TP-Agent: An Auditable LLM Agent for Predicting Pollutant Transformation Products in Oxidative Water Treatment
abstract: Abstract Predicting the transformation products (TPs) of organic micropollutants is important for characterizing their chemical fate during oxidative water treatment and prioritizing candidate structures for high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis. Limited labeled data and diverse reaction pathways make this task challenging. TP-Agent combines a large language model (LLM), training-only analog retrieval, and executable atom/bond edits to rank TP candidates with inspectable structural records. On 231 standardized-parent-disjoint reactions, TP-Agent achieved 78.8% strict Top-5 accuracy, compared with 65.8% for the bare LLM, 76.2% for standalone retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and 56.3 ± 1.5% for TP-Transformer across three training seeds. Parent-clustered bootstrap analysis supported the gain over the bare LLM; the 2.6-percentage-point difference from RAG was not statistically significant. Retrieval supplied most of the accuracy gain, while graph execution added candidate-linked structural records. Among 1095 candidates, 92.7% had exact edit-replay or deterministic-projection records, measuring structural linkage rather than mechanistic validity. Where available, candidate-linked LLM rationales provide chemical hypotheses for inspection. Estimated parallel latency and API-equivalent cost were 3.5 and 7.4 times those of RAG, respectively. TP-Agent thus combines TP candidate ranking with traceable structural operations and inspectable chemical hypotheses for HRMS follow-up.

Relationship Between Environmental Factors and Plant Distribution and Diversity in the North African Sahara Region: The Case of Tunisian Senghar‐Jabess National Park
abstract: ABSTRACT The environmental factors influencing plant community composition in North African deserts are still not well described. This study evaluates the impact of environmental variables on vegetation structure in Senghar‐Jabess National Park (2804 km 2 ), a protected area situated in the hyper‐arid Sahara of southern Tunisia. Data collection was carried out from March 2023 to February 2024 in Senghar‐Jabess National Park using quantitative quadrat sampling. The study recorded 17 plant species belonging to 12 families. Ward's hierarchical clustering identified three distinct groups: erg and sandy soils (Group 1), sandy regs (Group 2), and skeletal soils (Group 3). Across 20 abiotic variables, elevation, annual mean temperature, and distance to water sources accounted for 39%, 33%, and 24% of the variation among groups, respectively. Canonical correspondence analysis indicated that pH, electrical conductivity, distance to water sources, and UTM Northing significantly affected species composition ( p < 0.01). Fine sand and silt contents were diagnostic as important secondary gradients. The results demonstrate that geomorphological and edaphic factors influence species assembly in this extreme desert environment. The ordination also supports the hypothesis that erosion‐induced texture changes act as powerful abiotic filters shaping community composition. The CCA results demonstrate that erosion‐induced shifts in soil texture are fundamental drivers of vegetation differentiation and land degradation dynamics in desert ecosystems. These findings offer an ecological foundation for biodiversity conservation and sustainable land degradation management in the Saharan ecosystem.

title: Unraveling the Driving Mechanisms Behind Spatial–Temporal Evolution of Low‐Efficiency Cropland in Wildland‐Urban Interface: Evidence From Wuhan, China
abstract: ABSTRACT Cropland fragmentation and abandonment are critical global issues which have hindered the improvement of cropland utilization efficiency, undermining agricultural sustainability. In the context of rapid urbanization, cropland efficiency, especially within the wildland‐urban interface (WUI), is facing increasing challenges. Taking the WUI of Wuhan city as the research area, this study comprehensively incorporates cropland fragmentation and cropland abandonment to quantitatively evaluate the degree of low‐efficiency cropland. On this basis, the XGBoost‐SHAP model is adopted to systematically explore the driving mechanisms from natural and socio‐economic dimensions. The results show that: (1) During 2004–2024, the WUI expanded significantly, with a stabilizing growth rate since 2014. (2) Cropland fragmentation is the primary manifestation of low efficiency of cropland in the WUI, and cropland abandonment initially increased but later decreased. Both of them exhibit spatial heterogeneity in northern and southern Wuhan. (3) The distribution centroid of low‐efficiency cropland has been shifting to the northeast direction since 2014. (4) Low‐efficiency cropland in WUI stems from complex interactions, with spatial conflict between construction land and cropland playing a dominant role, while the influence of natural factors gradually diminishes over time. This study has important implications for identifying urban fringe areas and optimizing land‐use efficiency.

title: Agroforestry, Climate Resilience, and Land Degradation in OECD Economies: Roles of Innovation and Finance
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the growing prominence of agroforestry practices in environmental research, its specific impact on climate‐induced land vulnerability, land degradation, and territorial carbon dioxide emissions is insufficiently explored in OECD economies. This study investigates how nonlinear effects of agroforestry practices, financial markets, innovation, environmental taxes, along with final consumption expenditure, determine territory‐based carbon emissions in OECD countries over the period 1994–2021. This study applied the second‐generation Driscoll–Kraay technique to analyze the data, while quantile regression serves as a nonparametric approach as a robustness check. The results show that agroforestry has inverted‐U shaped curve underlying that agroforestry in the initial stages may cause land degradation while at the later stages, it supports the climate resilience practices and land restoration in OECD economies. Moreover, financial development exerts heterogeneous effects in both models, suggesting differing channels of support for financial development. Green innovation and environmental taxes significantly reduce territorial carbon emissions, while final consumption expenditure, as theoretically expected, increases it. The results show robustness through nonparametric quantile regression with the role of income. Policy implications emphasize the adaptive framework of financial mechanisms, innovation, and environmental taxation to support agroforestry practices in a customized yet constantly focused manner on the reduction of emissions while supporting the development of climate resilience strategies in OECD economies.

title: On the intersection of Black geographies and policy mobilities: Tracing circuits of anti-racism in Newcastle upon Tyne
abstract: This paper reflects theoretically on the intersection of Black geographies and policy mobilities by tracing the historical and contemporary movements of Black activists, intellectuals and anti-racist struggles in Newcastle upon Tyne. While Black geographies foregrounds Black spatial imaginaries, resistance and epistemologies rooted in racial capitalism and coloniality, it has insufficiently interrogated how racialized policy formations and their circulations function transjurisdictionally. Likewise, policy mobilities, which charts the movement and mutation of urban policy models across contexts, offers an opportunity to expose the racialized structures underpinning these movements. This paper develops a conceptual approach that examines how race and power circulate through circuits of racialized spatial practices, Black actors and political thought and anti-racist struggles. The paper traces how Black individuals, ideas and infrastructures – routed through historical visits by Martin Luther King Jr., Frederick Douglass and Muhammad Ali as well as through contemporary cultural programs like Freedom City and protest movements like Black Lives Matter – are mobilized within and beyond the urban. In so doing, it advances a global, relational understanding of Black spatial politics that provokes a rethinking of urban theory’s Euro-American biases.
journal_name: Environment and Planning C: Politics and Space

title: Branding cities or citizens? Virtue-based branding as a technology of subjectification in Louisville
abstract: City branding is increasingly understood as shaping not only how cities are seen but who their residents become. This paper contributes to the growing scholarship that conceptualizes place branding as a technology of subjectification, arguing that when a city is branded with a human attribute, it is in effect its citizens who are branded. Drawing on a qualitative case study of Compassionate Louisville, the research traces how compassion was institutionalized as a governing discourse following the city’s formal adoption of the brand identity. The study reveals how the brand narrative operates simultaneously as a moral ideal, a performative expectation, and a political resource used to legitimize policy and manage social contradictions. By framing compassion as an apolitical, universal virtue, the brand establishes a disciplinary framework that encourages self-regulation and moral conformity while depoliticizing systemic social suffering. The paper contributes to debates within political geography and urban studies by demonstrating how virtue-based branding acts as an affective technology of power, reshaping urban subjectivities.
journal_name: Environment and Planning C: Politics and Space

title: Novel CRISPR therapy is poised to gain first FDA approval to alter genes inside the body
Revisiting new accounting history four decades on: reconciling traditional and critical historiographies
abstract: Purpose Revisiting debates in New Accounting History four decades on, this paper advances accounting historiography through the development of a Neo-Critical Accounting History (NCAH) framework that systematically integrates the strengths of traditional accounting history with the theoretically informed and critical orientation of new accounting history. In answering the “how” question, the framework offers an analytical pathway through which accounting historians may proceed with a rigorous and socially attuned mode of inquiry. Design/methodology/approach The study is grounded in critical accounting approach, in particular, Habermas's method of rational reconstruction (Held, 1980) providing the philosophical foundation for proposing an agenda advancing framework for NCAH. The framework integrates the methods of historical academic monograph with key features of both traditional and new accounting history. Findings The proposed NCAH framework is articulated across three interrelated dimensions. First, it integrates traditional and critical historiography by combining historical rigour with critical depth to recover marginalised voices and enhance contextual analysis. Second, it advances epistemic pluralisation through rigorous source critique, methodological triangulation, and engagement with diverse archival and counter-accounts, thereby addressing archival silences, partialities, and power relations. Third, it embraces theoretical openness and contemporary relevance, enabling historical inquiry into emerging accounting-related topics aligned with broader societal and ethical concerns, and strengthening accounting history's engagement with contemporary scholarly and public debates. Originality/value The manuscript demonstrates how traditional and new accounting history approaches may be systematically integrated, including through approaches inspired by abductive reasoning. Within this framing, narrative is positioned not as an end in itself, but rather as a point of departure for deeper theoretical interpretation and historical analysis. In doing so, NCAH reconciles historical and archival rigour with theoretical openness, thereby enhancing the analytical depth of the discipline and its capacity to contribute to interdisciplinary scholarship, societal reflection, and professional practice.

title: Between the hammer and the anvil: Collaborative states, MNES and development
abstract: Most governments continue to attract MNE investment as the optimal means of achieving economic development. However, MNEs have had a patchy record in addressing inequalities. Contemporaneously, the zeitgeist over the last decade has leaned toward greater state interventionism as part of inward-looking domestic policies, where the state is the main actor shaping economic development. We argue that successful developmental outcomes require neither the hollowing out of the state nor heavy-handed interventionism, but rather a collaborative state that strategically coordinates the MNE-state nexus. MNEs do not generate positive development outcomes through market mechanisms alone, just as states cannot always substitute for market actors through direct intervention. Instead, development emerges from a calibrated symbiotic relationship where the state creates location advantages, builds absorptive capacity, and coordinates linkages between MNEs and domestic actors, while managing diverse stakeholder interests and avoiding regulatory capture. We identify two critical prerequisites for effective collaboration: (1) a Weberian technocratic bureaucracy insulated from political volatility, and (2) a developmental consensus among domestic interest groups that prioritizes long-term national upgrading over short-term gains.

title: Gaze Behavior in Pedophilia and Hebephilia: How Task Instruction and Sexual Interest Shape Viewing of Prepubescent and Pubescent Stimuli
abstract: Abstract Visuospatial attentional processes are central in eye-tracking research of deviant sexual interest, yet it remains unclear to what extent task instructions modulate early (time to first fixation; number of first fixation) and late visuospatial attention (relative fixation time). We examined gaze behavior in individuals with pedophilic, hebephilic, and teleiophilic sexual interests while viewing prepubescent, early pubescent, and adult stimuli under free-viewing and forced-choice (attractiveness rating) conditions. We additionally assessed viewing time (VT) as an established indirect measure of sexual interest. Pedophilic and teleiophilic participants showed earlier orienting toward their preferred age category, whereas gaze patterns in the hebephilic group were inconsistent and differed from the VT results. Late visuospatial attentional indices such as relative fixation time indicated that pedophilic participants fixated roughly equally across all age categories, whereas hebephilic and teleiophilic participants fixated longer on adult stimuli. Within the present experimental design, the forced-choice condition was associated with more pronounced group-related effects and shorter times to first fixation, irrespective of group and stimulus type. These findings may provide preliminary indications of the potential sensitivity of this task context for early visuospatial attention, while alternative explanations and limitations of the experimental design are discussed. This study contributes to the limited eye-tracking literature on deviant sexual interest by explicitly considering both pedophilic and hebephilic sexual interest.

Skill certifications and migrant labor market integration: Experimental evidence from Colombia
abstract: This paper studies whether government-issued skill certification improves labor market integration when workers skills are hard to verify. We evaluate a randomized offer of access to an occupation-specific certification program in Colombia to locals and migrants, two groups with different ex ante signaling capacity. The program certifies existing skills rather than providing training. Among locals, the offer increases employment by reducing inactivity and raises hours worked. The effects persist unevenly over time and are robust to attrition bounds and alternative outcome measures. Among migrants, estimates are less precise and provide no evidence of effects in employment, hours, or wages. The results show that a common skill certification generates different patterns of labor market adjustment among locals and migrants.

abstract: We estimate productivity spillovers from Japanese cotton-spinning firms in China (known as Zaikabo) to local Chinese cotton-spinning mills based on plant-level data for 1925 to 1938. In order to capture the important role of distance in facilitating such spillovers we geo-localised the plants. Our results provide clear evidence for positive spillovers from Zaikabo to local Chinese mills, which go hand-in-hand with an upgrade in production technology towards greater use of capital. Spillovers are very localised, being strongest within a radius of up to 10 km around the Zaikabo and particularly strong for mills in Shanghai. Exploiting information on the workforce composition of the Japanese affiliates, we find suggestive evidence of a skilled-labour channel: spillovers tend to be larger from Zaikabo employing higher shares of skilled labour. We also find some evidence in line with the idea that these gains are larger for Chinese mills with higher initial productivity, consistent with a role for absorptive capacity. Our paper is the first to document FDI productivity spillovers in a historical context and to characterise the channels through which they operate.
